title: Mark Sanchez's change-of-plea hearing has been rescheduled for January 25
summary: The confusion has been resolved regarding the status of former NFL quarterback and former Fox announcer Mark Sanchez's criminal case.
full_text: The confusion has been resolved regarding the status of former NFL quarterback and former Fox announcer Mark Sanchez's criminal case. After a change-of-plea hearing set for November 9 was scrapped without explanation , the hearing was reset for January 27. When that happens, the case will have a new judge. The prior judge, as explained by Sean Keeley of Awful Announcing , recused herself for reasons that were not disclosed. The involvement of a new judge becomes the most obvious explanation for the delay in turning an informal plea deal into a formal guilty plea, followed by sentencing. Sanchez faced multiple charges after an October 2025 altercation with a then-69-year-old truck driver in Indianapolis. Days before the criminal trial was set to commence, Sanchez agreed to plead guilty. It's still not clear whether Sanchez will be pleading guilty to one or more misdemeanors or one or more felonies. The separate civil lawsuit filed by the truck driver, Perry Tole, against Sanchez and others has been resolved via an agreement that is in the process of being formalized.
author: Mike Florio

title: Deion Sanders after Colorado's blowout loss to Oklahoma State: "I really don't understand it"
summary: Deion Sanders's fourth season as head coach of the Colorado Buffaloes started with an upset of Georgia Tech and a blowout of overmatched Weber State.
full_text: '' Deion Sanders's fourth season as head coach of the Colorado Buffaloes started with an upset of Georgia Tech and a blowout of overmatched Weber State. Since then, the wheels have come off. The Buffs have lost five in a row, capped by a 57-24 blowout loss to Oklahoma State on Saturday. Colorado actually led the game at halftime, 24-23. In the second half, the Cowboys outscored the Buffaloes, 34-0. “We're so disciplined in this and that, and this and that, and every darn thing we do, but it seems like as soon as we go in the field, we're not disciplined,” Sanders said after the game, via Brent Schrotenboer of USA Today . “I really don't understand it, because we are disciplined in every area of this program, when it comes to academics, when it comes to being somewhere on time, when it comes to wearing the proper uniform, when it comes to just your manners in the building. Everything. But [when] we get on the field at the most critical moments, we blow it .” The latest loss may have sparked another quarterback change, after Kaneal Sweetwyne replaced Isaac Wilson, who had replaced Julian Lewis in September. The end result is that Colorado hasn't won a Big 12 road game since 2024. And the Buffaloes are 2-15 against Power Four conferences since December 2024.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes told Josh Simmons to leave a team meeting
summary: The incident took place a day before Simmons was placed on injured reserve. Simmons later apologized.
full_text: ''' Chiefs left tackle Josh Simmons, who hasn't played this season and was placed on injured reserve on Thursday, was told to leave a Wednesday team meeting by head coach Andy Reid and quarterback Patrick Mahomes. The incident began with Simmons sitting with his feet up and Reid asking him to put his feet down, according to ESPN. Simmons said he was sitting that way because of his back injury, and Reid told him if he couldn't sit upright he should go get treatment from the training staff. As Simmons and Reid went back and forth, Mahomes told Simmons he should leave and stop disrupting the meeting. Simmons did. Simmons later apologized to Reid and team leaders, according to the report. On the injury report on Wednesday, the Chiefs said that Simmons didn't practice because of "back/not injury related-personal," which might suggest that his absence from practice was a combination of both his back injury and the dispute he'd had with Reid, although Chiefs vice president of sports medicine and performance Rick Burkholder said the personal reason for Simmons missing practice was the team giving him time to talk to his family and agents about how to proceed with his back injury. The Chiefs made Simmons their first-round draft pick last year in the hopes that he could protect Mahomes' blind side for years to come. But so far Simmons has only played in eight games and missed 14. Simmons hasn't practiced since August. The soonest he could play would be the Chiefs' Week 11 game against the Cardinals.
author: Michael David Smith

title: NFLPA has yet to launch "full investigation" of Jalen Hurts situation
summary: Hurts still have the ability to launch the ultimate external investigation: Litigation.
full_text: As the NFL hopes to turn the page on the Jalen Hurts conversation, thanks to a full day of football starting with yet another pregame-show-killing 9:30 a.m. ET game, there will be further developments that will result in further scrutiny of the situation. The most immediate development will be the "full investigation" that the NFL Players Association has referenced, but not formally launched. Consider the precise terms of the statement the NFLPA issued on Tuesday: “The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts,” the union said. “In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward.” Although the NFLPA has the power under Article 39, Section 5(f) of the Collective Bargaining Agreement to activate an investigation, a statement reacting to the league's knee-jerk endorsement of the medical care provided to Hurts by pointing out that a "full investigation" is needed before any conclusions can be reached is very different from an official activation of the investigation contemplated by the CBA. There's no current reason to believe there won't be a full investigation, whatever the process. But an investigation hasn't started, at least not yet. Looming over any investigation conducted or initiated by the NFLPA is the possibility of the ultimate external investigation: Litigation. Although the CBA limits the ability of the player to sue the team and/or the league in court, the doctors are fair game. Three years ago, for example, former Eagles safety Chris Maragos won a $43.5 million verdict in a malpractice case against Dr. James Bradley and Rothman Orthopaedics Associates for surgery to correct a meniscus tear and the ensuing rehab of the injury. (The award was later upheld on appeal .) More recently, former Browns receiver David Bell has sued Dr. William Meyers and others for core muscle repair that allegedly resulted in a career-ending injury to Bell's femoral artery. “We undertook a year-long investigation into this matter in which a number of truly world-leading surgeons and radiologists examined the matter, with many of them doing so on a no-fee basis. The findings were nothing short of astonishing and give us a high degree of confidence we can prove that hundreds of millions of dollars going to Dr. Bill Meyers, Dr. Adam Zoga, Jefferson, and the Vincera Institute to perform these surgeries, were prioritized over the basic medical principle of First Do No Harm, as we have alleged in the Complaint,” Bell’s lead attorney, Brad Sohn, said in a press release. Hurts has a potential lawsuit against the doctors who provided his care, independent of any more limited rights against the Eagles or the league. While it could get complicated — especially if Hurts may have to file a lawsuit in the U.S. and in England — a "superficial" blood clot in his leg resulting from being cleated during the Week 4 game against the Rams became a deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in each lung . It's fair for Hurts to ask whether the medical care Hurts received caused or contributed to the progression of the situation into something both serious and life-threatening. And the eventual impact of the situation on his career is currently unknown. The only prudent approach would be to investigate all aspects of the situation from the moment Hurts suffered the initial injury until the point at which the "bilateral pulmonary emboli" were diagnosed. Even if the Eagles and Hurts continue to be on the same page, Hurts can still pursue his rights against the various doctors who may have handled the situation in a way that fell short of the requisite standard of care. However it plays out, this one is far from over. One way or another, the answers that the Eagles and the league won't provide to the public need to be pursued through one or more investigative processes. And litigation is the best way for Hurts to get any compensation he may be owed for an outcome that may have been fully avoidable.
author: Mike Florio

title: Travis Kelce's receiving yardage total will soon break Tony Gonzalez's tight end record
summary: Kelce needs just 35 receiving yards to have a career total higher than Gonzalez, counting the postseason.
full_text: ''' Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce can continue to bolster his Hall of Fame résumé on Sunday night against the Seahawks. Kelce is just 35 yards away from breaking Tony Gonzalez's NFL record for career receiving yards by a tight end, counting the playoffs. Gonzalez retired with an NFL record total of 15,413 receiving yards: 15,127 in the regular season and 286 in the playoffs. Kelce currently has 15,379 receiving yards: 13,301 in the regular season and 2,078 in the playoffs. With 35 yards on Sunday Night Football, Kelce will surpass Gonzalez's total. Kelce can also continue to move up the career regular-season receiving record books. Kelce currently has 1,100 catches in the regular season, the seventh-most in NFL history. Cris Carter has the sixth-most with 1,101 and Marvin Harrison has the fifth-most with 1,102. So if Kelce catches three passes on Sunday night he'll move ahead of Harrison and into the Top 5 all-time. The only players with more than 1,102 catches in their NFL careers were Jerry Rice (1,549), Larry Fitzgerald (1,432), Gonzalez (1,325) and Jason Witten (1,228).
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bill Belichick, North Carolina fall to Syracuse in OT, 31-30
summary: After a pair of signature wins over Pitt and Duke, North Carolina and coach Bill Belichick have fallen to ACC rival Syracuse.
full_text: ' After a pair of signature wins over Pitt and Duke, North Carolina and coach Bill Belichick have fallen to ACC rival Syracuse. The Orange beat the Tar Heels in overtime on Saturday, 31-30. The victory came on an all-or-nothing two-point try by Syracuse after UNC had scored seven on the opening drive of the first overtime. North Carolina entered the game as 8.5-point favorites. The Tar Heels led by 10 in the third quarter, 20-10. The loss drops Belichick's team to 4-3 for the year. They host No. 1 Miami next Saturday. After that, UNC plays at UConn, Louisville, at Virginia, and NC State. The Tar Heels finished 4-8 last year, in Belichick's first season with the program.
author: Mike Florio

title: Browns extend DT Maliek Collins by two years
summary: The contract year of veteran defensive tackle Maliek Collins has resulted after only six games in new contact.
full_text: The contract year of veteran defensive tackle Maliek Collins has resulted after only six games in new contact. Agent Drew Rosenhaus tells ESPNFL that the Browns and Collins have reached agreement on a two-year, $30 million extension. The deal includes, per Rosenhaus, $23 million in guarantees. Collins had signed a two-year, $20 million deal with the Browns in 2025. He was due to be a free agent in March. The 31-year-old Collins was a third-round pick in 2016 of the Cowboys. After four years in Dallas, he spent one season with the Raiders, three with the Texans, and one with the 49ers before joining the Browns. Collins has started all six games this year for the 4-2 Browns. Last year, he appeared in 12 games, all starts. For his career, Collins has 154 regular-season appearances with 147 starts.
author: Mike Florio

title: After another day of Paris protests, NFL is on track to stage Steelers-Saints at Stade de France
summary: At this point, it's too late to turn back for Sunday's game.
full_text: It's too late to turn back now. With kickoff to Sunday's game between the Steelers and Saints in Paris less than 13 hours away, as of this posting, the plan continues to be full speed ahead for Steelers-Saints at Stade de France. Even if the league is potentially going to be stepping into a steaming pile of merde . Via Mark Maske of Front Office Sports , the game remains set for a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff after another day of local protests in Paris. More than 400,000 participated in the demonstrations, which resulted in more than 1,000 arrests. Per the Associated Press, a march that started peacefully ended with protesters throwing fireworks and other objects at police . They responded with tear gas, sound grenades, and water cannons. The question remains whether protestors will target the NFL game, in an effort to send a clear international message. No matter how secure the stadium may be, the path to the venue's security perimeter may not be. Hopefully, there will be no incidents. It's still a calculated risk for the NFL, one that many would regard as unnecessary. For the NFL, the necessity to play flows from the ongoing obsession to export the game to other countries. If something occurs, it will be impossible for the league to shrug and to say, "We didn't know that could happen." And it will throw a wrench into the plan to globalize the game. Even without any specific problems on Sunday, the situation underscores the realities of potentially putting teams in other countries, with other governments and other citizenries that could eventually complicate the effort to play all games as scheduled. For now, the league doesn't care. It only sees one thing — the possibility of transforming a billion-dollar business into a trillion-dollar behemoth if fans in other countries become as passionate about pro football as Americans are.
author: Mike Florio

title: Chase Young, Christen Miller were fined for violent gestures on same play
summary: The NFL's sudden embrace of the "No Fun League" dynamic resulted in a rash of fines that were replaced with a new approach to discipline for celebrations.
full_text: The NFL's sudden embrace of the "No Fun League" dynamic resulted in a rash of fines that were replaced with a new approach to discipline for celebrations. Under the revised rules, a couple of Saints players were fined for a celebration in the third quarter of the Week 6 win over the Giants. The NFL fined defensive end Chase Young and defensive lineman Christen Miller $14,926 and $11,915, respectively, for a "violent gesture." It happened with 36 seconds left in the third quarter. The TV copy of the game doesn't reveal the specific incident. Regardless, the fines were imposed. And the players possibly will appeal. The league and the NFL Players Association announced earlier this month that certain celebrations will be immediately subject to fines, including "[g]estures that depict violence , including the use of guns or other weapons, or gang-related signs." For celebrations that land in a gray area, the league will communicate with the player before fining him if/when it happens again.
author: Mike Florio

title: Fred Warner was fined for hit on a defenseless player, Malik Mustapha was not
summary: 49ers linebacker Fred Warner heard from the NFL a couple of times for plays he made during Week 6.
full_text: 49ers linebacker Fred Warner heard from the NFL a couple of times for plays he made during Week 6. Warner was fined twice for hits on Commanders tight end Chig Okonkwo in the 49ers' win on Monday night. Warner was fined $17,911 for a hit on a defenseless player and $47,762 for using his helmet to initiate contact. The defenseless player hit was initially flagged during the game, but it was picked up by officials. If Warner is disciplined for two more hits on defenseless players, he will be suspended for one game. Warner also has been fined for a hip-drop tackle, which carries the same possibility of suspension if he is guilty of three of them. 49ers safety Malik Mustapha avoided a flag for a hit on Stefon Diggs in the Commanders game, but some expected a fine for hitting a defenseless player given the ESPN broadcast's belief that it should have been a penalty. Mustapha was not fined, however, and that means he remains at one foul toward his own possible suspension for multiple hits on defenseless players this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bears' trick play fell flat due to clear rules violation
summary: Thursday night's game between the Patriots and Bears included a trick play from Bears coach Ben Johnson.
full_text: ' Thursday night's game between the Patriots and Bears included a trick play from Bears coach Ben Johnson. It ended up being a footnote to the contest, but the situation was and still is a head-scratcher. With the Bears facing a second-and-three play from the New England eight, quarterback Caleb Williams pretended with one had to give the ball to running back D'Andre Swift. With the other, Williams gave the ball to left guard Joe Thuney . He was tackled one yard short of the line to gain. A flag was thrown. It was an illegal forward handoff. By rule, a forward handoff is only permitted to an eligible receiver behind the line of scrimmage. "It's gotta be backwards, I mean, it's simple as that," Bears coach Ben Johnson told reporters on Friday. "So, once again, we felt like it looked good over the course of — we've been practicing it now for a while. You know, the initial version, we were actually putting it on the ground. Which, you know, in hindsight might have been the way to go. It's one of those things. Shooters shoot. We shot. We missed. So, keep it moving." It's strange, to say the least, that Johnson didn't know it was against the rules for Williams to hand the ball forward to an ineligible receiver. If someone like Dan Quinn had used a play like that, he would have gotten heavily criticized for it. Unlike Quinn, Johnson doesn't have a reputation for making mistakes like that. It was still a mistake — and it was compounded by the apparent fact that Johnson didn't alert the officials to the potential for a trick play before the game. Presumably, the officials would have told him, "You can't do that." Then there's the possibility that Johnson is playing 4-D chess. As Big Cat suggested on the latest episode of Pardon My Take , the whole thing may have been a setup for some other trick play that Johnson will unveil at some point later this year. Regardless, the forward handoff to Thuney was a clear violation of the rules. Johnson should have known it. Someone on the coaching staff should have known it. As they practiced the play "for a while," the potential illegality of a forward handoff to a lineman should have been flagged. Again, maybe Johnson knew. And maybe he has another trick play in the cylinder that will now be even more likely to work, given that the Thuney play has been put on film.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Philip Rivers is "expected to be in the mix" for NC State job
summary: Former NFL quarterback Philip Rivers interviewed for the Bills' head-coaching job in January.
full_text: Former NFL quarterback Philip Rivers interviewed for the Bills’ head-coaching job in January. He could be getting an interview at the college level next. Via Pete Thamel of ESPN, Rivers is " expected to be in the mix " for the head-coaching job at NC State. Rivers played for the Wolfpack from 2000 to 2003, before becoming the fourth pick in the 2004 NFL draft. He played for the Chargers from 2004 through 2019. Rivers spent 2020 with the Colts before retiring. He returned late last year to start three games for the Colts, after Indianapolis lost starter Daniel Jones to a torn Achilles tendon. Rivers has coached high-school football in Alabama since 2021. His son, Gunner, has committed to play at NC State in 2027. The job became open on Saturday. Dave Doeren, who spent 14 seasons at NC State, was fired after Friday night's loss to Stanford.
author: Mike Florio

title: The NFL should relocate the Steelers-Saints game in Paris to London
summary: NFL scraps multiple Saturday events due to ongoing protests.
full_text: With one day more to go until the Steelers and Saints play in Paris, the NFL shouldn't wait one hour more to relocate the game. No matter how safe and secure Stade de France will be for the game, it's not safe for NFL fans to be in Paris due to protests that from time to time morph into full-blown riots. Consider the latest moves made by the league as to the collateral activities. Via the Associated Press, the NFL announced on Saturday the closure of its "NFL House" event, due to "potential accessibility issues." Previously, the Steelers Fan House event was scrapped . The "Saints House" has been postponed until Sunday. Meanwhile, the U.S. State Department issued a security alert cautioning "Americans in Paris for the NFL game" to "exercise caution and be aware of their surroundings." Why would the NFL insist on pressing forward? The risk, however big or small it may be, isn't worth it. The league has said security at the game will be enhanced. Which necessarily means security resources that could be utilized elsewhere in the city are being devoted to something that is far from a necessity. Also, no matter how secure the stadium is, the fans who have bought tickets to the game will need to get to the perimeter where the NFL's security plan activates. A soccer match between PSG and Lyon recently was moved from Sunday to Monday , at the direction of French authorities. If the NFL won't do the prudent thing and move the game to London, the powers-that-be in Paris should direct the NFL to bump Steelers-Saints to Monday, too. (That would shift the game broadcast to Monday morning or afternoon, New York time. Which could inadvertently unlock a new standalone window for future NFL games.) It's surprising that it's gotten to this point. The warning signs have been obvious for weeks. On Friday, even the President chimed in . And the league's determination (or, more accurately, stubbornness) to proceed has led to a situation in which the NFL may still be forced to make an eleventh-hour-and-fifty-seventh-minute decision to do something other than play the game as scheduled. Which, for the teams, will only add to the overall in-season inconvenience of traveling to another country to play a football game. There's no reason to wait. They should make the move now. We're not privy to all of the specifics. The generalities continue to suggest that the league absolutely should pivot from the plan to play in Paris at 3:30 p.m. local time on Sunday. Why assume the risk that any fan will be endangered as they try to get to the game? Why take any risks that the enhanced security will be overrun by an event that the protester-rioters could see as a perfect opportunity to make their message resonate internationally? It seems to be increasingly obvious that relocation of the game is the right call. Even if nothing happens, there's already a cloud over the league's first-ever Paris game. And if there's even one incident in connection with playing the game as planned, the NFL will risk being dubbed what the French call les incompétents .
author: Mike Florio

title: The PFT 25th anniversary is coming next weekend
summary: Twenty-five years ago this month, I had a decision to make.
full_text: ' Twenty-five years ago this month, I had a decision to make. In June 2000, I'd stumbled into creating written content for NFL Talk, a long-defunct website I'd discovered a couple of months earlier. I didn't get paid for it, but it was fun. And I had a weird feeling there was a chance it could maybe, potentially, possibly become something. Some day. Somehow. As the 2000 NFL season unfolded, I started doing more and more for no compensation (they got their money's worth). I had the time for it, because I'd left the law firm where I'd become a partner and had started my own practice. By the spring, the tech bubble burst, NFL Talk and its related operations went bust, and ESPN bought the carcass. Through a string of events that still seems bizarre in hindsight, I ended up getting hired by ESPN.com to write a daily news and rumors column for the "ESPN Insider" service. The six-month contract paid $18,000. It wasn't huge money, but it was $18,000 more than I'd made in nearly a year. And I was stunned that anyone would pay anything for the stuff I was writing. Life nevertheless got very complicated. I'd get up early, spend 4-5 hours on the side job, and then go to the law office and put in a full day. As the law practice got busier, the days got very long. The six-month contract was due to expire on October 31. After 9/11 happened, I took a step back and considered why and how I'd gotten to the point at which I was putting in 14-18 hours per day on two different jobs. (ESPN never asked whether I had a second full-time occupation, and I never volunteered that information.) I was also frustrated by the fact that, after I submitted my daily content, it took 2-3 hours before it went live, after passing through multiple internal editorial hoops. I knew it would be better if the content could be posted instantaneously. In early October, ESPN offered a one-year deal, at $36,000. Through another string of events that still seems bizarre in hindsight, I decided to give up the bird in the hand and plunk down a whopping $500 (plus $50 a month) to create a place of my own, where the content could be posted as soon as it was ready — and where I didn't have to worry about others tinkering with my words. On November 1, ProFootballTalk.com went live. I still remember that " hold on to your butts " feeling just before the switch was flipped. There was no real plan, no mission statement, no balance sheets, no anything. I remember having a loose goal (which seemed very unrealistic at the time) of making the $36,000 per year that I'd given up when passing on the ESPN renewal. For years, PFT didn't make a cent. After nearly one year, I quit. (It lasted one day.) On January 1, 2004, I decided that if it was ever going to be whatever it could be, I needed to post content every single day. It's the only New Year's resolution I ever kept. Nearly 23 years later, the streak of posting fresh content each and every day has not ended. Next Sunday is the 25th anniversary of that "hold on to your butts" moment from November 1, 2001. I don't quite know how to feel about that. Longevity in any industry ultimately means "you're old." In this specific industry, the phrase "25 years" feels like 2,500. Regardless, we're just getting started. I've come to terms with the fact that I'll keep doing this until I physically can't, due either to infirmity or a blind date with the Grim Reaper. It's part of my routine, and I have no idea what I'd do with my days if I wasn't doing this. It never would have lasted if it wasn't for the folks like you (if you're still reading this) who take time from their busy lives to read a little of what we write or listen to a little of what we say. We're grateful that you trust us, especially when you've got so many options. And while some would insist on social media that it's a "hate read," I've been around the block enough times to know that the far more troubling emotions are ambivalence and indifference. We try to give you something to talk about. To learn about. To react to. The passion you have for pro football often splashes back onto the messengers who point out the possibility that your favorite team may not be the greatest collection of football talent ever assembled. Regardless, as we close in on 25 years, it only strengthens my commitment to keep it going. Next stop, 50 years. And maybe a lot more than that. When the anniversary officially arrives next Sunday, I've got a small token of appreciation planned. It's something that the folks who have been in the audience since November 1, 2001 will understand, and hopefully enjoy. (The AWLs of Pardon My Take already know what it is.) More specifics on that are coming soon. For now, as I think back to those last few days of loose planning and haphazard organization and reluctantly writing a $500 check to the local tech company that continued to honor its quoted price of $50 per month even as the operation consumed more and more space on its servers, it's the perfect time to say thank you to everyone out there who allowed this thing to survive in the lean years and to grow into whatever it now is. Even if I still don't quite know what it really is. Either way, hold on to your butts.
author: Mike Florio

title: Eagles list Saquon Barkley as questionable; DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks ruled out
summary: The Eagles have left the door open for running back Saquon Barkley to play on Monday night, but they will be down two wideouts against the Cowboys.
full_text: The Eagles have left the door open for running back Saquon Barkley to play on Monday night, but they will be down two wideouts against the Cowboys. Barkley is listed as questionable to play after moving up to full practice participation on Saturday. Barkley has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury and his presence would be welcomed on an offense that's low on wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were both ruled out on the team's final injury report of Week 7. Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore, and Britain Covey are the available wideouts on the 53-man roster. Defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen) and linebacker Nolan Smith (concussion) have also been ruled out for Philadelphia. Cornerback Jakorian Bennett (knee), tight end Grant Calcaterra (back), guard Landon Dickerson (knee, pectoral), linebacker Jalyx Hunt (knee, ankle), and tight end Eli Stowers (quad) join Barkley with questionable designations. Bennett, Calcaterra, Dickerson, and Stowers are all on injured reserve, so the Eagles will need to make roster moves to get all or some of them on the roster for Monday night.
author: Josh Alper

title: With Troy Aikman possibly exiting broadcasting, he extends an olive branch to Jerry Jones
summary: Hall of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman has talked openly for years about wanting to work in an NFL front office.
full_text: Hall of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman has talked openly for years about wanting to work in an NFL front office. He took a half-step in that direction last year, becoming a consultant to the Dolphins and continuing to work for the team while also working for Monday Night Football . In March, Aikman spoke openly about the Cowboys’ historical lack of interest in pursuing his services. Now that Aikman's time with ESPN is by all appearances moving toward a conclusion, Aikman seems to be extending an olive branch toward Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones. Asked by Mike Fisher whether Aikman would break bread with Jerry Jones, Aikman said this: "I would have lunch, breakfast, or dinner with Jerry any time he wants it. And it wouldn't necessarily have to be because it's a job interview. Just because, you know, we go back a long way. . . . I came in, I was 22 years old. I was his very first draft pick. There's a lot within that relationship, both from the beginning, when he began as the owner, when I began my NFL career as a quarterback for 12 years of my life, playing for him, and then, even in the years that have followed, you know, we've been through a lot. We've been through the highest of highs, we've been through some pretty tough moments as well. Our relationship is complicated. I think he would agree with that, but it is one that's built, I believe, on respect. This week, he said some really kind things, which meant a lot to me, quite honestly. So, yeah, I would welcome any conversation with Jerry, and quite honestly I don't know if there would be, or if there ever would be an opportunity. But if Jerry came to me and felt that, in his heart, I could lend some services that would help make them better, I would — I’d have a hard time not taking a good look at that ." Jones did indeed speak glowingly about Aikman during this week's quarterly NFL ownership meetings. " Troy is very capable , and he's so, really relatively speaking, he's in his youth as careers go," Jones said. "And he's very capable of doing any one of a number of things, certainly anything to do with football. I don't know of any area short of getting that kind of feeling, I don't know of any area that Troy Aikman wouldn't be qualified and competent to go into." Aikman's current role with the Dolphins remains fluid and undefined, but it was enough to prompt the NFL to place Tom Brady-style restrictions on his ability to enter the facilities of other teams or to attend practices before Monday night games. Despite Aikman's unfulfilled aspiration to work in a front office, he seems to be realizing that his time as a broadcaster could be ending — and he's apparently feeling some regret over that. “As I’m into my last year at ESPN, I’m realizing that this is something that could very well be taken away from me ,” Aikman told Fisher, via Tyler Lauletta of Awful Announcing . “For the first time, I’m realizing how much I really do — I’ve always enjoyed it. I’ve always known that. But until you risk having something taken away from you, I think sometimes you tend to maybe take things for granted. “And so, for the first time probably in my career, I’m realizing, you know, this is a great profession. It’s been a great ride for me, and I hope it’s not over. Time will tell. But, yeah. So, we’ll see. I’m excited about what the rest of this year holds, and I’m excited to finally get back into the booth for a Super Bowl.” With CBS already deciding to make J.J. Watt the full-time replacement for Tony Romo, there may not be a high-profile (and high-paying) seat for Aikman in 2027. If he truly wants to continue to call games, the best spot could be Greg Olsen's current slot as the No. 2 NFL announcer on Fox. And the money that goes with that assignment. It's still not clear why ESPN has apparently soured on Aikman. Maybe he overplayed his hand, by reportedly asking for $30 million per year . Maybe ESPN wasn't thrilled by his Miami moonlighting, especially since it has complicated his ability to be as prepared to call games as he could be. (It's also possible that Aikman took the position with the Dolphins before running it by anyone at ESPN, which if accurate would tend to impair the relationship between ESPN and Aikman.) Regardless, Aikman is now making it known that his upcoming free agency sweeps more broadly than broadcasting. He's also officially in play for the Cowboys or any other team that may choose to consider hiring him.

title: Ravens downgrade QB Lamar Jackson to out for Sunday
summary: Jackson will miss third straight game with high-ankle sprain.
full_text: The Ravens will turn to quarterback Tyler Huntley once again. On Saturday, quarterback Lamar Jackson was downgraded to out with a lingering ankle issue. It will be the third game missed due to the ankle sprain. The Ravens could have let the uncertainty ride until Sunday, since they're playing at home. Players listed as questionable often aren't downgraded on a Saturday unless they play for the road team and don't travel with the team. On Friday, Jackson expressed optimism that he'd be able to face the Bengals. "Right now, I'm heading in the right direction," Jackson said. He added that pain, not swelling, was the biggest lingering problem. Jackson said it doesn't hurt when he walks, but that the pain increases when he runs. He explained that trying to play through the pain would only hurt the team's effort to win. Jackson confirmed that he has a high-ankle sprain, contrary to some of the reporting that described it as something other than that. Typically, a high-ankle sprain requires more time to heal, and it does indeed create more intense and more persistent pain. He also said that he could know on Saturday whether he'll be able to play, and that he otherwise has a "grace period" until Sunday. The Ravens decided based on what they know as of Saturday to not wait another day before making it official that Jackson won't play. The team is 3-1 with Jackson starting, and 1-1 without him. Now at 4-2, they face the 3-2 Bengals on Sunday with Huntley getting his third straight start. title: The Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders have unionized
summary: One of the NFL's teams has another union to deal with — and the team in question didn't fight it.
full_text: '' One of the NFL's teams has another union to deal with — and the team in question didn't fight it. Via the Associated Press, the Dallas Cowboys have agreed to recognize the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Association as the collective bargaining representative for the team's cheerleading squad. "The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are an esteemed part of the Cowboys organization, deeply respected for the talent and dedication they exhibit," the union said in a statement. "They remain one of the most sought-after opportunities for talented dancers worldwide." Employers typically prefer to avoid unions, for obvious reasons. Through collective bargaining and the ability to strike, unions can secure better pay and better working conditions for all employees in the bargaining unit. The Buffalo Jills were the first NFL cheerleading squad to unionize, back in 1995. The Jills disbanded in 2014 after the filing of a lawsuit alleging violations of the New York minimum-wage laws. Questions about fair pay for NFL cheerleaders have been common over the years, along with allegations of improper conduct. The Washington franchise, while under the management of Daniel Snyder, faced civil claims arising from a " secret outtake " video. Those claims were later settled . In 2022, longtime Cowboys P.R. executive Rich Dalrymple abruptly resigned amid allegations that he secretly recorded the team's cheerleaders while they were changing clothes. Four cheerleaders received $2.4 million to settle their civil claims as a result of that incident.

title: Former Raiders RB Pete Banaszak dies at 82
summary: Former Raiders running back Pete Banaszak has died, the team announced Saturday.
full_text: Former Raiders running back Pete Banaszak has died, the team announced Saturday. He was 82. "The Raiders Family mourns the passing of Pete Banaszak, whose toughness, competitive spirit, and dedication embodied a legendary era of Raiders football and made him a cherished member of the Silver and Black," the team said in a statement. "The deepest condolences of the entire Raider Nation are with Pete's wife Sue, daughters Rebecca and Amy, grandsons Luke, Austin, and Connor, and all of his loved ones." Banaszak played his entire career with the Raiders. The team drafted him in the fifth round of the 1966 AFL Draft, and he retired after the 1978 season. He led the NFL with 16 rushing touchdowns in 1975, which remains a single-season franchise record. He won a Super Bowl XI ring, which was the franchise's first Super Bowl championship. Banaszak appeared in 173 regular-season games with the Raiders and played a central role in the famous "Holy Roller" play. Banaszak, a Wisconsin native, was inducted into the National Polish-American Sports Hall of Fame in 1990.

title: With Nick Bosa out longer than expected, 49ers may not have enough healthy players for roster spots on Sunday
summary: Bosa will miss fifth game with calf injury.
full_text: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa pulled a calf muscle in practice on the Thursday before Week 3. Even though the team didn't place Bosa on injured reserve, he has now missed four games. He'll miss his fifth on Sunday at Atlanta. On Friday, coach Kyle Shanahan was asked about remarks from Bosa indicating certainty he'd return for the Week 7 game against the Falcons and optimism he'd be back for Week 6 against the Commanders. " I just think he was a little too optimistic, especially for Bosa because he's pretty accurate," Shanahan told reporters. "He doesn't say stuff like that unless it's accurate. I just think it surprised him. He worked out, after he said that to you guys, and the next day he was just a little sore, which surprised all of us. That wasn't a great sign, especially going to play on turf and stuff this week, so I think it was more he was just a little too optimistic.” Bosa is just one of a long list of injured 49ers players. Shanahan acknowledged on Friday that the 49ers may not have 48 players healthy enough to dress for the game. Has that ever happened to him before? “No, I don't think so," Shanahan said. "I don't think here. I don't think ever in my career, so it's a unique situation.” The 2026 season has entailed plenty of unique situations for the 49ers. Through it all, they keep winning. Which makes it Shanahan's best year of coaching (so far), and which has him as the current favorite to be named the NFL's coach of the year.

title: Questions linger regarding whether Jed York received preferential treatment
summary: As it relates to the financial consequences of 49ers owner Jed York's suspension, relative to the financial consequences of a player suspension, there's no question that York received preferential treatment.
full_text: As it relates to the financial consequences of 49ers owner Jed York's suspension, relative to the financial consequences of a player suspension, there’s no question that York received preferential treatment. But that's not unique to York; the NFL's disciplinary system inherently makes it far more costly (relative to income) for a player to be suspended than for an owner to be suspended. A separate question lingers as to whether York received preferential treatment from the criminal justice system in Columbiana County, Ohio. Earlier this month, the San Francisco Chronicle explored whether York's expedited prosecution — which resulted in a one-day jail term and no probation, one day after the arrest — meshes with the usual approach to such cases. The Chronicle article explains that a review of all similar 2026 arrests in the county showed York and one other person were the only two out of 100 to have a prostitution-related charge reduced to disorderly conduct. Per the report, a "large majority" of the other defendants received 90- or 180-day suspended sentences, including "strict probation requirements." Meanwhile, a new item from Daniel Farr of the New York Post focuses on a website that seeks to compel political candidates to refund contributions made by York, and that pushes to have his entire criminal file released , without redaction. From the league's perspective, the matter is resolved. Commissioner Roger Goodell addressed the situation this week, after York's six-game suspension ended. Still, the issue has yet to fully go away. Although there are no formal legal procedures pending, the effort to scrutinize York's conduct and to explore whether he benefited from his status remain.

title: Saints vs. Steelers prediction: Aaron Rodgers, Tyler Shough to duel in first-ever game in Paris
summary: Plus, how to watch, what to know and a preview from an NFL expert
full_text:
A year after being the first team to win a regular-season game in Ireland, the Steelers will try to win the first-ever NFL game played in France.
Pittsburgh (4-2) is also trying to win a third straight game while keeping pace with the rest of the AFC North, the AFC's only division where every team has a winning record. The Steelers' recent success has been a byproduct of Aaron Rodgers ' resurgence, Jaylen Warren's emergence and a defense that is one of the league's best on third down and in the red zone.
New Orleans is coming off a much-needed win over the Giants , snapping a three-game losing streak. More work is required, however, if the 2-4 Saints are going to seriously challenge the Panthers for NFC South supremacy.
Here's how you can follow the action in real time, along with a game preview and prediction.
Different travel plans: The Saints touched down in Paris on Monday, six days ahead of Sunday's game. Conversely, the Steelers didn't get to France until early Friday after taking a red-eye flight from Pittsburgh. The Steelers then had to cancel practice upon arrival due to inclement weather.
Red-hot Rodgers: As of late, the 42-year-old Rodgers has been playing more like the 32-year-old version of himself. He's completed 68.8% of his passes with five touchdowns and just one interception in Pittsburgh's past two games. In addition to his accuracy, Rodgers has displayed impressive mobility and elusiveness.
8️⃣ making it happen 😮‍💨 @AaronRodgers12 pic.twitter.com/3yfsZ9PywD
Against the Buccaneers last Sunday, he shook off five sacks to lead Pittsburgh's largest fourth-quarter comeback since 1992. The Steelers ultimately won the game in overtime when Rodgers threw a six-yard touchdown pass to rookie Germie Bernard .
Speaking of Bernard, the rookie second-round pick has emerged as one of Rodgers' favorite targets. He caught six passes for 80 yards in Pittsburgh's Week 5 win over the Colts and had 11 receptions for 87 yards in last week's win in Tampa.
Big game for Warren?: Warren had to fight for yardage last week against Tampa's stout run defense. He might be in for an easier day against a Saints defense that is arguably the league's worst against the run.
Through six weeks, the Saints are 30th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed (828), 32nd in rushing touchdowns allowed (11) and 28th in average yards-per-carry allowed (4.8). They were torched in Week 4 by the Falcons ' duo of Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr. , who ran for a combined 207 yards and five touchdowns on 33 carries.
The Steelers' running game benefited last week from the return of Rico Dowdle , who played for the first time since Week 2 after spending a month on injured reserve. Dowdle is questionable for Sunday's game with a knee injury.
Which Shough will show up in Paris? It's been a roller coaster of a season so far for the Saints' second-year quarterback, Tyler Shough . He started the season with three impressive outings that were followed by two underwhelming performances. Last Sunday was a mixed bag. He completed just 16 of 30 passes for 144 yards, but he threw three touchdowns and no interceptions while helping the Saints snap their three-game losing skid.
On Sunday, Shough will face a Steelers secondary that came up with several key plays during last week's comeback win over the Buccaneers. Jamel Dean and rookie Daylen Everette had key interceptions, and Jalen Ramsey sealed the win with a sack on the game's final play.
Pittsburgh's secondary will be focused on stopping Chris Olave , who is far and away the Saints' most productive skill player. Olave's productivity has fallen off in recent weeks, but he did catch one of Shough's three touchdown passes in last Sunday's win over the Giants.
I'd be tempted to pick the Saints if this game had been played a month ago. But given the Saints' defensive issues and Pittsburgh's offensive awakening, I like the Steelers in this game as long as they take care of the ball and make enough plays in the red zone. Score: Steelers 27, Saints 20

title: Giants' John Harbaugh details J.J. McCarthy decision with convincing explanation: 'Heck of a skill set'
summary: The switch from Jameis Winston to McCarthy comes after the third-year quarterback has been with the team for four weeks
full_text:
New York Giants coach John Harbaugh saw more than enough from J.J. McCarthy during the fourth quarter of last week's loss to give him the starting nod in Sunday's matchup with the Houston Texans .
After coming off the bench to replace Jameis Winston and lead three scoring drives in the final 10 minutes, the leash is coming off McCarthy for a team in dire need of consistent quarterback play with Jaxson Dart on the shelf for the rest of the campaign.
With New York's bye week on the way after Sunday's game, it would be quite a surge of momentum to beat the Texans. The Giants would also pick up some confidence before the start of November, potentially 4-2-1 and atop the NFC East.
"What gives us the best chance to be our best? Gives us the best chance to play the best offense we can, and I thought Jameis has done a tremendous job," Harbaugh said this week on his decision . "Won us games, played well. But as we go forward here, this is going to be our direction, and we think it gives us some good options on offense."
Harbaugh said the move to McCarthy after a month is due in part to giving the franchise's freshest quarterback time in a different system following a trade with the Minnesota Vikings . Harbaugh joked that not even Tom Brady would be able to start immediately for a new team if he came out of retirement ready to go, given the complexities of learning a different playbook.
Winston threw for 957 yards, seven touchdowns and five interceptions in five games after the injury to Dart, going 2-2-1 overall.
"Both guys are great quarterbacks. It's not really a comparison kind of thing," Harbaugh said. "Just, you know, J.J.'s got a skill set that we can take advantage of, and we're excited to see what we can do with it. He's obviously out here throwing right now. I'm kind of watching him as you guys ask the questions out here, getting some extra work.
"He's got a heck of a skill set, you know? He can throw it. He's picked up the offense really quickly. He's an athletic guy, obviously, and he's going to play some good football."
Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan have spent the last few weeks with McCarthy, assuring Harbaugh that the third-year pro is ready to operate at full efficiency.
"The offense is — the book itself is huge, and it's always tailored toward probably your players, and certainly your quarterback, right? But he's got the game plan down," Harbaugh said. "I think he headed down last week, pretty fully, even more so this week. It has been tailored a little more toward his direction, probably, but he'll be ready to go."
McCarthy, a former first-round pick, told reporters this week he was "honored" to be named New York's Week 7 QB1.
"You know, thrilled to get out there, and tomorrow really get in the film room and just evaluate today's practice and get better, and go from there," McCarthy said.

title: NFL levies two fines to 49ers LB Fred Warner for hit on Commanders TE Chig Okonkwo
summary: Warner was initially flagged for the violation, but the officials picked it up
full_text:
The NFL has fined All-Pro linebacker Fred Warner for two infractions stemming from San Francisco's Week 6 win over the Commanders , according to multiple reports. In total, Warner was docked $65,673, specifically for a hit he inflicted on Washington tight end Chig Okonkwo.
During the 49ers ' 23-17 win on Monday night, Warner made helmet-to-helmet contact with Okonkwo as he brought in a 2-yard reception in the fourth quarter. Warner was initially flagged on the play, but it was eventually picked up by the officials.
He was fined $47,762 for a hit on a defenseless player and then $17,911 for using his helmet to initiate contact.
The NFL fined 49ers LB Fred Warner $65,673 for two unnecessary roughness violations last week — including $47,762 for this hit on Commanders TE Chig Okonkwo. Officials threw a flag on the play, but then picked it up. pic.twitter.com/Ro4ll4vtbX
This isn't the first time that Warner has found himself in the crosshairs of the league office. In fact, this is the linebacker's fourth fine of the season, with the league handing down two fines totaling $41,793 for his actions in the Niners' Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals . When adding all of those up, Warner has been fined $107,466 so far in 2026.
Beyond seeing his bank account decrease, the 29-year-old linebacker is now teetering on a possible suspension on two different fronts. If a player is disciplined for three hits on defenseless players, they receive an automatic one-game suspension, so Warner is two away from a brief ban. The same goes for hip-drop tackles, which is what Warner was fined for in Week 3.
The veteran is playing in his ninth season in the NFL and, aside from being hit with some fines, has bounced back in a big way after his 2025 campaign was cut short by an ankle injury. Through six games, Warner has posted 58 tackles, three forced fumbles and three pass breakups. Already, that forced fumble mark is one away from tying his career high (2023 and 2024), while his three quarterback hits are four away from matching his career high (2019).

We told you last week that the Colts were nowhere near being a 7-point favorite against anyone, including the Titans . That's especially true when the Indy offense continues to look lost with Daniel Jones at the helm and is now set to face Brian Flores' top-notch Vikings defense.
This season, Minnesota leads the NFL in blitz rate at a blistering 69.8%. The Vikings defense, which will be well rested after being on the bye, is No. 1 in the NFL in third-down and red-zone efficiency. Meanwhile, I'm encouraged by Kyler Murray as he's coming off his best performance of the season in Week 5. So far, his passer rating and yards per attempt have improved in each game. With the rest and home-field advantage, Minnesota should leave Indy in the dust.

Sure, the Jets burned us last week, but that shouldn't mean we look at them any differently in Week 7, especially with a fantastic matchup against the winless Dolphins . New York was competitive with the Patriots last week, and they've been a team we've backed several times already in 2026.

Deshaun Watson has been clutch this season, as he has four game-winning drives where he's been money. In that window, Watson has completed 75% of his passes (18-of-24), thrown for 179 yards, and has two touchdowns with zero interceptions. To his credit, Cam Ward has also popped in the fourth quarter this season as well, but Tennessee is also tied for the fewest points scored in the NFL over the first three quarters. If that persists, Cleveland has a defense capable of snuffing out any late Ward comeback attempt.

The Broncos offense is broken. More specifically, Bo Nix appears to be broken. Yeah, they beat the Seahawks last week, but they did that in spite of their quarterback play. title: Rise of the Peanut Punch: Why it's changing how defenses attack the football
summary: What was once a novelty is now a tool every defensive player uses
full_text:
During the second quarter of the Washington Commanders ' loss to the San Francisco 49ers , Niners' RB Christian McCaffrey took off through the middle of the defense on a screen pass. As Commanders' rookie Sonny Styles took McCaffrey down, EDGE K'Lavon Chaisson came flying in…throwing a punch at the football. The Peanut Punch, specifically.
The ball jumped out of McCaffrey's hands, onto the ground, and ended up being recovered by LB Frankie Luvu for a Commanders' turnover.
Elite peanut punch by K'Lavon Chaisson 👊 pic.twitter.com/zp180jRnz0
Fumbles are more and more common around the NFL this year, and part of it is due to the Peanut Punch. Once a novelty made legendary by Bears ' CB Charles "Peanut" Tillman, the Peanut Punch has become the primary cause of fumbles around the NFL. Through six games, there have been 175 forced fumbles, the highest number through six weeks since 2013. If we divide it between rushing and receiving, the 1.4% fumble rate on receptions is tied for the fifth-highest since TruMedia started tracking in 2000.
While there are many reasons for fumbles being so high, the expansion of the Peanut Punch around the league has been a very fun aspect to watch throughout the season. From players truly connecting on the punch and forcing fumbles to the wacky misses that end up seeing players get ejected for punching a guy's helmet, the Peanut Punch has become a constant threat to watch whenever your favorite team has the ball.
Despite being 2-4, the New York Jets have been one of the quietly fascinating teams to watch this season, mainly because they're forcing turnovers. They're second in the NFL in forced fumbles (10) through six games and have nine forced fumbles on the defensive side of the ball. In their loss to the Patriots on Sunday, LB Jamien Sherwood showed off some incredible hustle to force a fumble. When he got in range, guess what he did? That's right, he punched at the ball.
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn spoke to CBS Sports about how his team trains the timing of their punch-outs and how to judge punching the ball versus traditionally ripping it.
"I think it's two totally different situations," Glenn said. "There are some punch outs where, man, you want physical body on body, where you can punch and wrap. And then there are times when you're making an attack from an angle perspective to where, man, you want to take the ball, you want to rip it out.
"We practice both of them. We put in the same amount of time [practicing] both of them. I think they're both very effective techniques to be able to get the ball. I don't know where we're at for punch outs, but we have a number of balls from the ground. I think you can see our guys actually practicing those things. You get both of them from the punchouts and the rip out."
In a video the NFL released about the Peanut Punch, Philadelphia Eagles ' HC Nick Sirianni mentioned having the Eagles' video guy get them a cut-up of every fumble Tillman forced in his career, and he showed it to every coach and player on the team. Sirianni mentioned a blueprint the Eagles use to determine how and when to use the punch and get the ball out, and the Eagles have executed it well. Since Sirianni took over in 2021, the Eagles are second in the NFL in forced fumbles, behind the Pittsburgh Steelers .
What's really stood out about the Peanut Punch and its usage is that they've come from different angles. Players running in behind the ball carrier, angling in to help on a tackle. We've even seen DBs use it to force incompletions at the last second. In this story written about the Peanut Punch by ESPN's Matt Bowen in 2016 , Tillman is using the punch after squaring up a ball carrier and standing in front of them.
Tillman has used the punch from different angles before, but you don't really see many defenders squaring up and punching the ball out. It's primarily used to help defenders, coming in from different angles. Being able to get the ball out in practice like that is cool, but players attacking the football when the speed of the game is ratcheted up to 100 is what separates good teams from championship ones.
So how do ballcarriers protect themselves from the Peanut Punch? NFL legend and CBS Sports colleague JJ Watt broke it down during the Bills-Raiders broadcast. He showed that establishing more points of contact as a ball carrier prevents the ball from coming loose at the bottom, near the elbow, where it normally breaks free.
Holding the ball tightly and wrapping your other arm to create a harness with the ball prevents NFL players from getting the ball out, but it can also potentially break wrists ( as evidenced by Jim Nantz ):
JIM NANTZ JUST TRIED TO PEANUT PUNCH @JJWatt 🤣 "I did not think you were gonna go that hard" "my wrist is broken" 😭 pic.twitter.com/ocdRBn282r
Ball carriers on offense have to be hyper-aware of players punching at the ball in scrums and close quarters. New England Patriots' RB Rhamondre Stevenson has been on the wrong end of many fumbles in his career (seven since entering the league in 2021, to be exact), and with teams honing in on his hands, he has seen how teams are attacking the football.
"I think teams are just focusing on getting the ball out, no matter what they gotta do to get it," Stevenson said. "I think there's more punching, more ripping at it [the ball], and doing whatever they can to create a turnover."
Ballcarriers have to practice security against the Peanut Punch more often than ever now, because teams are going after them so much more.
Special teams is an area where Peanut punches can be especially chaotic, as is the case with kickoff or punt returns. New York Giants ' special teams coach Chris Horton said he talks with his team a lot about ball placement as a way to prevent becoming a victim of the Peant Punch.
"When we practice, we spend a lot of time emphasizing being intentional about protecting the football," Horton said. "If I'm running to the left, the ball should be on the left side, that way the defender can't punch it, or if he does, the ball is on the sideline and out of bounds. When we're out here [in practice], we want our guys going after the ball so we can get that experience so we know how to take care of the football."
The Peanut Punch has gone from a rare individual play to something you see in every game you watch on Sundays. When you're watching your favorite team protect or attack the football, you know that the punch is coming.
Most of the time, offenses know it too.
Yet, they still can't stop it.
author: JP Acosta

title: Aaron Rodgers, Kenneth Walker III address Eagles' handling of Jalen Hurts blood clot situation: 'That's crazy'
summary: Hurts is presumed to miss the rest of the 2026 regular season
full_text:
Jalen Hurts being ruled out indefinitely after blood clots were found in his lungs has drawn reaction from across the NFL .
The Philadelphia Eagles have been put under scrutiny for the handling of Hurts' medical issue, specifically in the lead-up to their Week 5 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. At the time, a superficial blood clot had been found in Hurts' calf following a team walk-through. Hurts ended up playing in that game before taking the team flight back to the United States. Upon their return stateside and further testing, Hurts was diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, which have put him on the shelf for what is believed to be the rest of the regular season.
The NFL concluded that the process that led to Hurts playing in Week 5 "was handled appropriately." However, the NFLPA has called for a further investigation into the matter. As for the players themselves, two of the league's most notable players have reacted to what has transpired with Hurts.
Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III has first-person experience with what Hurts is going through after dealing with blood clots in his lungs in high school.
"Yeah, honestly, just stay positive," Walker said during his Friday press conference . "You know, obviously, I guess you know about what happened in high school, like, with the blood clots and everything.  And he went on the flight, huh, and everything? Yeah, that's crazy. You know, honestly, just stay positive, and, you know, do all the things necessary that he needs to do, like, to get his body back right. But, yeah, I'll be praying for him, because that's not something, you know, we should take lightly."
Walker's concern for Hurts being on a flight in his condition has been a common one throughout the NFL, and a legitimate question in the team's handling of the situation. When asked about Hurts on Friday, Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers , who has had disputes with the NFL's medical staff in the past, admitted that he wasn't surprised by the confusing handling of the Eagles signal-caller.
"We're in the quarterback fraternity, so you don't want to see anything like that happen to anybody. Especially a guy who's still in football," Rodgers said during his Friday presser . "I don't know all the details about what's going on. All I've seen is what's been printed. Allen Sills, he's the guy in charge of all things medical at the NFL office, and he and I haven't always seen eye-to-eye about things. So, I can't say I'm real surprised."
In a response to the NFLPA's request, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said he welcomes an investigation into the handling of Hurts' blood clots but said that "the protocols were followed."
"The most important thing here is Jalen's health, ultimately, and the future of him," Goodell said. "He's a wonderful young man; not just a great player, but he's someone we all care deeply about. I'm more worried about his health, ultimately, but the protocols were followed."
With Hurts sidelined, Philadelphia has turned to backup quarterback Tanner McKee .
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: John Harbaugh challenges Tom Brady to leave retirement: 'I doubt for one second he could'
summary: The New York Giants coach sent a playful jab toward the future Pro Football Hall of Famer when assessing his quarterback situation
full_text:
J.J. McCarthy is set to make his first start for the New York Giants in Sunday's game against the Houston Texans , head coach John Harbaugh announced this week. This came after McCarthy relieved Jameis Winston in Week 6's loss to the New Orleans Saints and threw for 243 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter, and led three scoring drives.
The Giants traded for McCarthy last month in the wake of Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury. Unprovoked, this week in his assessment of this development in his quarterback room, Harbaugh likened the situation to former seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady hypothetically returning to the field.
Harbaugh used Brady in his analogy to describe McCarthy's need to learn the offense over the last few weeks before he was inserted into the lineup. Even one of the smartest signal callers in NFL history would need time to acclimate to a new scheme, he said.
"If Tom Brady decided he wanted to come back from retirement and actually could, which I doubt for one second he could, no matter what he thinks, you heard me, Tom — I don't think he'd be ready the first week," Harbaugh said Friday . "As much as you might want to put him in there, it wouldn't be in the best interest to play him the first week. There's a lot of things going on there."
To Harbaugh's point, McCarthy is adjusting to a new scheme after playing in 10 games last season with the Minnesota Vikings . McCarthy completed 140 of 243 passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions in 2025, his first season after missing the entirety of his rookie year due to injury.
The acclimation period takes time, according to Harbaugh, whose team expanded its playbook to 90 percent for McCarthy before last week's loss to the Saints. Operationally, the offense will adjust to McCarthy's strengths and his ability to move outside of the pocket.
"We fully feel as a staff, [Giants quarterbacks] coach [Brian] Callahan has done an amazing job working with him and getting him ready. We feel confident about it," Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy told reporters. "And now for us, it's a matter of doing what he does well and what we do well to put it all together."
Nagy said his offensive staff wants to keep play calls manageable for McCarthy in his first start.
Brady has no plans to return to the NFL as a player, but he did say during the spring he has asked about the league's policy on minority owners suiting up. Brady has an ownership stake in the Las Vegas Raiders and helped the franchise make advisory decisions this offseason.
"I actually have inquired, and they don't like that idea very much," Brady said . "We explored a lot of different things, and I'm very happily retired. Let me just say that, too."
author: Brad Crawford

title: Seahawks vs. Chiefs: How to watch as Kansas City's Kenneth Walker III returns to Seattle
summary: Here's what you need to know to catch the game
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs and Seattle Seahawks are facing off on Sunday Night Football this week. The Chiefs are looking to stay perfect, while the Seahawks look to get above .500 and take down the last undefeated AFC team.
Kansas City sits at 5-0 and is coming off a 22-6 divisional win over the winless Los Angeles Chargers . After missing the playoffs last season, KC is back in familiar territory as one of the strongest contenders as we near the halfway point of the regular season.
Seattle comes into their home stadium looking to shake off a 17-14 loss to the Denver Broncos in overtime. They are currently on a two-game losing streak, falling to their divisional leaders, the San Francisco 49ers , in Week 5. Since they faced the Broncos on Thursday Night Football last week, they've had some extra time to prepare and rest.
Despite how the records look, the Seahawks opened as favorites. The Chiefs will be without wide receiver Rashee Rice , who will miss his second straight game with a hamstring/knee injury. They will also be without starting right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion). Cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) was limited all week and is questionable, while tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited all week but carries no game designation.
On Seattle's side, safety Nick Emmanwori (hip) popped up on the injury report as a limited participant in Friday's practice and is officially questionable. Quarterback Drew Lock (right elbow) and linebackers Demarcus Lawrence (knee), Uchenna Nwosu (hip) and Connor O'Toole (hamstring) were all limited on Friday and are also questionable.
The last time the Chiefs and Seahawks met was in 2018, when Seattle came out on top 38-31.
Date: Sunday, Oct. 25 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location : Lumen Field (Seattle, WA) TV: NBC | Stream: fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -3 ( via DraftKings )
Sam Darnold seeing ghosts: Since it's October, and Sam Darnold is coming off a multiple-turnover game, bringing back this infamous quote feels appropriate. When he was with the New York Jets , he said he was "seeing ghosts" during a game against the New England Patriots , and the quote instantly became a meme. Darnold seemed to be seeing ghosts again against the Broncos last week, recording no touchdowns and two interceptions. He has seven total picks this season, second in the league, and is a main concern for the Seahawks offense. Darnold has proven what he can do, so it's not time to hit the panic button, but the turnover issues have to be worked out.
MVP returns: Not that long ago, running back Kenneth Walker was named the MVP of Super Bowl LX in a Seahawks uniform, and now he is making his return to Lumen Field for the first time as an opponent. The Seahawks run game hasn't just gone down since he has left; it's suffered. Walker has more rushing yards this season than the entire Seahawks offense, and in one fewer game. The Seahawks have 643 total rushing yards or 107.2 yards per game, and Walker has 665 yards (113.0 per game). The running back leads the NFL in forced missed tackles (52) and in yards (183) and touchdowns (six) against stacked boxes, meaning eight or more defenders. Walker no longer has the 12th man on his side, but I don't think he'll need it.
Strong defenses: The Seahawks defense has allowed the fewest total yards per game (237.3) in the NFL, and the Chiefs are toward the top of the league as well, at sixth-fewest in that category (306.0). Seattle's pass defense is its strong area, ranking among the league's best in fewest yards allowed per game (141.3), while the Chiefs excel at preventing the run. KC's defense has allowed the seventh-fewest yards per game (88.8). The Chiefs sit atop the NFL in rushing yards per game (159.8), and given that the Seahawks' defense is stronger against the pass, the Chiefs could run all over Seattle.
I am picking the Chiefs to win this one. I think Walker will continue his dominance in his old home and be a difference maker in the game. I think Darnold will begin to look better, but I still predict a turnover for the QB.
Pick: Chiefs 31, Seahawks 24
The Chiefs have a divisional game next week, facing the Broncos, who come into Week 7 at 4-2. Seattle has another primetime game next week. It will host the Chicago Bears , who have a few extra days off heading into the matchup after playing on Thursday Night Football this week. They defeated the Patriots and now sit at 5-2.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: National Tight Ends Day betting guide: 10 TEs who will score on this special Sunday

full_text:
Happy National Tight Ends Day!
This Sunday is a special one in the NFL ." Back in 2018, San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle declared "National Tight Ends Day" a holiday with some help from Jimmy Garoppolo . The NFL eventually joined in on the fun and officially listed the fourth Sunday of every October as a day to celebrate tight ends everywhere.
If you think this is stupid social media fodder, you're WRONG. In 2024, tight ends scored 16 touchdowns on 177 receptions. Those were the most catches by tight ends on any day in league history, per Yahoo Sports . Last year on "National Tight Ends Day," 12 touchdowns were scored by tight ends. Get ready for some big numbers this weekend.
Ever wonder where National Tight Ends Day came from? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/jsiDU4PHSW
Anytime TD bets have become popular wagers among football fans because of their longer odds. Even when it comes to an expected TD scorer, they make for a fun parlay leg. Below, we will break down 10 tight ends we think will find the end zone on Sunday.
Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
You're telling me the founder of "National Tight Ends Day" is plus money to score? Come on! Kittle has caught five touchdowns so far this season, which is tied for third in the NFL. The banged-up 49ers are on a short week and on the road vs. the Atlanta Falcons , but this price is worth it.
Sticking in Atlanta, Kyle Pitts has struck pay dirt on "National Tight Ends Day" before. He's also been on a heater as of late. Pitts caught a touchdown in the overtime loss to the Baltimore Ravens a couple of weeks ago, and then caught two touchdowns in the loss to the Chicago Bears last Sunday.
Maybe Pat Freiermuth will be the first tight end to score on "National Tight Ends Day." He and the Pittsburgh Steelers kick off NFL Sunday in Paris, France, against the New Orleans Saints . Two weeks ago, Freiermuth found the end zone twice against the Indianapolis Colts .
If not Freiermuth, maybe Juwan Johnson is our first tight end scorer this weekend. He got off to an incredible start this season, catching three touchdowns in the first three games of the season while averaging five receptions per game. However, he caught just four passes for 16 yards in Week 5 and didn't catch a pass last week against the New York Giants . I'll take him to bounce back.
Houston Texans tight end Dalton Schultz hasn't found the end zone yet this year. What a perfect day for him to score that first touchdown. Schultz's production has been up and down in 2026, but he did catch 12 passes for 140 yards in Week 2 against the Cincinnati Bengals when Nico Collins was out of the lineup. I'm expecting plenty of points against the Giants.
There have been some great free-agent additions this season, such as Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III and 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans . One player who should be mentioned in that conversation is Giants tight end Isaiah Likely . He's caught 39 passes for 383 yards and five touchdowns through six games, joining Plaxico Burress as the second player in Giants history to have 375 yards receiving and five receiving touchdowns in their first six career games with Big Blue.
No one does the "griddy" like Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki , and the forecast in Baltimore calls for his moment in the spotlight. The Ravens' secondary will have to account for Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins , leaving Gesicki with some opportunities to make a play. He's caught just 12 passes this season, but four of those 12 receptions have been touchdowns!
We're expecting some points when the Green Bay Packers take on the Detroit Lions this Sunday, as it's the highest listed total on the board (O/U 53.5). Tucker Kraft posted a career-high 143 yards receiving and two touchdowns during "National Tight Ends Day" last year.
Brock Bowers just became the fifth tight end all-time to record 375 yards receiving and three touchdowns in the first four games of a season. He scored touchdowns in each of his first three games, but didn't get to celebrate in the end zone last Sunday against the Buffalo Bills .
Last but certainly not least, our final tight end touchdown scorer is reserved for none other than Travis Kelce on "Sunday Night Football." He's caught just two touchdowns so far this season, but he does lead the Chiefs in receiving this year with 299 yards on 20 catches.
