title: Revisiting Raiders' 2026 NFL Draft: What Vegas is getting out of Fernando Mendoza, what's next
summary: Sitting behind Kirk Cousins was always the initial plan, but the Raiders may soon be pressed to start the No. 1 overall selection
full_text:
With the No. 1 overall selection, the Las Vegas Raiders were faced with a decision between Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza and the top-rated non-quarterback prospect. The franchise started anew with first-year head coach Klint Kubiak and Mendoza.
The Raiders invested in his development before he was ever officially a member of the organization. In addition to hiring Kubiak, an offensive-minded head coach who had proven his mettle by guiding Sam Darnold to the Super Bowl , the team signed free agent center Tyler Linderbaum to a market-setting deal and veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins to alleviate any pressure to start the rookie too early.
Was the franchise justified in spending the No. 1 overall selection on Mendoza?
The plan was always to sit Mendoza for an extended period of time, so his lack of playing time to this point is not a reflection of his performance. Mendoza saw his first meaningful action in a decisive loss to the Patriots earlier this month. In a game that had already been decided, Las Vegas elected to sit veteran Kirk Cousins and insert the No. 1 overall selection during the fourth quarter. Mendoza completed 6-of-8 pass attempts for 48 yards, but there was a lot to like in his debut.
First and foremost, the rookie looked comfortable with his mechanics. His upper and lower bodies were married, which meant that when he moved from one read to the next, his feet were already positioned to throw it. One of his farthest completions went to wide receiver Tre Tucker . Mendoza saw Kindle Vildor's momentum carrying him downfield and knew that Tucker was running a comeback into the vacant area, so he let go of the ball before the receiver had gotten out of his break. The ball was there waiting when Tucker had opened up out of the break. It was an easy completion that allowed for a few additional yards after the catch.
One of his two incompletions was a beautiful throw to the boundary in which rookie receiver Malik Benson had plenty of real estate to get his feet down inbounds and just didn't. It is worth noting that Mendoza was throwing to backups against New England's also backup defense rather than handing off to Ashton Jeanty or throwing to Brock Bowers .
One final play to discuss. Mendoza was locked in on Dareke Young , but recognized at the last second that Vildor was staring down the route and already breaking on the football. The Indiana product tucked the football, escaped and found a checkdown to the running back later in the play. The Raiders-Patriots history almost had another Tuck Rule submission in its history.
The Raiders - Patriots series almost added another Tuck Rule incident to its history. pic.twitter.com/vNiwquaWO0
One of the concerns coming out of Bloomington was Mendoza's operation with pressure at his feet. He was hardly pressured against the Patriots, so it is difficult to glean anything from that standalone game, but there may have been a bit of panic on the play above when he tucked the ball and found a blocker against his chest.
The Raiders are playing .500 football six games into the season. They did not win a third game until the regular-season finale a year ago. If the season begins to slip away from Las Vegas, then it may be time to bench veteran Kirk Cousins in favor of Mendoza.
Whether through media availability or a variety of commercials, Mendoza has let it be known that he is all about data. Starting several games this season will go a long way in the quarterback's quest to collect data points and troubleshoot this season's shortcomings in preparation for next season.
An NFL schedule rarely presents an ideal situation to insert a rookie quarterback. The next stretch of six games before the bye week in the team's schedule is brutal regarding defensive competency. The 49ers , Seahawks , Broncos and Browns all rank top-10 in defensive EPA/play, according to TruMedia. The Rams and Jets are also considered average or better.
There is no reason to believe Las Vegas may not have its quarterback of the future. Over time, there may be evidence to the contrary, but Mendoza's limited play has inspired cautious optimism.

title: NFL closes 'NFL House' in Paris amid security concerns as city braces for more protests
summary: The Week 7 matchup between the Steelers and Saints is still on as scheduled
full_text:
As the NFL prepares for its first-ever game in France, when the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints square off at Stade de France on Sunday morning, security concerns continue to loom over the Week 7 international contest due to the ongoing protests in Paris.
On Saturday, the league announced the closure of its "NFL House" in Paris as the French capital is gearing up for more demonstrations. Earlier this month, Parisians began rebelling against the rising cost of living and poor school conditions. Those protests, however, have turned violent, with stores being looted, property being burned, and continued clashes with police.
The NFL officially announced the closure to fans on Saturday morning via its "One Pass" apps, and it comes a day after announcing the shutdown of its pop-up NFL shop due to "potential accessibility issues," according to the Associated Press . The fan events at "NFL House" on Saturday included "French Athletes in Football" and "From the Field to the Community."
On top of this "NFL House" closure, the New Orleans Saints announced Saturday that their "Saints House" event has been postponed until Sunday.
Saints House has been postponed until Sunday. Official hours will be announced later today.
These are just the latest NFL-related cancellations due to the protests. On Thursday, security concerns led to the cancellation of a Steelers fan event in Bastille set for this weekend. Beyond the NFL, major museums, including the Louvre and Orsay Museum, are closed on Saturday, according to CBS News . Paris Saint-Germain's Ligue 1 matchup with Lyon was also moved from Sunday to Monday at the request of Paris police.
The U.S. State Department issued a security alert this week that "Americans in Paris for the NFL game" should "exercise caution and be aware of their surroundings."
While the NFL and French authorities will take every measure to ensure a safe environment for the game, these protests have raised questions about whether to play it in Paris. Despite that concern, the league and union officials told The Ringer on Saturday morning that the game is on as scheduled.

title: Revisiting Browns' 2026 NFL Draft: Did the K.C. Concepcion, Denzel Boston selections fix the offense?
summary: Concepcion and Boston are sparking the pass game, while Spencer Fano and Austin Barber have quickly solidified the rebuilt offensive line
full_text:
Cleveland's offense had really struggled in recent years under head coach Kevin Stefanski. The quarterback play was inconsistent to bad, and a once dominant offensive line had deteriorated. As a result, the franchise elected to change leadership, leading to the hiring of head coach Todd Monken.
The Browns are averaging 17.7 points per game this season; they averaged 14.8 points per game or less over the last two seasons. What has been the catalyst for that change? Well, they may have a few 2026 NFL Draft selections to thank.
General manager Andrew Berry opened draft night knowing that the left tackle and wide receiver positions must be addressed. They had been considering both Texas A&M's K.C. Concepcion (Round 1, No. 24 overall) and Washington's Denzel Boston (Round 2, No. 39 overall) with their second selection in the first round. They did not anticipate Boston being available at No. 39 overall and saw it as an opportunity they could not pass up.
At times, quarterback Deshaun Watson has been on different pages from his rookie receivers. Concepcion has been led into some dangerous hits, and Boston has been forced to make contested catches rather than the ball being on him as he comes out of his break.
The former's role had primarily been limited to the short and intermediate segments of the field. Among receivers with at least 15 receptions, his 6.60 air yards per target is the 10th-lowest in the league. Concepcion is elusive with the ball in his hands and has dispelled pre-draft concerns regarding drops — he has zero on the season. Accuracy and anticipation from a quarterback are incredibly important for a receiver like Concepcion because his greatest impact is felt post-catch. Watson has been off-target on 12.1% of his throws, according to TruMedia, which is worse than the average quarterback. Concepcion has been productive as a rookie, but the stat line could be even better. His potential is that of a high-level No. 2 in the league.
Boston is an entirely different type of receiver. He has a big frame with a physical play style, a combination that has been thriving in the NFL recently.   While Concepcion ranks low in air yards per target, Boston is first (16.45) among receivers with at least 15 receptions. He shows nuance getting out of his breaks but also has the size and aggressiveness to play above the rim. Although he has been credited with zero drops, a few downfield attempts have gone off his fingertips. Better rhythm with Watson would lead to increased production for Boston.
Additionally, Cleveland drafted left tackle Spencer Fano (No. 9 overall). They were originally positioned to pick No. 6 overall, but traded down with Kansas City in exchange for third and fifth-round choices. LSU cornerback Mansoor Delane was picked by the Chiefs, then Ohio State linebacker Sonny Styles and Arizona State wide receiver Jordyn Tyson were taken before Fano.
Fano started at left tackle for Utah, then moved to the right side when Caleb Lomu joined the fray. He has transitioned back to left tackle for the Browns with mixed results.
A smart player who communicates and picks up exchanges well, Fano has good foot mobility, but undersets at times, and he got walked back a bit against the Panthers and Jaguars . Most of his issues are correctable, and he has been an above-average left tackle for the franchise thus far. TruMedia credits him with eight pressures and one sack allowed on 353 pass blocking snaps through six games.
When the team traded veteran Amari Cooper , it left the organization grasping at straws. They had already acquired Jerry Jeudy , but Jeudy was never meant to be the primary outlet. It is clear that Boston and Concepcion will be the team's top two targets moving forward, which has made Jeudy expendable at the trade deadline — a development few could have seen coming in April.
Boston could be one of the top-15 wide receivers in the league. Concepcion has the potential to be a high-level No. 2 in the league.
Berry was also tasked with replacing five offensive line starters in one offseason. The project began with the acquisition of Tytus Howard and continued with free agent signings of Zion Johnson and Elgton Jenkins .
The unit, as a whole, has improved, but there is still work to be done. Looking forward, Johnson, Howard and, to a lesser degree, Jenkins have contracts that bind them to northeast Ohio through the 2027 season. Fano and rookie right guard Austin Barber are assured starting roles as well. The only question is whether the Browns will work Barber at right tackle and Howard at guard at some point, which Howard has done in the past.
Fano is an average to good left tackle with the potential to be a franchise cornerstone and top-10 at his position.
Cleveland has done an excellent job in the draft over the last two years and may be more reliable quarterback play away from seriously contending.
author: Josh Edwards

title: Revisiting Seahawks' trades for Leonard Williams, Ernest Jones IV: Duo powered Seattle's Super Bowl D
summary: Williams and Jones were part of Mike Macdonald's defensive overhaul
full_text:
Mike Macdonald made no bones about building the Seahawks in his image. Yes, Pete Carroll had been in Seattle for more than a dozen years and built a powerhouse that won one Super Bowl and made another. But Macdonald wasn't going to just keep the status quo, nor was he going to try to build Ravens 2.0 out on the West Coast, even if he had experienced tremendous success as the Ravens defensive coordinator.
The Seahawks' 2026 Super Bowl triumph, in Macdonald's second season, came from being bold. In Macdonald's first year, the Seahawks went 10-7 and just missed the playoffs — by all accounts, a good football team and a solid start to Macdonald's tenure. Macdonald didn't see it that way.
He fired Ryan Grubb as offensive coordinator and brought in Klint Kubiak. Shortly before free agency began, the Seahawks released Tyler Lockett , and D.K. Metcalf requested a trade on the same day. Not only did the Seahawks trade Metcalf to the Steelers , but they also sent Geno Smith to the Raiders . It was going to be a new offense, one built more in line with how Macdonald envisioned that side of the ball. In came Sam Darnold , up stepped Jaxon Smith-Njigba , and on came the Super Bowl rings earlier this year.
But the Seahawks' championship was more powered by a truly dominant defense — Macdonald's side of the ball — and to see how two key figures of that unit came to be, we have to go back to two trades: one made right before Macdonald arrived, another shortly after.
Ahead of the Seahawks' "Sunday Night Football" matchup with the Chiefs , we look back on how Seattle came away with absolute steals in acquiring defensive lineman Leonard Williams and linebacker Ernest Jones .
With the Giants 2-6 in late October, they were looking to sell at the deadline. The 5-2 Seahawks were looking to buy, especially at pass rusher after Uchenna Nwosu's injury. Williams was in the final year of a three-year, $63 milion extension, and with the Giants having extended Dexter Lawrence the previous offseason, it looked unlikely they would also hand out a hefty deal to Williams, who was 30 at the time. The two teams consummated a deal, with the Giants taking on most of the remaining money on the agreement.
After the season, even though Carroll had moved on and Macdonald had arrived, Williams remained a priority for Seattle. The Seahawks signed him to a three-year, $64.5 million deal as free agency began.
This was the second trade in two whirlwind months for Jones. After playing an integral role for the Super Bowl-champion Rams as a rookie in 2021, he ascended to a starter in his second season and made 15 starts in his third year. But Jones and Los Angeles couldn't come to an extension after his third season, so the Rams shipped him and a sixth-round pick to the Titans for a fifth-round pick just before the start of the 2024 season.
But the Titans were a mess to start the season (and all season, frankly, finishing 3-14 and earning the No. 1 pick). At 1-5, they traded DeAndre Hopkins to the Chiefs and, later that day, sent Jones to the Seahawks. After losing Jordyn Brooks and Bobby Wagner in free agency, Seattle had tried to fortify its linebacking corps with Baker and Tyrel Dodson on one-year deals, but it simply wasn't working out. The Titans got a linebacker to help finish out the season, plus a pick to build for the future in return.
Seattle, it turned out, had unearthed a star for the second trade deadline in as many years.
Playing alongside 2024 first-round pick Byron Murphy , Williams was already making a big impact early in the 2024 season: 2.5 sacks, 12 quarterback hits through six weeks. But the Seahawks defense was pretty middling overall and downright bad in some spots, including 28th in yards per carry allowed.
Macdonald was Baltimore's defensive coordinator when the Ravens acquired Roquan Smith from the Bears midseason. He knew a good linebacker could shape a defense, and while Jones wasn't Smith, Macdonald clearly saw him as an upgrade. It ended up being a huge one that impacted every aspect of the defense
Seahawks 2024 defense ranks
Jones was everywhere, racking up 94 tackles in just 10 games for Seattle. He had an interception, a forced fumble and half a sack. Though it wasn't quite enough for Seattle to make the playoffs, Macdonald could feel confident he had found his man in the middle. Williams registered 11 sacks, one-half sack short of his career high, and a career-high 16 tackles for loss.
The Seahawks gave Jones a three-year, $33 million extension ahead of free agency. The strong defensive unit as a whole proved to be a precursor to what was to come in 2025.
Macdonald doubled down on improving his defense after the 2024 offseason. The Seahawks signed DeMarcus Lawrence to bolster the edge and drafted do-it-all safety/defensive weapon Nick Emmanwori in the second round. The Murphy/Williams/Lawrence front became a wrecking crew, with Williams recording seven sacks and earning second-team All-Pro honors, the first of his career. He got an extension in the offseason and has three more sacks this year already.
Jones was also a second-team All-Pro, having gone from a player two teams moved on from to a vital piece of arguably the league's most dominant unit. His five interceptions last year were tied for the most by any linebacker and one more than he had in his first four seasons combined. He has another interception and three sacks — 1.5 shy of his career high — already this year.
This week, both will be key in slowing down Kenneth Walker III , their former teammate, who leads the NFL in rushing yards.
The most important thing to acknowledge in assessing how the Giants and Titans did is realizing that Williams and Jones wouldn't have had the same impact on their respective former teams. Macdonald is one of the game's brightest defensive minds, able to put his players in positions to succeed and develop talent everywhere. Speaking to "Hard Knocks" this offseason, Williams' wife even said Williams might have retired had he stayed with New York.
The Giants' considerable trade return netted Nubin, who has been a solid player when healthy. He's had a few injuries so far in his career, but he had 98 tackles as a rookie and 78 tackles — plus seven for loss — last year. He looks like a potential long-term starter or contributor. Mbow played in 13 games as a rookie (three starts) and has appeared in six games (one start) this season. He's mostly a special teams contributor and a depth option on the offensive line.
The Titans moved on from Baker after the 2024 season. He spent 2025 with Cleveland and is not currently on a team. Helm had some nice moments across a 44-catch rookie season, but he has just nine catches in six games this year. He looks like a low-level starter or solid No. 2 tight end.

title: Revisiting the 2026 NFL Draft: Jonah Coleman is all Broncos have to show for their efforts
summary: Fourth-round running back Jonah Coleman is the only draft pick to see the field this year, as Denver gets virtually zero production from its first-year players through six games
full_text:
The Denver Broncos likely expected to get very little contributions from their rookie class after trading away significant draft capital, but even they may be surprised by just how little. Through six games, the sum of Denver's 2026 rookie class snap count is just 46, and the majority of those came on special teams.
Who did the Broncos draft, and how have they fared? CBS Sports revisits the 2026 NFL Draft .
Denver traded its first-round pick to Miami in exchange for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle . Waddle has 22 receptions for 228 yards and one touchdown through six games. With the selection acquired from the Broncos, the Dolphins moved up slightly and chose San Diego State cornerback Chris Johnson , who has played the lion's share of defensive snaps for the franchise.
Onyedim has not yet played for the Broncos. The defensive line had been a position of strength for the team so far this season, but generally, players taken in the top 100 overall are expected to at least be part of the rotation. However, few players taken after Onyedim in the third round could have helped Denver right now. Perhaps Cowboys linebacker Jaishawn Barham or Patriots tight end Eli Raridon , but the options were limited so far.
Coleman is the only draft pick who has played this season. He played 28 offensive snaps and nine special teams snaps over two games before succumbing to an injury. Prior to said injury, he offered glimpses of being able to handle the feature role: standing tall in pass protection, catching passes out of the backfield and showing patience in the run game. The Washington product could soon return from the injured reserve.
Casey has served as depth along the offensive line and was never expected to be an immediate starter. Joly was left on the cutting room floor as Denver trimmed its roster to the 53-man limit. Miami claimed him on waivers, but he has played just five special teams snaps.
Northern Arizona wide receiver Kolbe Katsis has been on the practice squad for the Broncos, but he was called into action and contributed on special teams against the Rams .

title: How the Cardinals can defeat the Broncos
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are not dead after all. In fact, they are showing good signs of life. But now, they have an upcoming game against AFC power Denver Broncos. After that, the schedule is just as difficult with the Dallas Cowboys, Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams, and the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs. With a one-game […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 18: Josh Wallace #30 and Poona Ford #97 of the Los Angeles Rams tackle Michael Wilson #14 of the Arizona Cardinals in the fourth quarter of a game at SoFi Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are not dead after all. In fact, they are showing good signs of life. But now, they have an upcoming game against AFC power Denver Broncos. After that, the schedule is just as difficult with the Dallas Cowboys, Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams, and the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs. With a one-game win streak, Arizona has the opportunity to salvage what looked like another dismal season. RELATED: OPENING LINE FOR WEEK 7 Next up, the Broncos in a home game. Last year, Denver was the #1 seed in the AFC with a 14-3-0 record and at one time had an 11-game win streak. After missing the Wild Card round, in the divisional game they defeated the Buffalo Bills 33-30 in overtime, and then lost a heartbreaker 10-7 to the New England Patriots in the AFC Championship Game. So, they are a very good team. After six games this year, they sit at 4-2-0 and are in second place in the AFC West Division. How can the Cardinals beat this exceptional AFC powerhouse? Broncos are not a good road team Oftentimes, the home crowd is the twelfth man. The Cardinals wish their home field were a safe haven, but unfortunately this year they are 0-2. The Broncos are 3-0 at home but 1-2 while traveling to games. Denver has struggled mightily on the road. They were beaten badly by the undefeated Chiefs 31-10 in Kansas City, and 24-14 by another undefeated team, the San Francisco 49ers. At one time against San Fran, they had built a 17-6 lead while Denver had punted five times. Their offense was stymied repeatedly without any run game. QB Bo Nix only had the short passing game to stand on, while the intermediate passing zones were minimal. In the end, the Broncos only had 82 rushing yards. In Week 1 against the Chiefs, the first half was fairly close, but the game quickly got out of hand after halftime. Going into the final quarter, it was 24-10. Again, Denver could not run the ball whatsoever, and at the final gun, they had 61 rushing yards. Use the offense’s playmakers early and often The Broncos have a good defense. It was their catalyst from last season, and it has carried over into this year’s roster. Make no mistake, this is a very good team. They just defeated the Seattle Seahawks, who many believe is the best team in the NFC. Cardinals TE Trey McBride leads the league in receptions with 49. He has a knack for getting open, and so far, no linebacker has been able to cover him. Not sure if switching to a safety would help matters, but in a six-game sample, opposing defenses haven’t had an answer for him. The Broncos are ranked #5 in passing defense this year, so this is a tough situation for Arizona’s passing game. WR Michael Wilson is ranked #11 in the league in receiving. That means that the Cardinals have two top talents that should be thrown to repeatedly. Use this talent as much as possible. But the Cardinals have two aces in the hole: WRs Kendrick Bourne and Jalen Brooks. Bourne is the guy who can take the short-to-intermediate throws and advance a drive. Brooks can become a game-decider. In the Rams contest, he only had two catches, and the last one decided the outcome of the game. Use your weapons. Make QB Bo Nix very uncomfortable The Broncos signalcaller, Bo Nix, does really well when he has time to survey the field. He is a gifted quarterback who has a great arm and is very accurate. However, that is within the confines of a clean pocket. When Nix is forced to scramble or run, his ability to hurt a defense is greatly diminished. When he is flushed and expected to look downfield, he has lost a lot of his ability to move the sticks. But this article discusses how Nix has regressed this year. The key to disrupting Denver’s offense is to collapse the pocket and be on Nix’s tail every time he drops back to pass. Now, having said that, maybe Arizona’s defense can’t come through. Perhaps this shouldn’t even be listed as a method to defeat the Broncos. But it is a fact. But Denver’s passing attack is currently ranked #31 in the league. Their inability to pass the ball is their Achilles heel. The Cardinals’ pass defense is ranked #22, which is in the bottom third. Nix is ranked #21 in total passing yards (1,049), but is #73 in average yards per completion (5.6). He has thrown only six touchdowns all year, with three interceptions. Their offensive line is very good at run blocking, but has allowed the fourth-most sacks. That is a huge stat to know going into this weekend. Last week, the Seahawks contained Nix, and he had only 107 passing yards. Denver’s passing game is almost devoid of any explosiveness, as Nix relies on short completions as well as dink-and-dunk gains. Provide plenty of pressure on Nix. Now, can DT Walter Nolen step up? What about DE Josh Sweat? Can DE Darius Robinson show up two games in a row?

title: Falcons vs. 49ers: What will Week 7’s win or loss mean for Atlanta?
summary: It’s become danger time for the Atlanta Falcons, who have sandwiched their two impressive and feel good victories in prime time against the Saints and Packers in between a pair of two game losing streaks which have them stuck inside a hole, and they better get moving to maneuver their way out quick. The Birds […]
full_text: It’s become danger time for the Atlanta Falcons, who have sandwiched their two impressive and feel good victories in prime time against the Saints and Packers in between a pair of two game losing streaks which have them stuck inside a hole, and they better get moving to maneuver their way out quick. The Birds once again laid an egg in a home game which resembled at best a neutral sight battle and at worst an absolute Bears fan takeover, against Chicago. Things don’t get any easier as they now host the undefeated San Francisco 49ers, led by two Falcon coaches of yesteryear in Kyle Shanahan and Raheem Morris, who are looking to bury their former employer’s season. Here is the scenario the Falcons face if they beat the San Francisco 49ers in Week 7, as well as if they lose. If the Falcons win It will be one of the bigger upsets in the NFL season up to this point and they will bring the 1972 Miami Dolphins one step closer to their yearly champagne celebration, which happens after the final undefeated team suffers its first blemish. This one would bring about memories of 2019, when the 4-9 Falcons went to the Bay and upset the 11-2 Niners in one of the shocks of the season. This ship that is Atlanta’s season may start to get steadied just in time to avoid the impending iceberg that’s now clearly visible in the distance. The Birds would move to 3-4 with a chance to pull themselves back to the surface with a game against the struggling Buccaneers next week as they navigate the difficult portion of the schedule. The first place Carolina Panthers currently play the Bucs this week. Atlanta could get to within one game in the loss column if Tampa pulls off an upset. They would also shake away from the New Orleans Saints if the Kellen Moore led team stumbles in its game against Pittsburgh, played in Paris this weekend. If the Falcons lose Things will be derailing in real time as even a victory against Tampa next week (which is not a given) won’t be able to put them in a decent position. They would be 3-5 with games against the Bengals and Chiefs before the bye week and games against the Lions and Vikings on the other side of the bye. It doesn’t get much more brutal. Needless to say, at this point we will already need to start looking at Atlanta’s potential draft position moving forward, as 2-5 would be justification enough to do so. There’s a large cluster of 2-4 teams in the league right now, and any who lose this weekend will likely be in top 10 draft pick placement for the time being. Raheem Morris would continue what seems to have become a tradition of a former Falcons head coach who was fired returning to Atlanta the very next season and beating the Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Dan Quinn came back as Cowboys defensive coordinator and won in 2021, Arthur Smith came back as Steelers offensive coordinator and won in 2024, and now Morris will have come back as 49ers defensive coordinator and won.

title: Turning Point: Why Falcons defense needs a spark from their rookie class
summary: The Atlanta Falcons’ defense has been their most reliable unit this year. However, they’ve hit a wall in recent losses. Special-teams turnovers explain the outcome against the Chicago Bears, but Atlanta’s defense has given up 30 points in back-to-back weeks. Both the Baltimore Ravens and Bears’ offenses too often dictated the terms of each game. If the […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 05: Avieon Terrell #12 of the Atlanta Falcons celebrates during an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on October 5, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons ’ defense has been their most reliable unit this year. However, they’ve hit a wall in recent losses. Special-teams turnovers explain the outcome against the Chicago Bears, but Atlanta’s defense has given up 30 points in back-to-back weeks. Both the Baltimore Ravens and Bears’ offenses too often dictated the terms of each game. If the Falcons want to return to the Top 10-caliber defense they showed during the season’s first month, they’ll need a new spark. That spark should come from their three rookie defenders: Kendal Daniels, Harold Perkins, and Avieon Terrell. Unlike in 2025, when the Falcons intentionally dropped their rookies into the deep end , the team has been more patient with its 2026 class. Daniels and Perkins have both played significant roles at linebacker, but they essentially split the second-linebacker reps next to Divine Deablo. Daniels gets the work on early downs in the team’s base and big nickel sets, while Perkins exclusively works in the team’s regular nickel sets. Meanwhile, Terrell started the year with significant reps at nickel cornerback, but was relegated to spot duty at outside cornerback when Billy Bowman returned in Week 3. Avieon makes strong case to start over Mike Hughes However, against the Bears, Terrell made his first official start at outside cornerback thanks to injuries and performed well. With the Falcons’ cornerback room looking healthier this week against the San Francisco 49ers , the question remains whether Terrell reverts to a role player or continues to see starter reps. Given the struggles of starter Mike Hughes, it makes the most sense to see Avieon continue to get the bulk of the snaps opposite elder brother, A.J. That spot has been troublesome for the Falcons since A.J. arrived in 2020, when the team has had a revolving door of starters . Hughes has been the steadiest presence since 2024, not because he’s their best, but rather their only option. Unfortunately, the Falcons have spent the last few offseasons prioritizing other needs , leaving cornerback largely ignored. That changed when the team drafted Avieon with their top pick in 2026 . So far, the team has leaned into Avieon’s versatility to play both inside and outside, which has helped given the prevalence of cornerback injuries at the start of this season. But now it’s time to start cultivating Avieon’s long-term fit at outside cornerback. That appears to be the vision, based on comments from defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich earlier this month , when he praised Avieon’s high-end potential there. The Falcons haven’t had a reliable cornerback duo since the heyday of Desmond Trufant and Robert Alford, roughly a decade ago. If the Terrell brothers can form a steady pair, it should do wonders to benefit the team’s defense. Last week, Terrell acquitted himself well against the Bears, allowing just two receptions for 13 yards, according to PFF . That debut stands in stark contrast to the 58 receiving yards per game Hughes allowed in the same role over the five games before. While Ulbrich and the Falcons’ coaches have repeatedly expressed confidence in Hughes’ skills , last week provided the final evidence that Terrell is the better option. Avieon’s stingier coverage can help the Falcons return to their sixth-ranked coverage from the first four games , when they allowed just a 59 percent completion rate. The coverage has struggled in the last two losses, allowing a 79 percent completion rate and ranking dead last in that span . Rookie linebackers will need to step up against upcoming 49ers test While Terrell provides a youthful spark to the team’s secondary, the Falcons have had a similar one at linebacker with Daniels and Perkins. Both have been steady contributors through six weeks, but the 49ers could test that with Deablo out of the lineup . Both rookies will be instrumental in containing 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey and tight end George Kittle. Facing two Hall-of-Fame-caliber playmakers will be a huge challenge, but it will also be an excellent litmus test for how far both young linebackers have developed. How they fare on Sunday will help determine how bright the Falcons defense’s future could be, both in the short and long term. The short-term impact is obvious given the caliber of the 49ers offense and the Falcons’ upcoming opponents. San Francisco ranks second in EPA per play entering Week 7, according to Next Gen Stats . Atlanta also faces the No. 4-ranked Kansas City Chiefs , No. 5-ranked Detroit Lions , and No. 9-ranked Cincinnati Bengals over the next six weeks. This year, the Falcons defense hasn’t matched last year’s success against premier offenses, when it stymied top-ranked units like the Los Angeles Rams , Buffalo Bills , and New England Patriots . A huge factor in their 2025 success was the defense’s ability to take the ball away. This year’s defense hasn’t turned the ball over as readily, with just a single interception from safety Xavier Watts so far. Last year’s defense entered Week 7 ranked fifth in takeaways per game , while this year’s unit ranks 27th . Creating splash plays becomes the next evolution for Falcons rookies Atlanta’s two rookie linebackers aren’t responsible for that deficiency, but fixing it is the next step in their development. Both Daniels and Perkins have shown they can handle their assignments against the run and pass, with only a smattering of rookie mental lapses. As they get more comfortable with added reps, they can rise above what is being asked of them and do more than expected, which is where turnovers come in. It’s one thing to do your job by making a tackle and breaking up a pass, it’s another to strip the ball carrier or snatch a pick. Both Daniels and Perkins are poised for that leap, and it will hopefully begin against the 49ers. It’s about time all three 2026 rookies started showing out, which lines up well with when last year’s rookie class did the same. In the secondary, Bowman and Watts both made their fair share of splash plays in the first month of 2025. Terrell’s delay in making his own can be blamed mostly on limited reps, and if he begins getting starter snaps, he should have more opportunities to make game-changing plays in the coming weeks, as Bowman and Watts did. In the front seven last year, Jalon Walker began a breakout stretch in early November, and that month also marked the start of James Pearce’s seven-game sack streak . As October comes to a close, increased responsibilities should similarly push Daniels and Perkins to the next level. So far, the Falcons have leaned on the veteran safety net, but it’s time to take the training wheels off this 2026 rookie class and see if they can get more from their defense. Daniels, Perkins, and Terrell’s contributions should prove instrumental in that boost. The Falcons’ pass rush remains one of the league’s top units at generating pressure . With improved coverage and more turnovers, the Falcons defense is well-equipped to meet upcoming challenges against the 49ers and other top offenses. If the rookies can turn steady execution into game-altering plays, the Falcons won’t just survive this upcoming stretch, but also build a foundation of dominant defense for years to come.

title: Falcons vs. 49ers series history: Win-loss record, matchup results
summary: When you look at the geographic distance separating the cities of Atlanta and San Francisco (or rather, Santa Clara these days) you would never for a second imagine that they used to share the same division. Such was the reality of the old NFC West, however, and with it we’ve seen many a matchup between […]
full_text: SAN FRANCISCO - SEPTEMBER 23: Jessie Tuggle #58 of the Atlanta Falcons tackles Joe Montana #16 of the San Francisco 49ers during a National Football League game played on September 23, 1990 at Candlestick Park in San Francisco, California. (Photo by David Madison/Getty Images) | Getty Images When you look at the geographic distance separating the cities of Atlanta and San Francisco (or rather, Santa Clara these days) you would never for a second imagine that they used to share the same division. Such was the reality of the old NFC West, however, and with it we’ve seen many a matchup between the Falcons and 49ers. There’s good news and bad news from the Falcons’ perspective when it comes to their head to head history against San Fran — the good news is that this is the team against whom the Birds have the joint-third most victories against out of everyone in the NFL; the bad news is that only the New Orleans Saints have beaten them more times. Atlanta has a less than stellar 33-49-1 record against the team that “big brothered” them in the old West for decades. The Niners won the first five matchups and while you would think that they just never looked back, Atlanta then got the better of them for an extended period of time from the back half of the ‘70s into the early ‘80s, winning 10 out of 13 matchups between 1975 and 1981. Joe Montana restored order for the juggernaut Niners, however, leading his team to four Super Bowl titles in the 1980s and a 12-1-1 record against the Falcons between 1984 and 1990. San Francisco kept chugging along, winning most of the matchups throughout the 1990s, but the Falcons have had the slight upper hand since the onset of their “Dirty Bird” season in 1998, going an overall 11-9 from that season through present day. Each team has traded heartbreaking playoff supremacy over the other as well since that season, with the 14-win Falcons beating Steve Young’s Niners in the Divisional Round in 1998 and Colin Kaepernick’s rendition of the squad coming back from a 17-point deficit to beat the Birds in the 2012 NFC Championship Game. When these teams met last It was just last season when the Falcons were coming off of a euphoric victory against the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football, going into a meeting with the 4-2 Niners on Sunday Night Football. Although San Francisco was battling a multitude of injuries (including to starting quarterback Brock Purdy), they were still finding ways to win. Those ways on this night were mostly on the defensive side, as the Falcons went into the half with only three points on the board and trailing by a score despite their own defense’s best efforts. Atlanta had something going on their second and third drives but one ended on a strip sack of Michael Penix and the other ended the half entirely when the panicked quarterback committed an intentional grounding while in field goal range which triggered a 10-second runoff. Despite the struggles, Atlanta came to within three points with a Bijan Robinson receiving touchdown in the third quarter but the offense was stonewalled after that, getting shut out the rest of the way. The crucial play of the game came on a 3rd and 13 from Atlanta’s 21-yard-line with just over two minutes left (with the score still 13-10). The Falcons lined up with just 10 men on the field and failed to cover Christian McCaffrey who got an easy 17 yards before scoring a touchdown on the next play. It was a frustrating night full of mental errors for the Falcons, which served as a big letdown following the high of the Bills victory.

summary: It’s been an up-and-down season for the Atlanta Falcons as they continue to evaluate the remains of the Terry Fontenot era. full_text: AUSTIN, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 19:Texas Longhorns offensive lineman #74 Trevor Goosby waves to fans on September 19, 2026 vs Ohio State in Austin, Texas. (Photo by The University of Texas Athletics/University Images via Getty Images) It’s been an up-and-down season for the Atlanta Falcons as they continue to evaluate the remains of the Terry Fontenot era. As we continue to figure out what the floor and ceiling are for this year’s iteration of the Falcons, I think now, as we approach a brutal five-game stretch, is a good time to figure out where the potential room for improvement can come from for the Falcons in this way-too-early 2027 NFL mock draft. Atlanta Falcons Projected Current 2027 Draft Picks Round 1, Pick 14 Round 2, Pick 45 Round 3, Pick 76 Round 4, Pick 110 Round 6, Pick 214 (Compensatory Pick – David Onyemata) Round 6, Pick 215 (Compensatory Pick – Tyler Allgeier) Round 1, Pick 14: Trevor Goosby, OT, Texas Height: 6’7” Weight: 325 The Ohio State pass rush wasn’t great… but Trevor Goosby and Melvin Siani are also EXTREMELY good Just 2 pressures allowed combined between them against in Texas’s huge win over the Buckeyes pic.twitter.com/YlyiAgstFV — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) September 15, 2026 One of the best-case scenarios in the 2027 NFL Draft is finding an answer at left tackle. Round 2, Pick 45: Nick Marsh, WR, Indiana Height: 6’3” Weight: 210 Nick Marsh is such a unique player So few players can run routes and create after the catch like he does at his size pic.twitter.com/4B35mXY5zK — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) October 10, 2026 There’s something about a wide receiver who is tall, but moves like a receiver that’s five to six inches shorter. That’s Indiana’s Nick Marsh. At 6’3”, 210 pounds, he has the body control and route-running ability of a slot receiver while possessing the body of a true X-receiver. That combination makes him a great option to become a serious vertical threat in this offense and allow Drake London and Kyle Pitts to work the underneath areas of the field. Round 3, Pick 76: Kingston Lopa, S, California Height: 6’5” Weight: 21 0 Kingston Lopa, S California 🟡🐻 Listed at 6’5 210 • Rare length and size at safety, ability to contest plays that others can’t • Great ball tracker + Great Range • Productive; 5 Interceptions and 1 PBU in 4 games • 41.7 Passer Rating When Targeted • Great in man coverage… — peyton (@pdubyaa) October 16, 2026 Everyone needs to understand how absurd it is that Kingston Lopa can move the way he moves at 6’5”, 210 pounds. Lopa is unlikely to sniff day two, let alone the third round, but the model had him fall here, and I won’t pass up a chance to heap praise on Lopa. He has erased his matchups in the passing game and is a more than capable filler in the run game. Where he ultimately lands will be a mystery, as this loaded draft class could easily see multiple first-round talents fall to day two. Round 4, Pick 110: Jalen Mayo, CB, Houston Height: 6’2” Weight: 190 Jalen Mayo has been one of the best CBs in the country this season for Houston. Allowing only 8 catches through the first 6 weeks of the season. Very sticky in coverage and his length allows him to cover ground quickly if the WR gets behind him pic.twitter.com/N5W1nbkypc — Jay (@DraftwithJay) October 13, 2026 Another guy who will not make it this far on draft day, but Jalen Mayo is another guy that I’m going to heap praise on whenever possible. Mayo is so sticky in coverage; with his insanely long arms, he can limit the space for the ball to reach the receiver. Add in Mayo’s speed and ability to recover, and he is an all-around corner who can change everything for a defense. Round 6, Pick 214: Coleton Price, C, Kentucky Height: 6’3” Weight: 308 Coleton Price finding work & clearing the pocket #slab pic.twitter.com/tQT1BHYU2v — Brandon Thorn (@BrandonThornNFL) September 22, 2026 Kentucky’s resurgence under Will Stein is mainly due to the new-look offensive line in Lexington. While Lance Heard gets all the attention on the outside, the big man in the middle, Coleton Price, has been absolutely stellar for the Wildcats. Price is a solid pass protector and a mover in the run game; I think plenty of tools are there to build around for Price. Round 6, Pick 215: DJ Lagway, QB, Baylor Height: 6’2” Weight: 225 DJ Lagway had the best game of his career in Tempe 25/40, 306 YDS, 4 TDS, 0 INT, 1 RUSH TD vs Arizona State A career-high four TD passes, plus an 11-yard score on the ground. Baylor's first win ever over Arizona State, and its fourth straight. pic.twitter.com/V5FcoPtnKE — CFB Performances (@performancesCFB) October 8, 2026 If the quarterback position were solely based on the physical tools needed for the position, Baylor’s DJ Lagway would be at the top of everybody’s list. However, his decision-making and refusal to allow a bad play to just be a bad play have made it impossible for Lagway to live up to the hype he once had as the number-one prospect in the 2024 recruiting class. Nonetheless, Lagway’s elite arm strength and athleticism in open space make him a worthwhile grab later into day three.

full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 05: Gervon Dexter Sr. #95 of the Atlanta Falcons exits the field after warmups prior to an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on October 5, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Gervon Dexter Sr. always had the tools to be a force in the NFL. His emergence in his second year in 2024 was eye-opening, from his explosive get-off to his violent hand usage overwhelming guards. His ability to crush the pocket was valuable to disrupt the rhythm of opposing passing games. Whether it was a bad scheme fit or falling out of favor with a new coaching staff, Dexter Sr. wasn’t as impactful in 2025. Ian Cunningham knew from his time in Chicago that he could add him to bolster the Falcons’ front. The new general manager capitalized on the opportunity to acquire Dexter Sr. in the summer. That move is proving shrewd, with Dexter joining Brandon Dorlus to form a powerful interior pass-rushing pairing. In an off-season filled with several impressive under-the-radar moves by the new regime, trading for Dexter Sr. is by far the best decision for fans. As the Falcons continue to adjust through difficult circumstances, they have to be excited about the future. A pass-rushing group of Dexter Sr. Dorlus, Jalon Walker, and James Pearce Jr. could be a nightmare for opposing fronts. Although the fanbase is understandably down about the team’s current direction after multiple tough defeats, there is genuine reason to be confident in the defense. This result is brought to you by FanDuel Sportsbook.

title: NFL predictions: Ravens need Trey Hendrickson revenge game vs. Bengals
summary: The Baltimore Ravens let a 10-0 lead slip away in Cleveland in Week 6. Their Tyler Huntley-led offense disappeared after a strong start, placing a hefty burden on a defense that just could not hold in the fourth quarter. In Week 7, the Ravens host the Cincinnati Bengals. Huntley will start once again with Lamar […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Trey Hendrickson #91 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts as he takes the field against the New Orleans Saints prior to an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens let a 10-0 lead slip away in Cleveland in Week 6. Their Tyler Huntley-led offense disappeared after a strong start, placing a hefty burden on a defense that just could not hold in the fourth quarter. In Week 7, the Ravens host the Cincinnati Bengals. Huntley will start once again with Lamar Jackson’s high ankle sprain sidelining him for a third straight contest. News of his absence shifted Baltimore to 2.5-point home underdogs (via FanDuel Sportsbook). Here’s how Jesse Minter’s squad can beat the odds and secure their fifth win of the season: Baltimore’s offense runs through The King The Bengals’ new-look run defense has some obscene splits in the run game. They have stuffed opposing rushers and allowed explosive runs at the highest rate in the league, per Next Gen Stats. They are also allowing 1.47 yards over expectation/attempt and 2.62 yards before contact/attempt, both league-highs by a considerable margin. The contrasts continue depending on the gap. Between the tackles, opposing rushers are averaging just 3.3 yards per carry as opposed to 6.0 to the outside. The middle is closed for business, almost entirely thanks to Dexter Lawrence. The offseason trade acquisition has been as advertised to start his Bengals tenure, dominating the trenches next to fellow veteran addition Jonathan Allen. If nose tackles eat space in the trenches, Lawrence is Joey Chestnut. There is no running around him, and there is certainly no running through him. Instead, Declan Doyle needs to embrace one of the NFL’s time-honored offensive strategies: run away from the defense’s best player. Derrick Henry still gets the edge better than any 6-foot-3, 252-pounder has any business, and attacking the outside will take pressure off Cam Jurgens in his first start as a Raven. Few players are as familiar with Lawrence’s abilities as the former Eagles center. He knows there is no beating Lawrence. There is no stopping his 6-foot-5, 350-pound frame. But he can be slowed by an agile center who can wall him off on outside zone runs and force him to chase plays laterally. Jurgens has to beat Lawrence to the spot and dig in long enough for Henry to get by. From there, The King can attack a Bengals secondary that has struggled to tackle this season. Ravens need a Trey Hendrickson revenge game On the defensive side of the ball, the Ravens need another one of the NFL’s time-honored traditions: a revenge game. Trey Hendrickson downplayed his first matchup against his former team this week, but one line from his Thursday presser stood out: “As a Christian, I forgive.” But did he forget? Hendrickson has openly expressed his frustration with the Bengals during their multiple contract standoffs. He finally has a chance to stick it to the team that backed up the Brinks truck for their top offensive players but could not reward the NFL’s sack leader across the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Hendrickson’s matchup with Bengals left tackle Orlando Brown Jr. will be most crucial on third downs – Baltimore’s mortal enemy on defense this year. The former Raven’s overall pass-blocking metrics hold up, but he collapses in true pass sets – Pro Football Focus’ metric measuring standard dropback passing plays. Brown has allowed 11 of his 12 pressures and all three of his sacks in true pass sets, which will typically come in those third-and-long situations the Ravens need to solve. But the Bengals have coaches, too, coaches who will use tight end Drew Sample and running backs Chase Browns and Samaje Perine to chip Hendrickson. The Ravens have two potential counters. The first is using the focus on Hendrickson to set picks and free up other rushers, potentially Nnamdi Madubuike or a second-level blitzer looping to the outside. Jesse Minter will also have at least one opportunity for a more extreme call – overload pressure on the right side with Hendrickson dropping into coverage. This has to be deployed in the right moment against the right offensive formation, but Burrow has proven he can be baited into interceptions before. Hendrickson just needs to get some tips from Marlon Humphrey on catching with a wrapped hand. Now, it’s your turn! Put on your coaching cap and tell us how you would scheme up a Ravens win against the Bengals?
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens rule out Lamar Jackson; Tyler Huntley to start vs. Bengals
summary: The Baltimore Ravens downgraded quarterback Lamar Jackson’s status from ‘questionable’ to ‘out’ ahead of their Week 7 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals. Backup Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley will make his third straight start after an overtime win over the Falcons and a disappointing loss to the Browns. Jackson’s comments on Friday, as well as his limited […]
full_text: Oct 11, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Baltimore Ravens quarterback Tyler Huntley (5) celebrates with quarterback Lamar Jackson (8) after a touchdown during overtime against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens downgraded quarterback Lamar Jackson’s status from ‘questionable’ to ‘out’ ahead of their Week 7 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals. Backup Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley will make his third straight start after an overtime win over the Falcons and a disappointing loss to the Browns. Jackson’s comments on Friday, as well as his limited practice participation all week, portended this outcome. He revealed that he suffered a high ankle sprain and was struggling to put weight on his left leg when running. He indicated that he did not need to be 100% to take the field, but emphasized that he would be doing a “disservice” to his team if he plays before his body is ready. Downgrading Jackson’s status is reminiscent of the lead-up to last year’s Week 8 matchup against the Bears. He suffered a hamstring injury three weeks prior and returned to practice with limited-limited-full participation days and a questionable designation on the injury report. However, Jackson did not speak to media that week, and the team only changed his status after reports emerged that he was not expected to play. This year, Jackson provided rare clarity regarding his injury, answering over a dozen questions about his status. Despite his multiple references to a “grace period” before making a decision, it was clear that he was not ready to play as of Friday. Rapid improvements in time for a Sunday afternoon kickoff were never likely. Saturday’s reports also characterized Jackson as a game-time decision. The differences from last year’s approach should ensure the Ravens avoid another league investigation that resulted in a $100,000 fine. At face value, it seems unclear why the Ravens had to update Jackson’s status on Saturday, especially if he is in that 50-50 range. Baltimore has let plenty of other players go through a pregame workout and announced their status via the inactive list 90 minutes before kickoff. It would actually benefit the team to force their opponents to prepare for Jackson to start and sit. But a two-time MVP moves betting lines, and the league is inextricably tied with sportsbooks. If Jackson is not playing, that information (from their perspective) has to be made public.

title: Ravens discussion: who will step up after Tavius Robinson’s injury?
summary: The Baltimore Ravens will be counting on their young outside linebacker depth to step up after Tavius Robinson’s season-ending pectoral injury. The fourth-year defender occupied a 72% defensive snap share to start the season (46.6 per game) while also contributing to the kick return, punt return, and field goal block teams. He leads the defense […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Zion Young #9 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts as he takes the field against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens will be counting on their young outside linebacker depth to step up after Tavius Robinson’s season-ending pectoral injury. The fourth-year defender occupied a 72% defensive snap share to start the season (46.6 per game) while also contributing to the kick return, punt return, and field goal block teams. He leads the defense with 3.5 sacks and the edge rusher room with 18 tackles, leaving a sizable void to be filled. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s take on replacing Robinson: Nikhil Mehta Rookies Zion Young and Ethan Burke have the physical profile to step up in Robinson’s absence, but more than anything, the Ravens need Mike Green to figure out how to rush the passer off the left side of the defense. He spent plenty of time there in college, but has lined up on the blind side more often in Baltimore with better splits. Based on his film, he’s still getting the feel for transitioning from his explosive first step into his pass rush moves. Green clearly has the athleticism and skillset to make it work, but he has to do so quickly. If not, Eric DeCosta may have to scour the trade market for another edge rusher who can win on third down. Zach Canter The Ravens have a big role to fill with Tavius Robinson going down for the season. T-Rob was an every down player, setting the edge, getting to the quarterback and capable of sliding inside with power. While Ethan Burke has done well in his limited action and more is expected to come, and Kaimon Rucker and Adisa Isaac could get snaps of the practice squad, the best answer is Zion Young. Young presents a very similar play style to Robinson, an excellent edge setter with grown-man NFL play strength to be able to slide inside. While he hasn’t shown the pass rush chops like Robinson, who has 3.5 sacks in 6 games, Young will be the first, next man up and get the biggest uptick in snaps. The real answer will be the Ravens trading for Khalil Mack, but we’ll have to see if the Ravens can play themselves into a spot to justify a move like that at the deadline. Dustin Cox The Ravens will need their second-round rookie, Zion Young, to step up and help to fill the role left behind by Tavius Robinson. Young’s profile is similar to Robinson’s, as both are power rushers who are strong run defenders on the edge. The rookie will likely have to take on a lot more snaps than originally envisioned, but throwing him into the deep end now could hopefully produce results for the talented linebacker sooner rather than later. Baltimore will likely need to add another body to the mix, whether that be via a practice squad call up, free agency, or through a trade before the deadline, but Young is the most obvious replacement on the current roster. Now, it’s your turn! Which Raven are you expecting to step up after Tavius Robinson’s injury? Let us know in the comments section below!

title: Buffalo Bills Week 6 game balls: Three standouts help Buffalo escape Las Vegas
summary: “We are never going to apologize for winning. It wasn’t pretty but our goal was 2-0. Our best football has to be ahead of us.” Those were the words of Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady following Sunday’s 33-30 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders. And he wasn’t wrong. The Bills walked away with another […]
full_text: “We are never going to apologize for winning. It wasn’t pretty but our goal was 2-0. Our best football has to be ahead of us.” Those were the words of Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady following Sunday’s 33-30 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders. And he wasn’t wrong. The Bills walked away with another victory, but it was hardly the convincing performance fans had hoped to see. Buffalo allowed 30 points and 378 total yards to a Raiders team that kept finding ways to stay in the game. Still, a win is a win, and after back-to-back road games, the Bills accomplished exactly what they set out to do. Three players received game balls for their performances: running back James Cook, linebacker Dorian Williams, and kicker Tyler Bass. James Cook: 153 total yards and a touchdown James Cook continues to demonstrate why he’s such an important part of Buffalo’s offense. Cook finished with 22 carries for 95 rushing yards and a touchdown, adding three receptions for 58 yards to bring his total to 153 yards from scrimmage. His three-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter helped Buffalo extend its lead, while his contributions in the passing game provided Josh Allen with another weapon when the offense needed to move the chains. Cook accounted for nearly half of Buffalo’s 358 total offensive yards. His message after receiving his game ball was simple: “Let’s Keep it Rolling.” Considering how much the Bills have relied on Cook to keep the offense moving, that’s a message fans can certainly get behind. Dorian Williams: A career milestone Linebacker Dorian Williams earned his game ball after recording the first interception of his NFL career. Williams finished with five combined tackles, an interception, and a pass defended. On a day when Buffalo’s defense struggled to contain the Raiders’ passing attack, Williams provided one of the game’s most important defensive plays. The Bills allowed Kirk Cousins to throw for 313 yards and two touchdowns, making Williams’ interception particularly valuable. It’s a career milestone worth celebrating and a performance that earned him recognition from his head coach. Tyler Bass: Perfect when Buffalo needed him If there was ever a game to appreciate the value of a reliable kicker, this was it. Tyler Bass was perfect against the Raiders, converting all four field-goal attempts and all three extra-point attempts. His field goals came from 44, 28, 47, and 38 yards, with his final kick coming in the fourth quarter. That’s 15 points from Bass in a game Buffalo ultimately won by just three. When an offense settles for field goals instead of touchdowns, the margin for error gets smaller. Bass made sure Buffalo didn’t leave any of those points on the field. Four field goals. Three extra points. Fifteen points. Honorable mentions Not everyone gets a game ball, but a few other performances deserve recognition in my opinion. Josh Allen: Allen completed 23 of 33 passes for 255 yards, two touchdowns, and no interceptions, finishing with a 112.6 passer rating. He connected with Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman for Buffalo’s two passing touchdowns. It wasn’t an explosive afternoon by Allen’s standards, but he protected the football and helped the Bills put 33 points on the board. Keon Coleman: Coleman caught four passes for 59 yards and a touchdown, averaging 14.8 yards per reception. His 12-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter helped Buffalo build a 23-13 lead. With DJ Moore inactive, Coleman stepped up as one of Allen’s primary receiving options. Cole Bishop: Bishop played all 66 defensive snaps and finished with seven combined tackles and two passes defended. While the defense had its share of struggles, Bishop remained one of the constants in Buffalo’s secondary. Denzel Igbinosun: Igbinosun recorded three passes defended, the most of any Bills defender, while playing 42 defensive snaps. His contributions in coverage deserve recognition, especially on a day when the Raiders threw the ball 41 times. Final thoughts There are certainly things the Bills need to clean up, particularly on defense. Giving up 30 points and allowing an opponent to remain in each and every game is gonna wear on this defense. And perhaps Brady’s postgame message says it best: The Bills aren’t going to apologize for winning. They shouldn’t have to. But their best football still needs to be ahead of them.
author: Sara Larson

title: Bills climb in Week 7 NFL Power Rankings, but which AFC contenders are for real?
summary: Buffalo enters its bye week ranked third in the NFL across eight major outlets. With six AFC teams in the national top 10, which contenders are trending in the right direction, and which have reasons for concern? The Buffalo Bills may not be winning pretty, but they’re winning. And apparently, that’s enough to keep them […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 18: Head coach Joe Brady of the Buffalo Bills speaks to Josh Allen #17 in the third quarter at Allegiant Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Bills defeated the Raiders 33-30. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images Buffalo enters its bye week ranked third in the NFL across eight major outlets. With six AFC teams in the national top 10, which contenders are trending in the right direction, and which have reasons for concern? The Buffalo Bills may not be winning pretty, but they’re winning. And apparently, that’s enough to keep them near the top of the NFL Power Rankings. Following a 33-30 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, Buffalo improved to 5-1 and enters its Week 7 bye ranked third overall in the consensus rankings from eight major national outlets. The Bills climbed from an average ranking of 4.25 in Week 6 to 3.88 in Week 7, despite continued concerns surrounding their defense. Six of the eight outlets rank Buffalo third, while CBS Sports places the Bills fourth. USA Today remains the outlier, dropping Buffalo two spots to ninth despite Sunday’s victory. The message from the national media seems fairly clear: Buffalo is one of the NFL’s best teams, but there’s still plenty of room for improvement. Buffalo Bills Week 7 Power Rankings The most notable jump comes from NFL.com, where Buffalo climbed three positions to third. Despite the Bills’ defensive struggles, NFL.com’s Nick Shook acknowledged that Josh Allen continues to overcome many of the team’s shortcomings. Pro Football Talk also moved Buffalo up one position, from fourth to third, although Mike Florio pointed directly to the defense as an area that still needs significant improvement. USA Today took the opposite approach, dropping the Bills to ninth after another narrow victory. Buffalo surrendered 30 points and 313 passing yards to Las Vegas, including two fourth-quarter touchdown passes. It’s difficult to argue with the defensive concerns. The Bills have allowed 30 or more points in four of their six games this season. But at 5-1, they’re still finding ways to win. How Buffalo stacks up against the AFC’s top six With Buffalo enjoying its bye week, we’re changing things up. Instead of comparing the Bills with their next opponent, we’re taking a closer look at the six highest-ranked teams in the AFC. Are these teams legitimate contenders, or are their records and rankings hiding some serious concerns? AFC Power Rankings: Eight-outlet consensus Rankings represent the average placement across ESPN, NFL.com, The Athletic, CBS Sports, USA Today, FOX Sports, Yahoo Sports, and Pro Football Talk. 1. Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) NFL consensus ranking: No. 2 | AFC ranking: No. 1 Trending up: Kansas City continues to look like the team to beat in the AFC. The Chiefs remained undefeated following a convincing 22-6 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers, holding their opponent to just six points. Kenneth Walker III has given the Chiefs another dangerous offensive weapon, including a 128-yard, two-touchdown rushing performance against Los Angeles. Trending down: The biggest question may be how Kansas City handles stronger competition. The Chiefs have some challenging games approaching, including matchups against Seattle and Denver. Those contests should offer a clearer picture of just how dominant this undefeated team really is. Are they for real? Absolutely. Until somebody knocks them off, Kansas City remains the standard in the AFC. 2. Buffalo Bills (5-1) NFL consensus ranking: No. 3 | AFC ranking: No. 2 Trending up: Buffalo’s offense continues to find ways to put points on the board. Josh Allen remains the driving force, while James Cook has become an increasingly important part of the offense. Cook finished Sunday’s game with 153 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown, helping Buffalo secure its second consecutive road victory. Trending down: The defense. There’s really no way around it. Buffalo has surrendered 30 or more points in four of six games, including 34 to the Rams and 30 to the Raiders over the last two weeks. The Bills continue to rely heavily on their offense to overcome defensive shortcomings, something that could become increasingly problematic against the AFC’s best teams. Are they for real? Yes, but with an asterisk. Buffalo has the quarterback and offensive production to compete with anyone. Whether the defense can improve enough to support a deep playoff run remains the biggest question heading into the bye. 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) NFL consensus ranking: No. 5 | AFC ranking: No. 3 Trending up: Jacksonville continues to show signs of being a legitimate AFC contender. Travis Hunter’s growing impact has given the Jaguars another dangerous playmaker, and their offense demonstrated its ability to compete in a high scoring game against Houston. Trending down: The Jaguars suffered a 34-31 loss to the Texans in London, their second defeat of the season. While Jacksonville remains firmly in the AFC’s upper tier, the inability to finish a close game raises questions about consistency. Are they for real? The talent is there. Jacksonville looks capable of competing with the AFC’s best, but the Jaguars need to prove they can consistently finish close games. 4. Denver Broncos (4-2) NFL consensus ranking: No. 6 | AFC ranking: No. 4 Trending up: Denver continues to gain respect around the league. The Broncos climbed in the consensus rankings after defeating Seattle 17-14, and their defense has helped keep them competitive against quality opponents. Trending down: Offensive consistency remains the concern. Denver managed just 17 points against Seattle, and the Broncos have struggled at times to generate enough production to complement their defense. In an AFC featuring explosive offenses in Kansas City and Buffalo, that could become a significant limitation. Are they for real? Defensively, yes. Denver has the ability to make life difficult for opponents, but its offense will ultimately determine whether the Broncos are true championship contenders. 5. New England Patriots (4-2) NFL consensus ranking: No. 8 | AFC ranking: No. 5 Trending up: New England is quietly becoming one of the more interesting teams in the conference. The Patriots improved to 4-2 following a 26-19 victory over the New York Jets and continued to climb in the national rankings. Are they for real? They’re certainly making a case for the most inconsistent team in the AFC. The Patriots have earned their place among the AFC’s top teams, but sustaining that success against stronger competition will determine whether they’re legitimate postseason threats. At the time of publication, the Patriots earned another question mark already having played week seven’s game. Their play Thursday night against the Chicago Bears was sloppy. They lost 30-24, and dropped them to 4-3, which undoubtedly means they will drop in next week’s rankings. Their official emergence within the AFC remains on hold. 6. Baltimore Ravens (4-2) NFL consensus ranking: No. 10 | AFC ranking: No. 6 Trending up: Baltimore still has the talent to compete with anyone in the conference. At 4-2, the Ravens remain firmly in the playoff conversation, and their defense limited Cleveland to just 13 points in Week 6. Trending down: The offense is struggling without Lamar Jackson. Baltimore managed only 10 points in its loss to Cleveland, and the Ravens have slipped in the national rankings as concerns about their offensive production continue to grow. Are they for real? That depends heavily on Jackson’s availability and the offense’s ability to rebound. Baltimore remains dangerous, but its current trajectory is less encouraging than that of several other AFC contenders. Could Houston be the team nobody sees coming? The Texans may not be among the AFC’s six highest-ranked teams, but they’re making a case that they shouldn’t be overlooked. Houston’s 34-31 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars in London was a statement,…
