title: Buffalo Bills snap counts vs. Raiders: What Week 6 playing time reveals
summary: The Buffalo Bills escaped Las Vegas with a 33-30 victory over the Raiders on Sunday, improving to 5-1 on the season. While the scoreboard tells one story, the snap counts reveal another, particularly when it comes to offensive personnel, defensive rotations, and the impact of injuries. Buffalo’s offense logged 68 snaps, while the defense was […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills escaped Las Vegas with a 33-30 victory over the Raiders on Sunday, improving to 5-1 on the season. While the scoreboard tells one story, the snap counts reveal another, particularly when it comes to offensive personnel, defensive rotations, and the impact of injuries. Buffalo’s offense logged 68 snaps, while the defense was on the field for 66. The Bills controlled possession for 31:48 compared to Las Vegas’ 28:12, but the Raiders still managed 378 total yards and 30 points. Let’s take a closer look at how the Bills distributed their playing time in Week 6. Offensive snap counts: Consistency up front, changing personnel elsewhere For another week, Buffalo’s offensive line remained the model of consistency. Dion Dawkins, Alec Anderson, Connor McGovern, O’Cyrus Torrence, and Spencer Brown each played all 68 offensive snaps, joining quarterback Josh Allen at 100%. With DJ Moore inactive, Keon Coleman led the wide receivers with 58 snaps (85%), followed by Khalil Shakir at 41 (60%). Skyler Bell saw a substantial workload with 30 snaps (44%), while Joshua Palmer played just 17 (25%). The tight ends continued to play a significant role in Buffalo’s offensive packages. Dalton Kincaid logged 49 snaps (72%), Dawson Knox played 47 (69%), and Jackson Hawes played 25 (37%). Keleki Latu added just five offensive snaps. Kincaid briefly exited with an injury during the second half before returning in the fourth quarter. In the backfield, James Cook played 45 snaps (66%), carrying the ball 22 times for 95 yards and a touchdown. He also added three receptions for 58 yards, giving him 153 yards from scrimmage. Ty Johnson played 12 snaps (18%), while Ray Davis contributed on nine (13%). Defensive snap counts: Bishop leads while the secondary adjusts Safety Cole Bishop was the only Bills defender to play every defensive snap, logging all 66 plays. Christian Benford followed with 64 snaps (97%), while Greg Rousseau and Terrel Bernard each played 53 (80%). The secondary saw considerable movement throughout the afternoon. Damar Hamlin played 45 snaps (68%), Dee Alford played 43 (65%), and Denzel Igbinosun contributed 42 snaps (64%). C.J. Gardner-Johnson finished with just 28 snaps (42%) after being ejected late in the second quarter. Along the defensive front, Deone Walker led the interior linemen with 45 snaps (68%). T.J. Parker played 41 (62%), while T.J Sanders played 30 (45%). Bradley Chubb played only 21 snaps (32%). The veteran briefly left the game with an injury but returned during the second quarter. Dorian Williams logged 37 snaps (56%) and recorded Buffalo’s lone interception, setting up a third-quarter touchdown that gave the Bills a 23-13 advantage. Special teams: The players carrying the workload Joe Andreessen led Buffalo’s special teams participation with 25 snaps (78%), followed closely by Sam Franklin with 24 (75%). Special teams also played an important role in the victory. Tyler Bass was perfect on four field-goal attempts and three extra points, accounting for 15 of Buffalo’s 33 points. Gabe Dortch returned three punts for 37 yards, including a 22-yard return, while Ray Davis averaged 28.3 yards on three kickoff returns. Final thoughts The Bills leave Las Vegas with another victory, but Week 6’s snap counts offer several interesting storylines moving forward. Offensive takeaway: Buffalo continued relying heavily on its starting offensive line and multiple-tight-end packages. Coleman’s 85% participation made him the clear leader among wide receivers, while Cook remained the primary option in the backfield. Defensive takeaway: The Bills’ defensive rotations deserve attention. Bishop handled the entire workload, while Gardner-Johnson’s disqualification and Chubb’s injury affected personnel usage. Despite limiting Las Vegas to just 65 rushing yards, Buffalo surrendered 313 passing yards and two fourth-quarter touchdowns. Special teams takeaway: Buffalo received significant contributions from its coverage and return units, while Bass delivered a perfect afternoon in a game decided by just three points. With Baltimore up next, the Bills will need the bye week to get healthy and build on their offensive consistency while finding answers for a defense that allowed Las Vegas to remain within striking distance until the final whistle.
author: Sara Larson

title: Introducing DIP: A new NFL defensive metric that accounts for quarterback competition
summary: What if we had a new way to determine defensive quality in the NFL that would adjust for opposing quarterback quality? It could provide a new answer on just how porous the Buffalo Bills defense really been through six games this season. Introducing: Defensive Impact on Passing (DIP) This new metric measures how every NFL […]
full_text: What if we had a new way to determine defensive quality in the NFL that would adjust for opposing quarterback quality? It could provide a new answer on just how porous the Buffalo Bills defense really been through six games this season. Introducing: Defensive Impact on Passing (DIP) This new metric measures how every NFL defense impacts quarterback performance relative to how those quarterbacks perform against the rest of their opponents. The idea with DIP is to provide a cleaner, more fair snapshot of each defense’s effectiveness by accounting for the quality of the collection of quarterbacks it has faced throughout the season. DIP adds vital context to EPA per dropback by calculating the difference in each quarterback’s performance against a specific defense compared to his baseline against other defenses. For example, if a defense plays an elite-level quarterback averaging +0.348 EPA per dropback and allows an EPA per dropback of +0.212, it would actually be viewed as a “successful” outing for that defense because it surrendered a lower EPA per dropback than what was expected from that quarterback entering the game. On the surface, allowing +0.212 EPA per dropback would be universally viewed as a bad outing for a defensive unit. But not with DIP. The opposite would be true if a defense allowed a “low” EPA per dropback of +0.08 against a quarterback who otherwise managed an EPA per dropback well into the negatives. And now that we’re six full weeks into the NFL season, somewhat of a baseline for each quarterback has been established, so we can measure how defenses are performing relative to expectation Because DIP is measuring EPA per dropback and not EPA per individual quarterback matchup when looking at defenses collective DIP throughout a season, the formula here is pretty simple: DIP = Total Actual EPA – Total Expected EPA / Total Qualifying Dropbacks Like all defensive EPA-based statistics, a lower (negative) number is better, and I’ve adjusted for garbage time, so the “qualifying” stipulation in the denominator equates to those dropbacks when the the win probability is between 10% and 90%. Although I decided on the name DIP, the calculation is per dropback, so scrambles and sacks are counted as well. When determining the quarterback EPA per dropback baseline for a defense, his performance against that specific defense was excluded. Also, for a quarterback’s baseline to be counted, he needed to have at least 30 total dropbacks against other defenses to date this season. Yes, a lot of explainers, I know. Kind of necessary for the introductory article. Oh, and lastly, before I show you chart through Week 6, like all defensive EPA statistics, a negative number is better: Some quick takeaways: Unsurprisingly, the Seahawks defense is still incredibly stingy. The Patriots defense has been sneaky good. Before their Week 7 game against the Bears, they were 14th in EPA per dropback allowed in non-garbage time but were in the No. 3 spot in DIP through Week 6. Strong showing for the Jaguars in DIP too, as they went from No. 17 in EPA per dropback rankings yet are seventh in this metric. Coordinator Anthony Campanille has done a fine job, and he has the horses, particularly in his front seven. The Panthers defense only has 64.2% of their defensive dropbacks faced actually counted in DIP because they faced Cooper Rush in Week 2, Shedeur Sanders for part of Week 3, and Tanner McKee in Week 6, and none of those quarterbacks have at least 30 dropbacks against other defenses to compare to. Philadelphia’s defense has been better than probably given credit for despite facing a relatively strong set of quarterbacks in its first six weeks of the season, including Jayden Daniels, Matthew Stafford, Trevor Lawrence, and Bryce Young. The Texans defense is still not to its 2025 level, but it’s playing better than the raw figures would suggest. Houston is 21st in DIP (as opposed to 26th in regular EPA per dropback). The most sizable discrepancy between regular EPA per dropback allowed and DIP belongs to the Saints. They’re 22nd in regular EPA per dropback and 9th in this new metric. Teams with a lower DIP than their actual EPA per dropback allowed through Week 6 include the 49ers (7th to 16th), Browns (5th to 15th), Ravens (11th to 19th), and Giants (12th to 17th). The Bills get a bump from 25th in EPA per dropback to 23rd in DIP. They have seen a rather daunting run of quarterbacks to begin the year including C.J. Stroud, Goff, Maye, Stafford and Kirk. And it’s not as if things are getting easier when Buffalo returns from its bye in Week 8 to welcome the Ravens to Orchard Park. While the end of November does feature a clash with Patrick Mahomes, they do have games against Malik Willis and Geno Smith sandwiched between those battles with former MVP quarterbacks.

title: Bills news: Previewing potential trade targets
summary: With the Buffalo Bills on their bye week, Brandon Beane, Joe Brady and the rest of the front office staff are using this time to review what has gone right, what has gone wrong, and how the team can improve if it wants to finally win the franchise’s first Super Bowl. The NFL’s trade deadline […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - OCTOBER 19: Amik Robertson #2 of the Washington Commanders looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the Buffalo Bills on their bye week, Brandon Beane, Joe Brady and the rest of the front office staff are using this time to review what has gone right, what has gone wrong, and how the team can improve if it wants to finally win the franchise’s first Super Bowl. The NFL’s trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Nov. 10, and with the offense scoring at a historic clip and the defense allowing almost every opponent to hang around, Beane and co. would be wise to explore every opportunity to bring in talent for the stretch run. New live chat feature during the games Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Today’s edition of Buffalo Rumblinks leads off by examining Buffalo’s positions of need and exploring the best available players who have been linked to the Bills, including Miami Dolphins talented off-ball linebacker Jordyn Brooks (pictured below), who carries a minimal cap hit this year and is under contract for 2027 at $13M guaranteed. Check out the news items below and then let us know your thoughts on who Brandon Beane should acquire before the trade deadline in the comments section. title: Discussion: Is Baker Mayfield’s return good or bad news for the Panthers?
summary: The Carolina Panthers have gotten some good quarterback so far this season. They faced Cooper Rush and the Atlanta Falcons in Week 2 and the Tanner McKee-led Eagles in Week 6. Both of those games were wins. For a while, it looked like the Panthers were going to be the beneficiary of another backup quarterback […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - JANUARY 03: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) scrambles for yardage during the Regular Season game between the Carolina Panthers and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on January 03, 2026 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Cliff Welch/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Carolina Panthers have gotten some good quarterback so far this season. They faced Cooper Rush and the Atlanta Falcons in Week 2 and the Tanner McKee-led Eagles in Week 6. Both of those games were wins. For a while, it looked like the Panthers were going to be the beneficiary of another backup quarterback situation. Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield left the team’s Week 3 game against the Vikings with a dislocated thumb. The most optimistic side of his recovery timeline had him back just in time for this game, and that’s where he ended up. In his absence, the Bucs turned to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels. While his personal production is somewhat muted, it’s a lot better than you’d typically expect for an undrafted rookie quarterback just a few weeks into his NFL career. He even led the Bucs to a win over the Cowboys, which remains their only win of the season. So that brings us to our question, is the return of Baker Mayfield good news or bad news for the Carolina Panthers? MY TAKE: At first glance, this seems like an obvious answer. Baker Mayfield has been a very good quarterback since he found a home in Tampa, and Daniels is an undrafted rookie. However, the circumstances make this a little bit murkier of a take. Daniels has a better QBR than Mayfield in their starts this season, and he’s a much more dynamic runner. Mayfield hasn’t played a game in nearly a month and is going to be taking his first live reps since he dislocated the thumb on his throwing hand. I’m not a quarterback, but I think throwing thumbs are important. All that said, I think Mayfield’s return is bad news for the Panthers. It’s not as bad as it maybe would have been if previous versions of Mayfield were playing, but I think there’s more that can go wrong from a Panthers perspective against him. We know how much he feeds off having a chip on his shoulder, and I think there’s only one team that he holds more ire towards than he does the Panthers. He could come out and flop given everything that’s going on, but I can’t fully trust that he’s not going to get revved up and do some nonsense to give the Panthers a hard time.

title: Chicago Bears Week 7 Flashbacks: A GW Drive, NFL History, and More!
summary: Even though the Bears beat the Patriots on Thursday night, this time machine has no brakes! We’re back with three more games from Week 7 from Chicago Bears history. Hop aboard and enjoy this trip on the Gridiron Time Machine! 1. 2007, Bears @ Eagles: Griese engineers a 97-yard miracle October 21, 2007 | Bears […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - OCTOBER 22: Eddie Jackson #39 of the Chicago Bears reacts after the Bears intercepted the football in the fourth quarter against the Carolina Panthers at Soldier Field on October 22, 2017 in Chicago, Illinois. The Chicago Bears defeated the Carolina Panthers 17-3. (Photo by Wesley Hitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Even though the Bears beat the Patriots on Thursday night, this time machine has no brakes! We’re back with three more games from Week 7 from Chicago Bears history. Hop aboard and enjoy this trip on the Gridiron Time Machine! 1. 2007, Bears @ Eagles: Griese engineers a 97-yard miracle October 21, 2007 | Bears win 19-16 The defending NFC champions had stumbled to a 2-4 start in 2007, and things weren’t looking particularly promising in Philadelphia. Chicago’s offense struggled to find the end zone for most of the afternoon, relying on four Robbie Gould field goals to keep pace with the Eagles. When Donovan McNabb connected with Matt Schobel for a touchdown late in the fourth quarter, Philadelphia took a 16-12 lead. The Bears eventually got the football back at their own three-yard line with 1:57 remaining, no timeouts, and needing a touchdown. Enter Brian Griese. With communication problems affecting his helmet headset, Griese called his own plays and marched Chicago 97 yards down the field. He connected with Bernard Berrian and Devin Hester on crucial completions before finding Muhsin Muhammad for a 15-yard touchdown with nine seconds remaining. Griese finished with 322 passing yards and a touchdown, while Muhammad caught five passes for 79 yards. Chicago escaped with a 19-16 victory, improving to 3-4 and keeping its postseason hopes alive. 2. 2017, Bears vs. Panthers: Eddie Jackson makes NFL history October 22, 2017 | Bears win 17-3 Sometimes the defense doesn’t just help win a football game. Sometimes it scores every touchdown. That was the case when Carolina visited Soldier Field in Week 7 of the 2017 season. Rookie safety Eddie Jackson wasted little time announcing himself. On this day in 2017, Eddie Jackson made history with a 75-yard fumble return TD and 76-yard pick six against the Panthers pic.twitter.com/ygZZgVv838 — Depressed Bears Fan (@ImBearsFan) October 22, 2025 On Carolina’s opening possession, Jackson scooped up a loose football and raced 75 yards for a touchdown. Early in the second quarter, he intercepted a deflected Cam Newton pass and returned it 76 yards for another score. Just like that, Jackson had scored 14 points by himself. He became the first player in NFL history to record two defensive touchdowns of at least 75 yards in the same game. The Bears defense finished with three takeaways and five sacks, holding Carolina to just three points despite being outgained 293-153. Perhaps the most ridiculous statistic from the afternoon belonged to Chicago’s offense. Mitchell Trubisky completed just four passes for 107 yards, while the Bears managed only five first downs. None of it mattered. Chicago walked away with a 17-3 victory, improving to 3-4 and recording consecutive wins for the first time since 2015. 3. 2022, Bears @ Patriots: Chicago spoils Belichick’s historic opportunity October 24, 2022 | Bears win 33-14 This one seems particularly appropriate with New England visiting Soldier Field Thursday night. The Bears entered their Week 7 Monday Night Football matchup in 2022 riding a three-game losing streak. Meanwhile, Patriots coach Bill Belichick was sitting on 324 career victories, including the postseason, tied with Bears legend George Halas for second-most in NFL history. A victory against Chicago would move Belichick past Papa Bear himself, but the Bears had other ideas. Justin Fields had a solid game, completing 13-of-21 passes for 179 yards and a touchdown while rushing for another 82 yards and a score. Throwback to the last time the Bears beat the Patriots, which coincidentally happened in Week 7. pic.twitter.com/bOclQcaeKV — 𝕲𝖗𝖎𝖒 𝕮𝖚𝖙𝖙𝖞 (モナンがい 𝕾𝖟𝖓) (@iamcogs) October 22, 2026 Chicago jumped out to a 10-0 lead before New England turned to backup quarterback Bailey Zappe, who briefly sparked the Patriots offense and gave them a 14-10 advantage. That was the last time New England would score. The Bears rattled off 23 unanswered points, rushing for 243 yards while forcing four turnovers, one of which forced by Spider-Man himself, rookie Kyler Gordon. Fields led the way on the ground, while David Montgomery and Khalil Herbert each contributed 62 rushing yards. Cairo Santos added four field goals as Chicago cruised to a 33-14 victory. The win was Chicago’s first in Foxborough and prevented Belichick from passing Halas in front of the franchise he helped build. Gary Baugher Jr. is a second year contributor to WCG, bringing football insight backed by over 16 years of experience in organized football and more than 30 years as a passionate fan of the game. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs .

full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals will travel to Baltimore on Sunday this week, looking to improve to 4-2 on the season. On Saturday, their eyes should be on some talented prospects across college football. While there are not a ton of top matchups like there were last week, it should still be another exciting week across the country. Some of the top games this week include Texas vs. Ole Miss, Kentucky vs. Vanderbilt, and Utah vs. Houston. Let’s take a look at a few prospects that the Bengals could be scouting this week. Lance Heard, LT, Kentucky Heard transferred from Tennessee to Kentucky ahead of the 2026 season. The former five-star recruit has really taken a step forward in his development this season. The talent was always there, but he was so inconsistent the past couple of years for the Volunteers. This year he has been the definition of consistency. He has allowed just 8 total pressures in 7 games played. The 6’6”, 325-pound left tackle has an 85.7 pass-blocking grade so far this season. He has a ton of experience playing tackle in the SEC. He has over 2,200 career snaps played already. The Bengals gave Orlando Brown Jr. a two-year contract extension this offseason. His play has been up and down for most of the season, but he did play his best game of the year against the Dolphins. While left tackle might not ultimately be the biggest need come draft day, it should still be in consideration for Cincinnati. Brown will be turning 31 years old in May, and the dead money cap hit would only be $4.6 million dollars if they decide to let Brown go after the 2027 season. Continuing to make sure that Joe Burrow is well protected should always be a priority. Lance Heard (#53) is reaching his potential after transferring to Kentucky from Tennessee. The former 5-star recruit has great pop in his hands, good arm length, a finishing mentality, and fires off the snap in the run game. He has been playing like a 1st round prospect this… pic.twitter.com/gywFeM9Gs9 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 18, 2026 Zereoue Williams, LT, Utah I will stick with another talented left tackle prospect for the second player of note. Zereoue Williams had to wait his turn behind first-rounders Spencer Fano and Caleb Lomu at Utah. That move is paying off for him this season. He has come out of nowhere to put himself firmly in the mix to be drafted in the first round. Williams has ideal size at 6’8” and 315 pounds for an offensive tackle. His basketball background shows up consistently with how light he is on his feet. Williams has allowed just 3 pressures through 6 games played for Utah this season. Williams didn’t play football from seventh grade until his senior season. The inexperience is certainly there since this is also his first full-time starting season at Utah. Instead of looking at that as purely a negative, I see a player with tremendous upside still. With what he is putting on tape already, this is a player that might have All-Pro potential at the next level. full_text: (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images For some teams, the Saturday roster moves are a strong indication of what will happen with their questionable players on Sunday. Cleveland Browns fans are hoping that is true, with CB Denzel Ward and LB Quincy Williams being added to the injury repor t the last two days, but only one practice squad elevation on Saturday. For Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans on the road , the Browns did activate RB Dylan Sampson off of injured reserve on Saturday. HC Todd Monken had expected his backup, pass-game savant back would return this week, and now that is official as Cleveland removed his questionable status as well. S Grant Delpit also cleared concussion protocol and has no injury status for this week’s game versus the Titans. To make room on the Browns roster, the team placed OL Teven Jenkins on injured reserve after he missed the first six games of the season and was already ruled out for Week 7. With Ward and Williams still questionable, it was notable that Cleveland only elevated DT Sam Kamara , his third and final such elevation, and not another defender in case one of the starters is unable to go. For their part, Tennessee signed DT Timmy Horne to their active roster and elevated RB Kalel Mullings and WR KJ Osborne , which could be a sign that RB Tyjae Spears and WR Calvin Ridley might miss this week’s matchup. Good news for Sampson and Delpit, and seemingly good news for Ward and Williams. Not a bad Saturday news drop. We still will not have official word on Ward or Williams until the inactive reports come out 90 minutes before kickoff on Sunday. Which of the four good or potentially good news pieces do you think will be the biggest in Week 7 for the Browns?

title: Browns: Is the 2027 QB plan going up in flames?
summary: The Cleveland Browns entered the 2026 regular season with a sound plan in place to fix the quarterback position. Get through the season as best they can, clean out all (or at least most) of the current quarterback room after the season, then head into the 2027 NFL Draft armed with a pair of first-round […]
full_text: (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns entered the 2026 regular season with a sound plan in place to fix the quarterback position. Get through the season as best they can, clean out all (or at least most) of the current quarterback room after the season, then head into the 2027 NFL Draft armed with a pair of first-round selections to draft the next presumed franchise quarterback. It appears, however, that Deshaun Watson never got the memo. Despite being mostly bad at the things teams generally need their quarterbacks to be good at, Watson and the offense have been good enough when it counted to pull off fourth-quarter game-winning drives in all four of Cleveland’s wins this season. That is the highest total through six games for a Cleveland quarterback since Baker Mayfield did it during his rookie season in 2018. That, along with a defense that continually exerts its will and a special teams unit that has been solid, has the Browns sitting in first place in the AFC North Division heading into Sunday’s game against the Tennessee Titans. It has also opened up the possibility of doing what was once unthinkable, which is signing Watson to a new contract after the season. At least that is the speculation from The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones , who caught up this week with owner Jimmy Haslam at the NFL league meetings. The Browns are 4-2 and atop the AFC North. Now, they have a question few expected to be asking this season: Could Deshaun Watson play his way into more years in Cleveland? Read more on what @jjones9 is hearing, for free: https://t.co/F4TEyoY23d pic.twitter.com/vqJFkmWL0W — The Athletic (@TheAthletic) October 24, 2026 And while Haslam said there is still a lot of football to be played, he admitted he likes what he has seen so far: “That’s way premature to talk about (a new contract). We’re just focused on beating the (Tennessee) Titans. People have to respect the way that he’s battled back from the injuries. And then you look at the game-winning drives. We’ve got to be able to keep that up.” While a clean break after five years of turmoil would seem to be in everyone’s best interest, an unnamed league source pointed out that the Browns could be Watson’s only option if he still wants to be a starting quarterback: “The door is wide open for him to be with the Browns. It’s the only line on a starting quarterback job he’ll have. And even if you are in position to take one high (in the draft), or get in position to do so, you’re in no rush to play the rookie.” Cleveland being Watson’s only option is a bit debatable, as the NFL is still a league where teams are desperate for quarterback play. But there is always going to be the question of Watson’s off-field issues; even if he truly left those in Houston, a new team would have to weigh them into the equation when deciding if Watson is worth it or not. Let’s take a step back for a moment. The season is only six games long, so any talk about a new contract for Watson is incredibly premature. Even if the Browns were pondering the idea of a new contract for Watson, it would be one of the most stunning moments in league history if they did anything without letting the season play out. The key takeaway is that the Browns are in first place and playing meaningful games as we near the end of October. Any talk about the quarterback position for 2027 can take a backseat for now. full_text: As the Cleveland Browns get ready to travel to Nashville to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season, the top of the AFC North continues to belong to the orange and brown . Injuries, including DT Mike Hall Jr. being out this week , continue to be a big variable for the Browns and their opponents . All the positivity heading into Week 7 wasn’t as strong if we look back to when Hall, along with DT Mason Graham , were injured in Week 4 versus the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football. Graham is expected to return in Week 7 after getting injured early in Week 4 and being ruled out after halftime. Just before the intermission, Hall injured his ankle, was helped off the field, and then carted into the locker room. Cleveland (and Pittsburgh) fans know what happened next for the former Ohio State defensive lineman: The Browns defense pick up their 4th sack of the night! @PITvsCLE on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/IGODY4j1OS — NFL (@NFL) October 2, 2026 Hall later said he knew his teammates needed him with Graham out for the game. From being carted off the field to exploding for a huge third-down sack that pushed the Steelers out of field goal range, Hall’s impact was appreciated after a game where the score (27-24) might have been decided, partially, by his return and big sack. Since that game, Hall is set to miss his third straight contest. While that may be frustrating to some Browns fans, it also puts his Week 4 return into context. Running off of adrenaline and knowing what his teammates needed, Hall not only returned to the field but made a huge impact, while dealing with an ankle injury that will have needed a month off, at least, between games played. Three weeks later, it is clear that Hall’s ankle injury was and is significant. That adds even more respect to his Week 4 return and play. Join the conversation! title: NFL Week 7: 3 other games for Browns fans to keep an eye on
summary: The Cleveland Browns face off against the Tennessee Titans in Week 7 of the NFL season, with a win moving the visitors to 5-2 and a loss calling their early-season success into question. Injuries mean that any Saturday news from the Browns will be analyzed and scrutinized, including whether RB Dylan Sampson is activated from […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns face off against the Tennessee Titans in Week 7 of the NFL season, with a win moving the visitors to 5-2 and a loss calling their early-season success into question . Injuries mean that any Saturday news from the Browns will be analyzed and scrutinized, including whether RB Dylan Sampson is activated from injured reserve. The bigger questions will be about practice squad elevations on defense, with CB Denzel Ward and LB Quincy Williams questionable for the game . With Cleveland sitting at the top of the AFC North and fourth in the AFC playoff picture , there are a couple of games of importance going on around the league that they’ll want to watch. Two of the teams ahead of them in the playoff seeding, the Buffalo Bills (2nd seed) and Jacksonville Jaguars (3rd seed), have their byes this week, which limits the games of interest. With the Los Angeles Rams owing the Browns their first-round pick in the 2027 NFL draft, “Rams Watch” is on every week, especially with injuries piling up and WR Puka Nacua questionable for Week 7 . With two AFC North teams facing off this week, that leaves just three vital games for Cleveland fans, besides their own, to watch in Week 7: Steelers vs. Saints in Paris, early Sunday kickoff The first game on Sunday, kicking off at 9:30 AM on NFL Network, is important for Browns fans for two reasons. First and obvious, the Pittsburgh Steelers are part of the AFC North and are tied for the best record in the division. Second, the Steelers and New Orleans Saints are Cleveland’s next two opponents . The result of the game will be important, but watching to see how Pittsburgh’s energy is and any injuries coming during an international game could be a big deal for Week 8’s AFC North matchup. Last year, the Browns traveled to London the week before having to face the Steelers and looked lethargic after the long travel. The only difference this year is that Paris is a little further away than London, and Pittsburgh gets to play at home the next week, whereas Cleveland had to go on the road. Bengals vs. Ravens at 1 PM At the same time the Browns are playing, a pretty big matchup between the Cincinnati Bengals and Baltimore Ravens will be going on. The Bengals are in last place in the AFC North, at 3-2, and go on the road to face the Ravens, who should be getting QB Lamar Jackson back . Too early in the season for tiebreaker conversations; instead, fans will be rooting for a very physical game on the field. Ramvs vs. Raiders at 4:25 PM Los Angeles could have Nacua playing this week, but his injury flaring up during practice calls that into question, along with the team having to go on the road. DE Myles Garrett could start practicing soon, but will have at least a week or two before he’s likely to play once he begins that process. A loss in Week 7 would drop the Rams to 2-5 and potentially lead to Los Angeles selling heading into the NFL trade deadline. Given some of the matchups this week, the Rams could be slotted to send the Browns a Top 8 pick by the time this week’s slate of games is over. Given that the Jaguars and Bills are on byes this week, a Cleveland win would slide them up to the third seed for now (5-2 gets the nod over JAX at 4-2). Checking in on the Steelers and Saints while getting your breakfast and game-day spread will have you more prepared for the Browns Week 8 and 9 matchups, while “OctoBox” users on YouTube will probably want to have Bengals vs. Ravens available at 1 PM as well. The chance for Los Angeles to lose again and have their season continue to head in a negative direction would just be icing on the cake for Cleveland fans in Week 7. So we wanted to know just how deep the criticism went. Was it just that he needs to shape up? Or was it that […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images | Getty Images You have chosen. All week, there has been plenty of chatter about the job being done by Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer. That chatter has been of the negative variety. So we wanted to know just how deep the criticism went. Was it just that he needs to shape up? Or was it that he needs to ship out? Ship out carried the day. When asked what they would do if they were Jerry Jones concerning Schottenheimer, 68% of Cowboys fans said they would fire him. Things have turned quickly for Schottenheimer, who was just this past offseason being lauded for his offense and his handling of the team. His rookie season wasn’t a success when using wins and losses as a measure, but most wrote it off to the abysmal defense. Now, things have changed. Schottenheimer has been under heavy scrutiny for his offensive consistency and his in-game decisions. Given history, it’s unlikely Jerry Jones will fire him in-season, but a majority of fans have, if only in spirit. Brian Schottenheimer needs a win in the worst way against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night, now as a 4.5-point favorite. Bonus question: If Schottenheimer was fired, who would be your ideal coach to replace him? We also did a confidence poll, and only 6% were confident the team was headed in the right direction. Things are getting ugly. For your NFL odds, head over to FanDuel.

title: Cowboys at Eagles: Matchups to watch in Week 7
summary: Anyway you choose to look at it, this Week 7 matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles is a must-win game for the Dallas Cowboys, and one that will play a heavy hand in how Jerry Jones and Company decides to approach the rest of the season. The NFC East division title as well as their playoff […]
full_text: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Anyway you choose to look at it, this Week 7 matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles is a must-win game for the Dallas Cowboys, and one that will play a heavy hand in how Jerry Jones and Company decides to approach the rest of the season. The NFC East division title as well as their playoff hopes could all hinge on the outcome of this single game. With both teams sitting in 2-4, this is a matchup that looks pretty even on paper. Both teams have fallen way below expectations this year and have been dealing with injuries to key players. The one that never grates around this issue the past should walk away with the “W”, but to do so they’ll have to win certain matchups this week. Below are the ones we’ll watching. RB Javonte Williams vs. Eagles run defense A lot of the Cowboys struggles on the offensive side of the ball can be linked to their ineffectiveness in the running game. They’re currently ranked 31 st in the league through six weeks, averaging only 76 yards per game. A lot of that has to do with them being forced to abandon the running game due to the fact they’ve been playing from behind nearly every game. That could change this week against the Eagles 19 th ranked run defense. If Dallas can get Williams going on the ground, it opens up everything else and makes things much easier. DT Kenny Clark vs. Eagles C Drew Kendall Kenny Clark going up against the Eagles new center Drew Kendall is a matchup that should favor the Cowboys. The former 2025 fifth-round pick out of Boston College has taken over the full-time starting job after Cam Jurgens was traded to the Baltimore Ravens and only has a total of four starts under his belt so far in his young career. His inexperience is something Clark can take advantage of, both as a run defender and pass rusher. No. 95 has a chance to be a true difference maker this week and could help sway the game in Dallas’ favor. Cowboys secondary vs. Eagles QB Tanner McGee With Saquon Barkley expected to return this week after missing two games with a hamstring injury, the Cowboys defensive game plan will revolve heavily around containing him and putting the game in QB Tanner McGee’s hands. McGee will be making his second start this season after Jalen Hurts was put on IR with blood clots and will be looking to the next QB to victimize Dallas’ struggling secondary. Joey Porter Jr. has improved things, but it’s not enough. Everyone around him needs to step up their game and reinforcements could also help.

title: Cowboys draft: College football targets for Week 8
summary: Hopefully the Cowboys can win over the Eagles and keep us from talking about the draft too much in the coming weeks. Still, it’s never too early to scope out some talent while you are watching college football this Saturday. Ole Miss vs Texas Ole Miss has rebounded from its only loss by dominating consecutive […]
full_text: Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images | Getty Images Hopefully the Cowboys can win over the Eagles and keep us from talking about the draft too much in the coming weeks. Still, it’s never too early to scope out some talent while you are watching college football this Saturday. Ole Miss vs Texas Ole Miss has rebounded from its only loss by dominating consecutive SEC opponents, while Texas has fallen from number one to 19th after back-to-back defeats and poor quarterback play. The Longhorns now need to protect Arch Manning against an active Ole Miss front and prove their own offensive line can regain control of a game. Ole Miss: Blake Purchase, edge rusher Purchase transferred from Oregon to Ole Miss looking for a larger role, and the move has allowed him to turn athletic promise into more consistent production. So far, Purchase has recorded 23 tackles, 6.5 tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks and 2 forced fumbles this season. Those are not dominant numbers, but they show a player becoming more disruptive as his responsibilities grow. His first step is his best tool. Purchase anticipates the snap well and can threaten the outside shoulder before an offensive tackle settles into his pass set. He understands how to reduce the surface area available to a blocker, dips underneath contact and accelerates toward the quarterback once he clears the edge. That speed also appears when he chases running plays from the back side. Purchase offers more against the run than his size might suggest. He plays with good effort and keeps moving after initial contact. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas has already invested in its edge group, but it has not received enough consistent production from it. Rashan Gary produced a strong pressure total against Green Bay, but he hasn’t been consistent. Von Miller is a short-term veteran, while Donovan Ezeiruaku and Malachi Lawrence are still developing. The Cowboys need more young rushers rather than assuming one player will solve the problem. Purchase would give Christian Parker another movable pressure piece. He could initially play on passing downs, contribute on special teams and attack from different alignments while he adds strength. His closing speed would be useful in a defense that wants to create confusion before the snap and force quarterbacks to hold the ball. Texas: Brandon Baker, offensive lineman Baker arrived at Texas as the top offensive tackle in the 2024 recruiting class. He started at right tackle in 2025, did not allow a sack and improved steadily after a difficult opening assignment against Ohio State. Texas moved him to right guard this season, giving evaluators evidence that he can handle multiple positions. The 6-foot-4, 315-pound junior plays with balance and controlled feet. At tackle, Baker showed enough lateral movement to stay connected against speed rushers. Moving inside has allowed him to use his natural strength more often. He generates movement on double teams, keeps a wide base against power and has the mobility to work into space on pulls and screens. Why The Cowboys Care The Cowboys have solid starters across much of the offensive line, but the unit has not been consistently reliable. Terence Steele remains a big question around the long-term conversation at right tackle. Dallas cannot allow one injury or one poor matchup to shrink the entire offensive plan. Baker would provide several solutions. He could backup the guard position and offer emergency tackle depth. His experience at both spots would allow Dallas to dress fewer offensive linemen on game day without leaving itself exposed. If the club eventually changed its tackle alignment, Baker could help it move pieces without creating another immediate hole. Houston vs Utah Utah is 6-0 and owns the longest active winning streak in the FBS. Houston is 6-1, has won four straight and is playing ranked opponents in consecutive regular-season games for the first time since 1977. The matchup places Houston’s explosive passing game against one of the country’s most efficient defenses, while Utah running back Wayshawn Parker faces a Cougars unit allowing fewer than 100 rushing yards per game. Houston: Amare Thomas, wide receiver Thomas has produced at every stop of his college career. After two productive seasons at UAB, he transferred to Houston and immediately became the Cougars’ leading receiver. He caught 67 passes for 966 yards and 12 touchdowns in 2025, including six scores of at least 20 yards. He is coming off seven receptions for 126 yards and two touchdowns against Oklahoma State and now has six touchdown catches this season. The 6-foot, 200-pound senior wins through detail rather than rare physical traits. Thomas changes pace during routes and uses leverage and sharp route breaks to create separation. He understands how to settle into open areas against zone coverage and works back toward the quarterback instead of waiting for the football to reach him. Why The Cowboys Care Thomas would offer a different skill set from CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. He could play inside or outside, give Dak Prescott a reliable answer against pressure and turn quick throws into useful gains. His route awareness would also help an offense whose combinations have not consistently placed receivers in positions that suit them this season. His lack of top-end speed should keep him in the Day 3 conversation. That makes him the type of affordable receiver Dallas could add without forcing the pick. Thomas would have to earn snaps on special teams, but his production and polished route running give him a chance to outperform his draft position. Utah: Wayshawn Parker, running back Parker has become the engine of Utah’s balanced offense. He’s rushed 89 times for 597 yards and seven touchdowns through six games, averaging 6.7 yards per carry. He posted consecutive games of more than 170 rushing yards against Iowa State and Kansas, and he enters the Houston matchup with 2,313 career rushing yards. His running style is built on vision and sudden changes of direction. Parker presses the line patiently to force linebackers into declaring their gaps, and then accelerates through the crease. His low center of gravity helps him bounce off arm tackles, while his lateral quickness lets him redirect without losing all of his speed. Why The Cowboys Care Running back depth is easy to overlook when a starter like Javonte Williams is quietly productive, but Williams shouldn’t be asked to carry the entire backfield again next year. Parker currently projects as an early Day 3 or late Day 2 option. That is an appropriate price for Dallas to build a more dependable rotation without diverting its limited selections from the offensive line and defense. Parker could fill that role. His vision and compact running style would translate to the Cowboys’ inside and outside-zone concepts, while his open-field movement would add an explosive element behind Williams. If his receiving and pass-protection skills develop, he could eventually handle complete drives rather than entering only for designed carries.

title: Breaking down the numbers: Cowboys at Eagles preview
summary: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the Cowboys travel to Lincoln Financial on Monday Night Football to take on the Philadelphia Eagles. Cowboys […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the Cowboys travel to Lincoln Financial on Monday Night Football to take on the Philadelphia Eagles. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott threw for 258 yards on an astonishing 54 attempts. He’d finish the game with a 65.2 passer rating. Javonte Williams rushed the ball just 11 times against Green Bay for 41 yards. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens combined for 15 receptions on 29 targets, racking up 143 receiving yards Brevyn Spann-Ford split time with Jake Ferguson at a near 50/50 rate. The second-year tight end continues to improve his stock this season. The defense didn’t force a third-down stop until the near the six-minute mark in the second quarter. They tightened up in the second half, allowing just two third-down conversions and a total of 83 yards. Eagles key stats from last week The Eagles offense gained a total of 222 yards last week in their loss against the Panthers. Just 35 of those yards came on the ground from the beat up Philadelphia rushing attack. Tanner McKee threw the ball 45 times, finishing with a 77.5 passer rating. The leading receivers for the Eagles were DeVonta Smith ( seven receptions, 75 yards) and Dallas Goedert ( six receptions, 61 yards). Stay grounded This game could come down to which team’s rushing attack is the most successful. Last week, Javonte Williams and the run game had a few moments, but Dallas got away from it far too early. Coach Brian Schottenheimer has been under scrutiny this week for completely abandoning the run game, a tendency we’ve seen often throughout his career in Dallas. This week, it’ll be imperative to run a balanced offense against an Eagles defense that has struggled, but isn’t void of talent. On the Eagles side, it looks like Saquon Barkley has a good shot at returning to the lineup this week. This offense will not want Tanner McKee to throw the ball over 40 times again if it can be avoided. The Eagles offensive line has struggled to get much going for any of their running backs this season. But Dallas has also had their share of problems in limiting opponent’s rushing attacks. The formula is clear for Philadelphia, but can they execute? What do the numbers mean? This week, we’ve got two underperforming NFC East teams in a primetime Monday night matchup. The Eagles offense has struggled this season, even before the unfortunate Jalen Hurts health situation. The Cowboys have been mostly healthy on offense, but have lacked the killer instinct situationally while also no-showing the last two weeks. So which team has a better shot at putting up points and securing the win? As bad as Dallas has been the last two weeks, this offense still features two of the league’s scariest targets on the outside. They still have a top 10 quarterback who, at times, elevates himself into top five territory. The offensive line still features several All-Pro and Pro Bowl players. Make no mistake, they are dangerous and can go off any given week. This week, if coach Schottenheimer can return to a balanced offensive attack, the Cowboys will take home the win. The Eagles simply do not have the firepower to keep up, even against a struggling Dallas defense. And if Prescott and the offense can jump out to an early lead, this could get ugly for Philadelphia. The Cowboys have not put a holistically decent product on the field, especially the last two weeks. They have certainly been bad. But the Eagles have been just as bad, if not worse, and are now without their franchise quarterback. Tanner McKee is a stationary target without a good offensive line. They lack adequate talent at wide receiver, outside of DeVonta Smith. If the Cowboys defense ever had a moment to show up and get right, this would be a great time. If the Cowboys can stifle the biggest threat on the field in Barkely, this should be a long day for the Eagles backup quarterback. Everything points to Dallas winning, which of course should scare the pants off Cowboys fans. We saw a similar situation against a backup quarterback in Tampa Bay in week five. But records aside, that Buccaneers team is better than Philadelphia. They possess more offensive weapons, they have a mobile quarterback, and Todd Bowles put together a defensive gameplan that exposed a fatal weakness. The Eagles defensive scheme is vastly different and won’t crowd the line of scrimmage throughout the game. This plays to the Cowboys favor. Dallas has done very little to earn or trust this season. But if they can head up to Lincoln Financial and simply do their jobs against a beat up and beaten down Eagles team, this game should finish with a convincing Cowboys win.

title: Cowboys news: Dak Prescott explains why establishing the run is so important
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are averaging less than 80 yards a game running the football, and they need to get it going somehow against a tough Philadelphia Eagles defense. Mike Pettine provides a ton of experience to the Cowboys, and they hope it spreads throughout the entire coaching staff. It’s been struggle for the Cowboys’ offense […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are averaging less than 80 yards a game running the football, and they need to get it going somehow against a tough Philadelphia Eagles defense. Mike Pettine provides a ton of experience to the Cowboys, and they hope it spreads throughout the entire coaching staff. It’s been struggle for the Cowboys’ offense handling pressure over the last two games, but correcting won’t be difficult according to Dak Prescott. Also, Dallas continues to get good news when it comes to injuries. Dak Prescott details how finding rhythm in run game can help spark Cowboys offense – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys running game has taken a step back from last season. Dak Prescott dives into the importance of finding it again going forward. If Dallas can get the run game going, then it sets up an area Prescott is confident in and one he’s been at the best at over the course of his career: Play action, which can also get the Cowboys’ offense back to hitting more explosive plays. “From there, you get your play action, your passes,” Prescott said. “If you look at those numbers, I can guarantee you more than half of those were run action type plays and explosives. From there, a lot of things can open up.” Cowboys leaning on Mike Pettine as sounding board for Christian Parker, coaching staff – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News Mike Pettine will spend most of his time watching film on the Cowboys and their opponents. The goal is to help Christian Parker and the other coaches as well. Pettine started working Wednesday of last week. He said his first few days were like drinking water from a fire hose. By Sunday, he was in the coaches’ box in Green Bay helping Parker and the Cowboys defense. Parker reflected on when the two coached together in Green Bay, starting in 2019. Parker was in the coaches’ box back then, operating as Pettine’s “eyes in the sky.” The roles were reversed Sunday. “He’s the same for me during the game,” Parker said. Will Cowboys Brian Schottenheimer give up play-calling? Here’s his answer – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram Dallas has seen their offense hit a rough patch lately. Despite this, Brian Schottenheimer is certain he can get them back on track with him as the play caller. “No, absolutely not,” Schottenheimer said. “I have incredible confidence in our offense. We have not played well the last two weeks, we have addressed a lot of the reasons why. We haven’t changed who we are. We are still a good explosive offense with weapons. We can hurt you a lot of different ways. I certainly haven’t lost the ability to call plays. I’m an elite play-caller in this league, and it can change around quickly.” The Cowboys have played poorly vs. the blitz the past 2 weeks. What’s the problem? – Jon Machota, The Athletic Dak Prescott has been kown for being excellent against the blitz. With that not being the case lately, some serious questions need to be answered. “I just have to simplify the plan,” Prescott said after Sunday night’s 23-13 loss at Green Bay . “That starts with me and really it ends with me. You give yourself a few options on a blitz and you get in the game and you want to do this one, want to do that one, and I just have to be more simple and more direct in exactly what I want to do. I don’t want to get too into it and tell my answers, but it is definitely fixable.” Cowboys Injury Report: Dallas Getting Much-Needed Defensive Reinforcements – Randy Gurzi, SI.com Dallas hasn’t had the best luck on the injury front this season. Thankfully, their defense is set to get some key guys back on Monday night. Injuries have been a major concern for the Dallas Cowboys this season, especially on the defensive side of the ball. That’s been frustrating for a unit that was struggling to start the season, and things only got worse when their most talented players were put on the shelf. There has been some good news this week, however, with players such as linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and cornerback Cobie Durant trending toward a return when Dallas plays the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football in Week 7.

title: Most fans believe Sean Payton has trust in his QB
summary: Despite a somewhat fortunate win by the Broncos more than a week ago, a majority of fans are feeling good about the direction of the team AND that the head coach has full trust in his quarterback. And in our two polls this week, the magic number was 63%. But when it comes to confidence […]
full_text: Despite a somewhat fortunate win by the Broncos more than a week ago, a majority of fans are feeling good about the direction of the team AND that the head coach has full trust in his quarterback. And in our two polls this week , the magic number was 63%. But when it comes to confidence in the direction of the team versus belief that Sean Payton trusts Bo Nix, one 63% majority seems better than the other. I am much more comfortable with a roughly two-thirds’ majority being confident in the direction of the team. It’s such a broad question, and there’s no telling what reasons the 37% minority has for not being too confident — and that seems pretty fair right now. But when that big of a minority doesn’t think the head coach trusts his QB, that 37% looms a little larger. Personally, I don’t think it’s a matter of Sean Payton not trusting Bo Nix to fulfill his potential as the franchise quarterback he drafted him to become. But it does seem like he’s not sure of , yet so Payton becomes more conservative with his play calling at times. “I have to play better. We have to play better. The offense has to play better. …I feel like I can overcome some of the stuff that is putting us in a bad spot, and I feel like I can play better.” Bo Nix The problem is, when he doesn’t show that necessary level of trust in Nix, Payton is holding back the entire offense — and there’s no reason to do that. Yet when asked if he was ever thinking about benching Nix, Payton gave that question the kind of emphatic answer it needed and dismissive tone it deserved: “To answer your question, no.” No, because that would be insane. Nix hasn’t played well consistently these first six weeks of the season, but he knows it, and he’s working on it. “I have to play better. We have to play better. The offense has to play better,” Nix said. “[Coach] is going to take his [blame] and that’s what great leaders do. I feel like I can overcome some of the stuff that is putting us in a bad spot, and I feel like I can play better.”

title: Sean Payton is focused on keeping the Broncos locked in every week
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! There’s a tendency in sports to throw out the “trap game.” Where a team looks past the current opponent to one coming in the following game or week. For the Denver Broncos, if there was a time for that to happen, it could be this week. The Broncos (4-2) just got […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks on in front of offensive coordinator Davis Webb of the Denver Broncos against the Seattle Seahawks during the first quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! There’s a tendency in sports to throw out the “trap game.” Where a team looks past the current opponent to one coming in the following game or week. For the Denver Broncos, if there was a time for that to happen, it could be this week. The Broncos (4-2) just got out of the six-game gauntlet to start the regular season and now face the Arizona Cardinals. The notion goes that the Broncos perhaps don’t take Arizona (2-4) as seriously as they should, since they play the Kansas City Chiefs the following week. Denver head coach Sean Payton isn’t buying that, as he said to the media on Friday: “The first thing I thought about was, ‘Who do we play next week?’ It has to be. I’m trying to not be cliché. It has to be the focus. You come back after the weekend, and you’re like, ‘All right, we have a three-game stretch. Here it is. Here’s Arizona. Let’s focus on Arizona.’ These guys are smart enough that they understand enough of our league. “These guys (Arizona) just came off a real impressive win against the Rams. When you have the schedule like we do in the NFL with 17 games, I couldn’t tell you after the bye. I have no clue. I know where we’re going at some point; I just don’t know when.” Payton then expanded on the key to not overlooking an opponent. “I think a little bit gets back to who you’re bringing in the building,” he said to the media. “The makeup and the guys that are smart. They understand how this league works. So that experience, that makeup certainly helps me when we’re focusing on this game.” What helps a veteran coach like Payton is knowing the type of message to deliver to his team. And that changes each week. “You learn to understand what’s important and then what’s not important,” Payton said. “When you’re a young coach, you’re talking about everything, and when you talk about everything, pretty soon you’re not really covering anything because you’ve hit everything. What you learn, maybe with a little bit of experience, is what to ignore, even with your team, as you prepare. “But very in touch to the challenges today, and the challenges within each week. I would say I think about that race all the time. What’s going to be this week’s theme? All of that. Probably too much sometimes, but your mind races relative to what’s necessary for this win.” Broncos links

title: Ultimate Fan: Time for Denver to dial up an aggressive offense
summary: It seems like a long time ago we were reading a UFG and watching the Broncos (because 10 days is an eternity in an NFL season!) but we are back and ready to see this team kick it into another gear after some time off and a slightly easier opponent. Kingbronco58 is back to show […]
full_text: Sep 27, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Los Angeles Rams during the second half at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It seems like a long time ago we were reading a UFG and watching the Broncos (because 10 days is an eternity in an NFL season!) but we are back and ready to see this team kick it into another gear after some time off and a slightly easier opponent. Kingbronco58 is back to show us how the Broncos’ offense can take charge for four quarters (looking at you, Payton), what Nix needs to do, and how the defense can continue to make life miserable for opponents. Kingbronco58 is one of our younger fans (who I met at a Broncos Raiders game years ago!) who joined the flock in the McDaniels era, which I always have to point out because it’s a little amazing he stuck around! But I’m so glad he did, and his Broncos Mount Rushmore is a testament to his fandom (now if he’ll just go watch those old Elway games too!!) "I’m confident in myself. I know I’m going to get back and be exactly what I was, if not better because as I’ve got older, that’s how it’s been. My training is going like this (points up) and at the end of the day, it’s all about getting better” —Bo Nix https://t.co/1KyOrDZ4UT — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) October 23, 2026 Week 7: Broncos at Cardinals MHR – It’s been a while since the OT win over the Seahawks. Quick thoughts on that second-half collapse, but OT save for the W? Kingbronco58: I think the second half collapse just speaks to the second half adjustments made by Mike McDonald and a talented Seahawks defense. With the way the game started, I thought we were finally about to see the offense put together a complete game. Hopefully this week, we finally get to see it come together. But at the end of the day we escaped a gauntlet of six games with a 4-2 record, and I think most would have been happy with 3-3 before the season. MHR – Ironically, this question was from last year’s Week 7 game… but it’s sadly appropriate again this season! The “offense struggles, defense saves the day” is a common theme. How frustrating is it that by Week 7 Bo Nix and the offense are still (and once again) mostly relying on the defense to “get” the win? Or should we be cool with having such a strong defense? Kingbronco58: It’s definitely frustrating that we are seeing it again, especially when we added Waddle in the offseason thinking he’d help the offense take the next step. I personally think this is still largely tied to Bo not mentally over the hurdle of his playoff injury. Theres been a ton of chatter on Twitter about how the Broncos need to move on from Bo after two years of slow starts. We’ve seen Bo go toe to toe with some of the best QBs in the league after starting slow. I’d rather see him peak in the playoffs when it matters than disappear when it matters. Having a strong defense that can carry when the offense is finding its footing is a luxury many teams would love to have, so I don’t see any reason that wouldn’t be cool. MHR – The Broncos offense also falls into a familiar pattern – very few yards on 1st and 2nd down, creating 3rd and long which always brings a lot of pressure and usually leads to a three-an-out. In general terms, what is holding this team back? Or is it just playing really good defenses? Kingbronco58: I feel like the offense struggling has been for a variety of reasons. We generally do a poor job challenging the middle of the field on the passing game. Wide receivers drop too many balls. No one consistently gets open. Dobbins has looked awful to start the season and the run game has been inefficient. And our play calling lacks creativity. Do all of these need to be fixed before the offense gets back on track? I don’t think so. But we need to see improvements in a lot of areas, playing really good defenses obviously doesn’t help when we are already struggling. But for the second year in a row we see the offense show up in plenty of games in the second half. MHR – Will we ever see the Jaylen Waddle we were promised? Kingbronco58: I really hope so, I can’t tell where the disconnect is with Waddle. But having traded a first round pick for him, his performance thus far is disappointing as fan and as a fantasy football owner. MHR – Bo Nix has acknowledged he needs to play better, and Sean Payton has taken some responsibility for the offensive struggles. Are you concerned about Nix’s performance overall? Any worry about the long-term projection for Nix as the franchise QB? Kingbronco58: I’m a little concerned, but we saw this last year as well. I feel like he’s playing not to lose instead playing to win while also struggling to overcome the mental aspects of his injury. He still has shown some flashes, like the Jacksonville game, and even the second half of the Rams game. I’m not rushing to make any decisions on Nix as the franchise QB yet. The reality is we are just now in year 3. We have the 5th year option and a franchise tag before we are absolutely locked into Nix as the franchise guy. A year ago Texans fans were having the same conversation, asking if Stroud was done after having a down year. And Stroud has really bounced back this year, so lets not rush into trying to draft another QB because Nix has struggled so far this year. For what its worth, I still Bo-lieve. This is for you, @Broncos fans: Evan Williams says his former Oregon teammate Bo Nix will be back STRONGER THAN EVER 💪 @evan_williams32 | @heykayadams pic.twitter.com/mfDXYlRHwG — Up & Adams (@UpAndAdamsShow) October 23, 2026 MHR – The Cardinals’ defense has struggled overall, but Budda Baker remains one of the league’s most versatile defensive backs, recording 42 tackles, 3.5 sacks and an interception this season. If he ends up playing, how concerned are you that Baker will be a big disrupter for an already inconsistent offense? And even if he’s out, how do you think the offense will handle Arizona’s tendency to disguise its defensive looks? Kingbronco58: I guess to an extent I’m not that worried about a specific guy or disguised defenses. I’m sure this response will come back to bite me. The Broncos have already played some really good defenses, including teams that have coordinators that like to disguise defensive looks. I think this is the easiest matchup of the season so far; if the offense struggles again I don’t think they deserve any excuses. MHR – The Broncos’ running game has struggled to establish much consistency, but Arizona has been one of the league’s worst teams defending the run. Is this finally the week Denver gets its ground game going? And which running back do you think should and could carry the load? If Jonah Coleman is back, does that change anything? Kingbronco58: I don’t think the run game gets going this week unless the Broncos have a big lead. The O-line hasn’t been consistent opening up holes in the run game this season. I want to see Harvey get more carries. We all know that he’s extremely good in the passing game, but not getting him carries telegraphs what the offense is going to do. I think Dobbins carries the load again this week, but it wouldn’t surprise me if Coleman becomes the guy as we get later into the season. I expect Coleman to play this week but after a month off, I don’t see a drastic improvement in the run game as he will be eased into playing time. MHR – This is game three with Sean Payton calling plays. Do you think the switch was a good choice? How would you grade his play-calling the last two games? What would you like to see improved and what specifically do you think should be Payton’s emphasis this week when it comes to passing plays, run/pass balance, creativity, etc.? title: Future Broncos: Thoughts on Denver being trade deadline buyers
summary: Broncos Country, apologies for last Saturday’s hiatus from Future Broncos. I was on a long drive and trip after Denver’s big win against the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football. We will get back in the swing talking prospects soon. For this installment, I wanted to discuss some potential pre-trade deadline moves that have been […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 14: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts runs the ball during the NFL 2025 game between Denver Broncos and Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 14, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Broncos Country, apologies for last Saturday’s hiatus from Future Broncos . I was on a long drive and trip after Denver’s big win against the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football . We will get back in the swing talking prospects soon. For this installment, I wanted to discuss some potential pre-trade deadline moves that have been floated and whether or not the Broncos should be interested. It’s something we haven’t covered here yet, so I thought this would be a wise time to do so with the deadline just a few weeks away. With the Colts starting off the season 2-4, their front office made a bold move and decided to fire long-time General Manager Chris Ballard. That has caused quite a stir across the media waves with many well-respected analysts believing that Indianapolis could be big sellers prior to the deadline. The two major players often discussed are running back Jonathan Taylor and left guard Quenton Nelson. First and foremost, there are no doubt these two are tremendous players. Secondly, I think it’s safe to say Denver could use a boost at the running back position since J.K. Dobbins has struggled, Jonah Coleman has been hurt, and RJ Harvey hasn’t had a lot of carries or reps in his second season. However, some reports have suggested the Colts are looking to recoup their first-round pick they gave up to the New York Jets to acquire cornerback Sauce Gardener. If that’s the price tag, there is no way the Broncos should be interested. It’s not just the draft capital that matters—it’s the fact Taylor has a massive two-year contract thereafter Denver would have to absorb. Yes, the Broncos are scheduled to receive a fourth-round compensatory pick for John Franklin-Myers. Moreover, will have an additional seventh-round selection from the New Orleans Saints to finalize the Devaughn Vele trade. That’s extra Day 3 capital which will be nice, but let’s be real. The Broncos aren’t in a position to trade away another top draft selection—especially for an aging running back. That’s happened three of the last five years due to acquiring Jaylen Waddle, Head Coach Sean Payton, and Russell Wilson with a total of four first-round picks involved. The truth is, Denver has a lot of long-term and future needs to address. It doesn’t seem wise to toss away a top pick on a short-term and expensive rental at running back. With respect to Nelson, he is in the final year of his contract with the Colts. He’s an All-Pro player and one of the best offensive linemen in the NFL. He would certainly be an upgrade over Ben Powers who has had an up and down tenure with Denver. Though I’d imagine his price-tag will also be high. It would also come under the condition the acquiring team would offer him one of the largest contracts at the position. You can’t just trade off premium draft capital for a half a season rental. And honestly, the Broncos already have one of the highest paid offensive lines in football. It’s truly an area where they need to get younger and start saving money against the cap. Another player that has been floated potentially is Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta. I’m not so sure the Lions are even remotely interested in trading him off. He has been a productive player for them, but the nagging injury history is a concern. They are still in the thick of it in a tight NFC North battle, so I don’t even think he is a realistic option for Denver. Acquiring him would also mean finding a way to extend him since he is in the last year of his rookie contract. I guess I’m not certain he would be much of a needle mover. How quickly could he even pick up Payton’s offense and find a way to be a meaningful contributor? Would he even be a frequent target on offense? How quickly would he get chemistry with Bo Nix? Quite frankly, I’d rather see Denver invest a top pick to address their big need there than attempt to go this route. All things considered, I just don’t see the Broncos being huge buyers before the deadline. I could be very wrong about this. It’s fair to say they should be aggressive because these moves may line up with the idea of maximizing their Super Bowl window. Though if they don’t pan out, it would also be at the expense of drafting and building for the future—which they’ve done far too often over the past few seasons. I’m curious to know what you all think. Should the Broncos be buyers? What type of draft capital would you be willing to give up in the event these players were really on the market before the deadline?

title: Broncos vs. Cardinals: 3 Players to Watch in Week 7
summary: For their Week 7 matchup, the Denver Broncos trek south to take on the Arizona Cardinals. The Broncos have fared well thus far going 4-2 against a tough gauntlet of opponents. In order to achieve their fifth victory of the season, these three players need to show up and make an impact against the Cardinals. […]
full_text: Aug 21, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos defensive end Zach Allen (99) before the preseason game against the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For their Week 7 matchup, the Denver Broncos trek south to take on the Arizona Cardinals. The Broncos have fared well thus far going 4-2 against a tough gauntlet of opponents. In order to achieve their fifth victory of the season, these three players need to show up and make an impact against the Cardinals. Zach Allen — Defensive Lineman Sunday’s matchup will be bittersweet for Zach Allen. It’s a return back to where he started his NFL career. He spent four seasons with the Cardinals having the privelege to learn under J.J. Watt and was coached up by Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph. Flash forward to the present day and Allen has cemented himself as one of the best interior defensive lineman in the National Football League. The eighth year pro is coming off back-to-back All-Pro seasons. Through six games, the former third-round pick out of Boston College is putting up another incredible season . He already has 4.5 sacks, 31 tackles, and 16 quarterback hits. Finding a way to pressure and rattle Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett will be a huge key to the game. I have a feeling Allen will be playing with a little bit more intensity and fire going up against the team that drafted him all those years ago. I have no doubt he is going to have an impact and help lead the Broncos to a big win. Jonathon Cooper — Edge Rusher After spending the first six games on the NFL Commissioner’s Exempt List, Jonathon Cooper is scheduled to make his 2026 regular season debut against the Cardinals. With Jonah Elliss sidelined with an injury suffered against the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football , the Broncos will need the sixth-year edge rusher to hit the ground running and make an impact versus the Cardinals. The past three seasons, Cooper has been one of the most underrated edge rushers in the NFL. He posted at least eight sacks a season from 2023-2025, averaged over 15 quarterback hits a year, and has been a strong defender against the run. His presence in the starting lineup should help Denver’s defense be even more formidable. J.K. Dobbins — Running Back A lot of fans across Broncos Country were hoping for Denver to make a big splash this off-season to add more juice to their running back group. Instead, the Broncos brought back J.K. Dobbins on a two-year deal. He showed a lot of promise early on last season, but missed most of the second half of the season due to injury. In six games, Dobbins hasn’t made much of an impact for Denver. Quite honestly, he looks like he may have hit a cliff. He has just 270 yards on 81 carries with two touchdowns. Outside of a few runs of ten yards or more, he is really struggling to get quality yardage and sports a paltry 3.3 yard per carry average. The Cardinals have a bottom ten run defense in the NFL. They’ve allowed at least 140 yards or more in three contests. If there was any game for Dobbins and the Broncos’ rushing attack to finally make a mark, this one would be it. In the event that doesn’t happen, I’m not sure what Denver should do. More carries to RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman make sense, but perhaps General Manager George Paton might need to get on the phone and inquire about adding a back before the trade deadline. With Chris Ballard out in Indianapolis, perhaps Paton can ask about what it would take to get Jonathan Taylor? Probably too much, but a strong running game will be essential for Denver to be contenders this season.

title: The Broncos aren’t overlooking the Cardinals
