full_text: Nate Landman went on the injury report this week and now he’s officially out. It’s another blow to the Rams who seem to have their 2026 season falling apart. As the injuries and losses mount up, how can this team stay positive? A win on Sunday would go a long way, but with all the injuries, a win may be a long shot. Puka Nacua’s status is up in the air. It was no sure thing that the Rams would play the playoffs this year, but it seems very likely, and now? It seems like a stretch as L.A. seems more likely to fall to 2-5 than 3-4. Injury Report, Week 7 at Raiders: Puka Nacua and Trent McDuffie questionable, Nate Landman ruled out (therams) “Nacua left Thursday’s practice early with the aforementioned calf injury. Head coach Sean McVay on Friday said Nacua “took part in a majority of the practice, left, (and then) got it checked out.” McVay also said that “I don’t think he (Nacua) knows exactly when it occurred.” However, McVay did characterize the injury as “minor.” “You look at it, and there’s just a little minor thing in there, and felt it where he wasn’t able to have some of the power and full explosion, and just kind of noticed it,” McVay said. “But I don’t think he was aware of any sort of specific play that led to it.” Cornerback Trent McDuffie (groin) is also listed as questionable. McDuffie did not practice all week. Meanwhile, inside linebacker Nate Landman (concussion) was ruled out, but is “making good progress,” McVay said. With Landman out, McVay confirmed Los Angeles will elevate inside linebacker Eric Kendricks from the practice squad.“ Puka Nacua, Trent McDuffie questionable, Nate Landman ruled out for Week 7 (nbcsports) “McDuffie has registered seven passes defensed with an interception. The Rams will be without linebacker Nate Landman (concussion) on Sunday, as he’s been ruled out. The team will elevate veteran linebacker Eric Kendricks from the practice squad to play in the game.“ Latest updates on Rams WR Puka Nacua’s calf injury (ramswire) “Already without Davante Adams for the next 6-10 weeks , losing Nacua for any amount of time will be a huge blow to the Rams offense. Terrance Ferguson is also on IR with an ankle injury, while the defense has lost plenty of playmakers, too. We’ll be providing the latest updates on Nacua’s status below.“ Raiders vs. Rams Betting Pick: Back the Home Underdog (sp0rtsgrid) “The 2-4 Los Angeles Rams visit a Las Vegas Raiders team that has been a bettor’s delight. title: Maxx Crosby, Tyler Linderbaum among Raiders that must step up in Week 7
summary: A get-right game for the Las Vegas Raiders? These types don’t come often for the Silver & Black but that’s what the Week 7 home date with the Los Angeles Rams is shaping up to be. Pegged as a “super team”, the visiting Rams have been anything but that. Sean McVay’s squad is 2-4 overall […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images A get-right game for the Las Vegas Raiders? These types don’t come often for the Silver & Black but that’s what the Week 7 home date with the Los Angeles Rams is shaping up to be. Pegged as a “super team”, the visiting Rams have been anything but that. Sean McVay’s squad is 2-4 overall and riding a two-game losing skid which began with a Week 5 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills. That was followed by an 18-16 defeat to the Arizona Cardinals last Sunday. And now the offensive genius that McVay is contends with a roster decimated by injuries. L.A. will be limping into this matchup having lost key contributors in Week 6 to injury, such as wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring), defensive tackles Kobie Turner (groin) and Poona Ford (ruptured triceps), and kicker Blake Grupe (torn ACL). In addition to that, the Rams will be without standout linebacker Nate Landman (concussion) in their outing in Las Vegas. Full #Rams injuries from Week 6: – WR Davante Adams – ruptured hamstring, out 6-10 weeks – DT Kobie Turner – groin, out 4-6 weeks – DT Poona Ford – ruptured triceps, out for season – K Blake Grupe – torn ACL, out for season Also: Myles Garrett isn't ready to come back and is… pic.twitter.com/wJFSAU46qu — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 19, 2026 It’s a perfect storm of a get-right opportunity for the 3-3 Raiders to get back in the win column as their galivanting on a three-game losing streak. And in order to rid themselves of consecutive losses and take advantage of a silver nugget in front of them, Klint Kubiak’s desert marauders need elevated play from certain players: Such as edge rusher Maxx Crosby and center Tyler Linderbaum. Football often begins and ends in the trenches and both represent elite talent at their respective positions on Las Vegas defensive and offensive lines. It’s almost blasphemy to say Crosby needs to step up considering his uncanny stamina and will but not even that non-stop motor or sheer determination is lighting up the stat sheet like it used to. The 29-year-old 6-foot-5 and 255-pound edge rusher is off to the slowest start of his career when it comes to finishing plays behind the line of scrimmage. Crosby remains a harrier for quarterbacks and is among league leaders in pressures through the first six games, however, he only has two sacks on the year and also only two tackles for loss. At this current rate, the Raiders elite pass rusher is on pace to rack up just five sacks (his career low was seven in his second season in the NFL in 2020) and five to seven tackles for loss (career low was 13 in 2021). These are two categories where Crosby tends to go ham in the box score. Maxx volume 🔊 Don't miss an all-new Mic'd Up with Maxx Crosby LIVE NOW! 📺: https://t.co/bddAGwCPtg pic.twitter.com/6JKTB3uWcN — Las Vegas Raiders (@Raiders) October 22, 2026 Not only pressuring but hitting or taking down Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford is a must-do this Sunday for the Raiders and it’s Crosby who leads that charge. According to Pro Football Reference, Crosby is charted with 24 pressures, 11 hurries, and 10 hits on the quarterback. Those pressure numbers are impressive considering PFR charted Crosby with 29 total pressures last season — one in which he had 10 sacks. Crosby hasn’t received much help from his fellow defensive linemen in the sack department, however. And elevated play from defensive tackles Adam Butler, Folorunso Fatukasi, and the returning Tonka Hemingway (concussion) will be tremendous for getting interior pressure on Stafford — whose arm powers the Rams top-ranked and second-ranked passing game in terms of attempts and yards gained. Flip the trenches to the offensive side of the ball, Las Vegas needs improved play at the pivot from Linderbaum. The high-priced free agent acquisition was rag dolled by Buffalo Bills defensive tackle Deone Walker in last week’s matchup and the Raiders can ill-afford to have that happen anymore. Getting manhandled at the point of attack hurt Las Vegas run game and offensive line as a whole, but Linderbaum appears ready to showcase Week 6’s performance was the outlier. And this brings us to the ground game — the aspect of the Raiders offense that continues to struggle despite the concentrated effort the team has done to improve upon it. “Yeah, I think the common theme is myself. We got to be better as coaches at getting our guys in the best situation, and just keep improving. And that starts on the practice field,” Kubiak said during his media session on Friday. “So, this time of year, when guys start getting a little bit dinged up, some of the reps go down a little bit, so just being really intentional about what reps you give them versus what fronts, so we can give them a good picture of what to expect in the game.” Tyler Linderbaum talks about the team's response this week as the #Raiders look to improve the run game against the LA Rams on Sunday pic.twitter.com/fymaeO4yPk — Raider Nation Radio (@RNR920AM) October 22, 2026 Improved execution by the front five on the offensive line and quick decision-making by running backs Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr. is integral if Las Vegas intends to topple Los Angeles. While the Raiders run game may boast the third-worst group in the NFL (475 yards rushing), the Rams run defense allows seventh most rushing yards (762). Facing a Rams team without two key defensive tackles and the stud linebacker should help the Silver & Black, too. “Yeah, guys, we just got to go do it. Got to quit talking about it, and we got to go do it,” Kubiak said when asked how close his team is to finding a groove running the ball. Even with a struggling ground game, Kubiak and veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins lead the NFL’s seventh-most productive aerial attack (1,581 yards) and Las Vegas has the second-most passing touchdowns (14) in the league. Cousins is completing 63.4 percent of his passes with a league-leading 14 touchdowns (and just five interceptions). He’s only been sacked eight times and if the offensive line and ground game are clicking, it should further open up the array of artillery Kubiak dials up. Heightened effort and execution form tight end Brock Bowers and speedy wide receiver Tre Tucker can make the Raiders top two pass catchers (28 receptions, 382 yards, three touchdowns and 24 receptions, 371 yards, three touchdowns, respectively) even more dangerous in this home clash with the Rams.

title: Raiders Mailbag: What players should Las Vegas target at NFL Trade Deadline?
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are gearing up for what feels like a “must-win” game in Week 7 against the hobbled Los Angeles Rams. However, the NFL Trade Deadline is quickly approaching (Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 1 p.m. PST), and that’s the biggest focus of this week’s mailbag. So, let’s get to it! Q: What players […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are gearing up for what feels like a “must-win” game in Week 7 against the hobbled Los Angeles Rams . However, the NFL Trade Deadline is quickly approaching (Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 1 p.m. PST), and that’s the biggest focus of this week’s mailbag. So, let’s get to it! Q: What players would be good options for the Raiders’ timeline to buy at the trade deadline? A: Understandably, I got a bunch of questions about Quenton Nelson, so I’ll dive into my thoughts on him in the question/answer below and focus on other players here, all of whom come from The Athletic’s big board . Shout out to Daniel Popper for putting that together! DT Jeffery Simmons, Tennessee Titans Normally, I wouldn’t be in favor of trading for someone who will turn 30 in the summer. But 2025 was Simmons’ best season, and he’s been playing well this year, so it’s not as if he’s showing signs of regressing. Also, he signed an extension in the offseason and would be under team control through 2030. The issue with Simmons to the Raiders is that he was arrested for violence against a woman, and Mark Davis typically draws the line there. However, the incident occurred when Simmons was still in high school and was over a decade ago, and he hasn’t been in any legal trouble since then. DT Moro Ojomo, Philadelphia Eagles Ojomo is an impending free agent, so trading for him would also require a contract extension. The other end of that is that John Spytek could wait until the offseason and just sign Ojomo in free agency without having to give up a draft pick for him. So, it’s just a matter of how much it’s worth to get ahead of the 25-year-old’s market and add a player who would fill the defense’s biggest hole right now to help keep this season afloat? And of course, what the Eagles are willing to accept to part with Ojomo. If Ojomo isn’t traded, there’s a good chance he hits the open market since Philly recently paid defensive tackles Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis. WR Brian Thomas Jr., Jacksonville Jaguars I’ve been pounding this drum for a while. Obviously, Thomas’ production has been underwhelming since his near 1,300-yard performance as a rookie. Otherwise, we wouldn’t be talking about him as a trade candidate. But I get the feeling that’s a relationship issue with Liam Coen. It feels like they’ve never been on the same page and have been butting heads since Coen got the job last year. So, if it’s pennies on the dollar, trading for a 24-year-old who could solve the WR1 problem might be worth the risk. With the fifth-year option, the Raiders could get two-and-a-half seasons to see how Thomas performs in Klint Kubiak’s offense before giving him a big-money extension. G Landon Dickerson, Philadelphia Eagles Buyer beware with Dickerson because he’s had several significant injuries, dating back to his college days. The recent ones seem to have really impacted his play on the field, too. However, when healthy, the three-time Pro Bowler is a very good guard and just turned 28 years old. It’s just a matter of how much risk Spytek and Co. are willing to take because last season wasn’t pretty for Dickerson, and he’s only played in one game so far this year. Q: Should the Raiders give up a 2nd and 4th along with a player to get Quenton Nelson? I may be delusional, but I think this offense could get close to elite with a dominant guard. They need to get the run game fixed, especially when Mendoza takes over. A: I don’t hate the idea of trading for Nelson at all! He’s been a Pro Bowler literally every year of his career, made three first-team All-Pro teams and three more second-team selections, and is playing well this year. Clearly, Nelson would be a MASSIVE upgrade over what the Raiders currently have at guard. But where I get a little pause is that he turns 31 in March and is in a contract year. That makes me more cost-conscious when it comes to a trade. To be clear, I’m not as worried about an offensive lineman’s age since the organization has to protect its investment in Mendoza, especially with a lineman of Nelson’s caliber. But Spytek does have to factor in that the team might only get two or three really good years from Nelson, which impacts how high of a pick he should be willing to give up. Also impacting the price tag or Spytek’s willingness to get a deal done now is that Nelson might be available on the open market this offseason, anyway. It’s the same logic as Ojomo above: How much is getting ahead of the market worth? I wish I had an answer to that question, but there’s only one person who does… For me, second- and fourth-round picks AND a player would be too much. If it’s just a second, I think the Raiders should do that in a heartbeat. They aren’t finding a guard who is even close to as good as Nelson is on Day 2 of the draft. I start to waver when two picks are involved because that’s two players who could get second contracts in Las Vegas when Nelson is likely going to be a one-contract addition. Also, that’s where the fact he might be available in free agency for no draft picks really weighs on my mind. Ultimately, I think Nelson should be on the table for the Raiders, where Spytek is at least picking up the phone and giving the Colts a call. Q: Trench Questions: How do you feel about the DTs so far this year? We clamored for a true nose tackle in the draft and got next to nothing. Anyone you’re impressed with on our roster? Is there a trade candidate you feel like could provide what we need? A: I touched on a lot of this above, but defensive tackle is by far the weakest position group on the Raiders’ defense right now. Thomas Booker IV is probably having the best season of the position group, and Booker is nothing to write home about. If Spytek doesn’t trade for one of the two defensive tackles mentioned above — and you could throw Vita Vea in there, too — then it needs to be one of the general manager’s top priorities in the offseason. He’s ignored it for too long and the defense is paying the price. The draft class has been pretty disapointing at the position as a whole this year, but I still really like Ole Miss’ Will Echoles and Tennesssee’s Xavier Gilliam has been a huge riser this season. In free agency, I’ll be keeping my eye on Ojomo and Kobie Turner from the Los Angeles Rams to give you a few names to keep tabs on for the offseason. Q: Chances of seeing Jackson Powers-Johnson or Trey Zuhn III start at LG? I’m not mad at Caleb Rogers getting live reps at RG if they see him as a future long-term RG. I’m sure Burford isn’t the long-term answer at LG. A: I get the feeling Powers-Johnson’s days in Las Vegas are numbered. It hasn’t been a big deal this year because I think he realized after the Raiders gave Tyler Linderbaum a bag in free agency that his only chance at seeing the field is at guard, but JPJ made it no secret during his first two years that he wants to play center. Now that he’s not even starting at guard, I can see a “mutual parting of ways” coming in the future. Maybe not at the deadline, but that will at least be a talking point in the offseason. I view this as a similar situation to Tyree Wilson this past offseason. Zuhn, on the other hand, I could absolutely see starting at left guard at some point this season. As you mentioned, Burford played well last week after getting called out in the media ( you’re welcome, Spencer! ), but he’s been far from consistent this season and throughout his career. Also, he’s only on a one-year contract while Zuhn is in year one of a third-round rookie contract, giving the latter a lot more future/long-term value. When does that happen? Well, your guess is as good as mine because, in my opinion, Klint Kubiak is too attached to Burford. But if the veteran doesn’t start stringing good games together, the rookie is waiting in the wings, and Kubiak might get forced to make that change. Today, we move into the Big XII, taking a closer look at Iowa State and Arizona. The Dolphins are undergoing a complete rebuild this year and will have many roster needs in the 2027 NFL Draft. They will likely select early in the first round, but the draft is about more than just the first pick. Today’s who to watch takes a look at several players who may be day two or day three options, or could be players signed as n undrafted free agents. Iowa State 2027 Draft prospects Jaylen Raynor, quarterback (Senior) – Raynor started 36 games at Arkansas State before moving to Iowa State for his senior season this year. Raynor is a mobile quarterback who can use his legs to extend passing plays or take off as a runner. He threw for 2,261 yards and 19 touchdowns last year, and he also rushed for 423 yards and 7 touchdowns. This year, he has 1,001 passing yards and 7 touchdowns, plus 166 rushing yards and 3 rushing touchdowns in six games. He needs to tighten up his mechanics and accuracy, but his improvisation skills could make him an intriguing option on day three. Isaac Terrell, edge (Senior) – Terrell moved to Iowa State this year after starting his college football career at Washington State. He has proven he can disrupt the backfield and win one-on-one matchups on passing downs through sheer effort. He was a solid edge setter at Washington State, but he will need to prove he can stay effective this season. He needs to add additional pass-rush moves to his repertoire. In the NFL, he is an early depth option who can develop into a starter; probably a day three pick or undrafted free agent signing. Maasai King, tackle (Redshirt senior) – Playing right tackle for Iowa State, King has the strength and technique to continue developing in the NFL. At 6-foot-4 and 310 pounds, he may need to kick inside to guard, but his experience at tackle could keep him in consideration for a swing tackle role. He needs to prove he can handle speed rushers, and he could improve his hand placement to increase his draft profile. He is likely an undrafted free agent who could slide into the late rounds by the end of the year. Omari Hayes, wide receiver (Redshirt senior) – At 5’9 “, 170 pounds, Hayes is a slot receiver with good hands who can continue to develop his route-running. He uses his quickness to create separation and can turn short passes into bigger gains with his yards-after-catch ability. He is likely a camp receiver who can find a place on a practice squad or as a depth player with special teams ability early in his career. Ty Claiborne, wide receiver (Redshirt senior) – Behind Hayes on the Iowa State depth chart, Claiborne offers a different skill set. At 6-foot-2 and 215 pounds, he offers a bigger target to the offense and plays more like a possession receiver than a quick slot receiver. He can move into different roles and could become a boundary option with further development. He probably an undrafted free agent who can come into camp and fight for a roster spot. Arizona 2027 Draft prospects Noah Fifita, quarterback (Redshirt senior) – Fifita is a pocket passer with the mobility to avoid pressure and extend plays. He has touch and accuracy in his throws and reads well. His biggest issue is his size. At 5-foot-10, he has throwing lane issues and he has to compensate for that. He may not have the strongest arm in the class, but he does throw with anticipation that could offset some of the concerns. He is probably an undrafted free agent who could catch on as a practice squad, developmental quarterback. Taye Brown, linebacker (Senior) – Brown is not afraid to tackle. He recorded 93 tackles last season and has 39 this year through six games. He will put his nose in there and bring down the ball carrier. He has to prove that he is more than just a tackler, though. His coverage ability on tight ends will be an important part of his analysis this year, and he has to prove he can shed blocks and force a play into the teeth of the defense rather than just cleaning up when the play comes to him. He is a special teams player who can turn his raw tackling ability into a depth linebacker role early in the NFL; likely a day-three target. Cam Chapa, safety (Junior) – A transfer from Northern Colorado this year, Chapa led the Big Sky in tackles in 2025, and he has continued to show he can be a force as a free safety for Arizona this year. He has 28 tackles and an interception in 2026. He has good range at center field and closes well on the ball in the air. He is not afraid to step up into the box and assist against the run. He needs to keep proving he can succeed in the Big XII for his draft profile to rise, and a return to Arizona for the 2027 season would not be a surprise; if he declares, Chapa could be a day-three steal with further development. Jay’Vion Cole, cornerback (Redshirt senior) – Cole’s collegiate career began at Cal Poly in 2022, then moved to San Jose State in 2023, to Texas in 2024, and finally settled at Arizona for 2025 and 2026. He is a strong zone-coverage cornerback who goes up and gets the ball, but he gets washed off the ball in run defense. He needs to prove his man-coverage skills, especially on double moves, but he has the potential to be a good outside option who can also kick inside as a nickel cornerback. He is probably a day three prospect. Tristan Bounds, tackle (Redshirt senior (sixth year)) – Bounds was granted a sixth year of eligibility by the NCAA after a leg injury ended his 2025 season early. He spent his first four years at Michigan before moving to Arizona last year, where he played 10 games with eight starts. At 6-foot-8and 320 pounds, Bounds has the size to play tackle in the NFL. He is probably a depth option who can continue to work his way into being a day three draft target.

summary: The 5-0 Minnesota Vikings are undefeated but far from perfect, and Two Old Bloggers Darren Campbell and Dave Stefano demand improvement before the schedule gets brutal. With Kyler Murray at quarterback, a Brian Flores defense allowing just 12.8 points per game, and the November 10 trade deadline looming, this episode breaks down why “Get Better […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Cesars Superdome on October 11, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 5-0 Minnesota Vikings are undefeated but far from perfect, and Two Old Bloggers Darren Campbell and Dave Stefano demand improvement before the schedule gets brutal. With Kyler Murray at quarterback, a Brian Flores defense allowing just 12.8 points per game, and the November 10 trade deadline looming, this episode breaks down why “Get Better or Bust” isn’t a catchy title — it’s a mandate. Darren Campbell opened with a sobering reminder: “5-0 though, that was just a little bit too optimistic for my cold, pessimistic Vikings fan heart.” While celebrating the undefeated start, both hosts emphasized that the offense must evolve. “We need that version of Kyler Murray that we saw against New Orleans to again show up for the final 12 games and into the playoffs,” Darren insisted. Dave Stefano echoed the urgency: “We need to be able to do that so they can show that, hey, we can survive a shootout.” Drew Bunting joined for Theme 3 with a deep dive on the Colts, calling Brian Flores’ defense “impossible to figure out” and comparing diagnosing it to solving a Rubik’s Cube in 40 seconds. The trio also tackled the J.J. McCarthy trade fallout, Cam Bynum’s return to U.S. Bank Stadium, and whether the Colts — fresh off firing GM Chris Ballard — are in full meltdown mode under owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon, aka “the Terminator.” Key Points: Kyler Murray must improve : The Vikings need the New Orleans version of Murray — throwing in rhythm, using his legs, limiting turnovers — over the final 12 games Spread the ball around : Jefferson can’t be the only target; Addison, Hockenson, and Jennings need consistent involvement Defense is elite but tested coming : Flores’ unit leads in nearly every category, but the Bills, 49ers, Packers, and Bears loom Health is the X-factor : The 2016 Vikings started 5-0, then injuries decimated the offensive line and they finished 8-8 Trade deadline decisions : Will the Vikings pursue Jonathan Taylor, Quenton Nelson, or a safety like Budda Baker before November 10? J.J. McCarthy starts for the Giants : The “prince that was promised” guarantees weekly comparisons with Kyler Murray Colts in turmoil : Ballard fired, Anthony Richardson in the news, Carlie Irsay-Gordon running the show Statement game opportunity : The Colts can’t pressure the QB, can’t cover, and turn the ball over on 17% of possessions Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: This episode is a goldmine for any Vikings fan trying to separate signal from noise during a perfect start. Darren, Dave, and Drew deliver the kind of unfiltered, stat-backed analysis that makes Two Old Bloggers a must-listen on Vikings 1st & SKOL — and a Bleav Network partner worth your weekly attention. Fan With Us! We have your Minnesota Vikings talk amongst the Two Old Bloggers , Darren @KickassblogVike , and Dave @Luft_Krigare along with our numbers guy, Drew Bunting. Join the conversation! Fan with us at Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL on the Bleav Network @BleavNetwork . So here’s the question: Are the 5-0 Vikings a true Super Bowl contender, or are we watching another fast start destined to flame out like 2016?

title: Minnesota Vikings News and Links: There Are No Easy Games!
summary: I think it is a big game this week. They all are really. The Colts are going to be fired up to try and get a win and not have three straight losses. The defense is going to have to stop the run because I imagine the Colts will lean heavily on Taylor and try […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings drops back to pass against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at Cesars Superdome on October 11, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images I think it is a big game this week. They all are really. The Colts are going to be fired up to try and get a win and not have three straight losses. The defense is going to have to stop the run because I imagine the Colts will lean heavily on Taylor and try to win the time of possession battle. Jones will face blitzes, disguised blitzes, and hopefully a lot of pressure. When he faces pressure he completes 47.2% of his passes with 3 TDs and 4 INTs and has a passer rating of 73.9. I think the Vikings defense will continue to do what it does and try to make it as miserable as possible for Jones. I am hoping for more of the same from the offense. The Colts will be without Sauce Gardner which might lead people to believe the Vikings will try to pass more. They will have Addison, Hockenson, and Mason back too. I could see an attempt at getting more rushing yards to slow down the Colts interior pass rush. DeForest Buckner is going to be a handful. As long as Murray continues to complete a high percentage of his passes and move the chains, the defense will stay rested and, at the very least, Reichard will get some chances at more field goals. I would love to see a 21 -10 victory with the offense kicking 7 field goals just so the folks can wail and gnash their teeth at the offense and bemoan the 6-0 start. But I like to see things burn. The trade talk is ramped up and will only get louder the until the deadline passes. The Colts are a media favorite to tear it down just because they got rid of their GM. I am not sure they will. I suppose Nelson and Buckner could get moved if they indicate they will not re-sign next year. The Colts have 80M in cap space for next year and if they move on from Jones it goes up to 91M. If they make it a post June 1 cut then they will get up to 118M in cap space. The franchise tag amount for Nelson would be about 29M. They can easily do that and probably should. How many teams want to give up a all Pro future Hall of Fame guard? I doubt he goes anywhere. My target would be Taylor but they just extended him and probably wont move him. They are going to need him with any QB and to go with Nelson. It makes too much sense to try to get him though. The Vikings top two backs will be free agents and I am not sure they should bring either one back. Maybe Mason? The available free agents right now do not look good at all. If you give up a 2nd round pick plus other stuff to get a proven All Pro back like Taylor, what is wrong with that? If they do not then they might have to use a first or second on a rookie back who may or may not pan out. I would give the 2027 2nd, 2027 5th, and a conditional 2028 5th for Taylor. I’d throw in Mason just for them to have someone to finish the season. I doubt he gets moved though. Barkley is not going anywhere at the deadline because it would trigger a 26.5M dead money cap hit on the Eagles 2027 cap. Since Buckner made his comment which was “I’m sick and tired of the same song and dance every year”, it is unlikely he signs an extension next year. It would ne nice to get Buckner but he is 32 and will need an extension as he is a free agent next year. I am not sure the team could or should give anyone an extension that plays defensive tackle that is not named Jalen Redmond. I know there are some in the media (Alec Lewis) who believe Teasley is going to be aggressive but there might not be a deal available. I do like Tyjae Spears RB Titans, Tuli Tuipulotu EDGE Chargers, and Jeremy Ruckert TE Jets. Who do you like? Minnesota Vikings News and Links Vikings Jake Golday Isn’t Playing; Why 2nd-Round Pick Is Benched https://heavy.com/sports/nfl/minnesota-vikings/jake-golday-dallas-turner-cashman-wilson-nfl-news/ The Minnesota Vikings spent a second-round draft pick on linebacker Jake Golday, who also has a history in college as a pass-rushing defensive end. So why has he played just seven defensive snaps all season? … Draft writer Justin Melo of Sports Illustrated offered his explanation as to why the Vikings haven’t utilized Golday. “Golday looked outstanding throughout the preseason, but it’s notable when a second-round rookie isn’t playing any regular-season snaps,” Melo wrote on Friday. “Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores has put him on the field just seven times. Now, it’s difficult to crack this 5-0 lineup right now. Golday also played defensive end in college before making the transition to linebacker, so it’s totally normal for his acclimation period to be taking a bit longer.” … Minnesota might have used Golday more frequently if the team’s outside linebackers were not playing as well as they have throughout the team’s undefeated start. Dallas Turner, a first-round pick in 2024, had to wait his turn for two full years before he became a full-time stater in 2026 after the team traded Jonathan Greenard to the Philadelphia Eagles during this year’s draft for two third-round selections in return. … Furthermore, Minnesota’s inside linebackers have been playing exceptionally well also through the undefeated start. Blake Cashman ranks 10th in Pro Football Network’s player impact scores, while Eric Wilson ranks 44th in the same category among linebackers. Because of how well the linebacking corps has played specifically, and how well the Vikings defense has performed as a whole, there simply has been minimal need for Golday in the defense to this point. Vikings Offer Major Update on Jordan Mason After Cutting RB From Roster https://heavy.com/sports/nfl/minnesota-vikings/jordan-mason-injury-deejay-dallas-cut-oconnell-nfl-news/ “Jordan Mason — practiced fully all week, really good week of work — we’ll work through what that looks like. But he is technically questionable right now,” O’Connell told reporters. “No other player will go in with a designation for the game. So, we’ve been able to get a little more healthy. We’ll talk to Jordan and see, but things are looking positive for him being available.” … Also on Friday afternoon, the Vikings announced that they had released running back DeeJay Dallas from the team. Vikings Have No Excuse to Keep Sidelining Forgotten Rookie Amid Safety Concerns https://www.si.com/nfl/vikings/onsi/vikings-no-excuse-keep-sidelining-forgotten-rookie-safety-concerns-01m5n3s2rb9e The Vikings have a real problem at safety. Veterans Harrison Smith and Josh Metellus are ranked among the ten worst safeties in the NFL this season, ranking dead last and sixth-worst, respectively, on Pro Football Focus. Despite the success of defensive coordinator Brian Flores’s unit, a change is needed. That said, the answer to Minnesota’s safety issues might already be on the team’s roster—a 2026 NFL Draft pick has yet to make an impact this season. The Vikings selected Jakobe Thomas with the 98th overall pick in April, yet he hasn’t played a single snap this season. The 6’1″, 211-lb defensive back was inactive for each of Minnesota’s five games before the bye, which doesn’t bode well for his chances against the Colts in Week 7. Thomas played in one preseason game after working hard to recover from a back injury sustained during training camp. In that exhibition game against the Broncos, he had five tackles, three of which were solo efforts. His 79.4 tackling grade ranked second-best among Vikings defenders that game, according to PFF, while his 66.0 run defense grade was seventh-best. Now that he’s healthy and the safety room needs all the help it can get, Thomas needs to be active on game day. Note: Pretty bold (and dumb) to attempt to tell Flores who to play Vikings Week 7: Potential Trade Targets Among Most Important Things to Watch for vs. Colts…

summary: It’s time to take a look at the results of our SB Nation Reacts polls for this week about our Minnesota Vikings, so let’s see what our readers thought about our questions this time around. Our first question is the same question we ask every week, which is how confident everyone is that our favorite […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 16: Christian Darrisaw #71 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on after the game against the Chicago Bears at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s time to take a look at the results of our SB Nation Reacts polls for this week about our Minnesota Vikings, so let’s see what our readers thought about our questions this time around. Our first question is the same question we ask every week, which is how confident everyone is that our favorite team is moving in the right direction. As one of the last three undefeated teams in the NFL. . .however they may have gotten there. . .fans still seem to be relatively happy about how things are going to this point in the season. Of those who responded to our poll, a full three-fourths of you feel that the team is, in fact, heading in the right direction. Yes, it hasn’t always been pretty, but the good guys have taken the field five times this year and have wound up on the right end of the final score on all five of those occasions. They’ve done it despite a bunch of injuries at key positions, including at the quarterback spot and missing Justin Jefferson for the better part of two full games, and they’ve just kept on emerging victorious. Hopefully things will start clicking on the offensive side of the ball at some point the way they have on defense and special teams. Speaking of injuries, the Vikings appear to be ready to welcome back four very important players this coming Sunday when they face the Indianapolis Colts. All of them missed the Week 5 game in New Orleans, and one of them missed even more than that. But of those four returning players, which of them is going to have the biggest impact with their return? Well, we asked and you answered. Of the four returning players, the majority of you decided that offensive tackle Christian Darrisaw’s return will make the biggest impact, with 45% of you who responded to our poll making him your choice. Right behind him was running back Jordan Mason, who hasn’t played since he sustained a thumb injury in Week 1, who was the choice of 35% of those who answered our poll questions. Tight end T.J. Hockenson, who had a big game in Week 4 before his early departure in Week 5, was picked by 19% of our respondents, and apparently nobody is hyped up for the return of wide receiver Jordan Addison, as he was the choice of just 1% of the people who responded to our poll for this week. As always, we want to thank all of you who took the time to respond to our poll for this week, whether it was simply by voting in the polls or by sounding off in the comments section on top of that. Those are your SB Nation Reacts results for this week, folks. We’ll have a new set of polls for you next week, so keep your eyes open for those!

Justin Jefferson Receiving Yardage : Over 72.5 yards (-114) Yeah, I’m going back to what should be a “gimme” for the first one. title: Rewriting the Narrative: The Vikings’ New Story
summary: Narrative is a funny thing in the NFL. Sometimes I question where all of the different storylines come from or why the media focuses on certain aspects over others. Not to be a conspiracy theorist (even though it’s sometimes a hobby for me), but I am sure the NFL marketing department sends information out to […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Will Reichard #16 of the Minnesota Vikings kicks a field goal against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL football game at Cesars Superdome on October 11, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Narrative is a funny thing in the NFL. Sometimes I question where all of the different storylines come from or why the media focuses on certain aspects over others. Not to be a conspiracy theorist (even though it’s sometimes a hobby for me), but I am sure the NFL marketing department sends information out to certain insiders to cover the stories they want to be prevailing storylines. Maybe that’s not true, but there are no definitive facts that could convince me that there isn’t a possibility that most NFL storylines portrayed in the mainstream media are contrived from somewhere inside an NFL VP or executive suite. A new narrative that could pick up steam after this weekend is that the Vikings “chose the wrong quarterback.” People are losing their minds over J.J. McCarthy coming into a game in the fourth quarter, down by 24 points, and leading a feverish comeback that ultimately felt short. It looked all too familiar to Vikings’ fans. For some reason, J.J. McCarthy has always thrived in the 4th quarter. The narrative that is already forming is that Kevin O’Connell’s system wasn’t right for McCarthy and that things are simplified in John Harbaugh’s offense. While that may be true, I didn’t see anything on Sunday that leads me to believe that McCarthy will find any more success in New York than he did in Minnesota. Jason LaCanfora is reporting that some New York Giants executive says there is going to be a major shift in offensive philosophy for New York and to look at the 2018 Ravens with Lamar Jackson in his rookie season. Apparently, New York has been eyeing McCarthy for quite some time to bring in as their starting quarterback. I find that slightly far-fetched based on them only willing to trade a 5th-round pick to acquire him. If McCarthy finds success in New York, there will be questions about why he didn’t find success in Minnesota. Persevere Toward Excellence I know what you’re thinking: STOP TALKING ABOUT THE NEW YORK GIANTS. I am, right now. Narrative lives in a world of hypotheticals. We live in the real world. Reality cannot be denied, and the Vikings are 5-0 going into a very winnable game against the Indianapolis Colts. The Minnesota Vikings have started a season with a 6-0 record six times in the modern NFL era. Of those six seasons, they made the playoffs in all but one, which was in 2003 when they lost on the last play of the season to the Arizona Cardinals. The game that culminated in the classic Paul Allen screaming “NOOOOOOOOO.” All these narratives can be squashed if Kyler Murray goes out and performs to the level at which he is capable. The experiment of drafting a first-round quarterback is over, and we are officially under the Nolan Teasley regime. Minnesota knew what they had in McCarthy. Maybe the Giants were willing to give more in a trade, but the narrative that I am choosing to perpetuate is that the front office was simply ready to move on and was satisfied getting any value back. I wish J.J. the best, but the franchise has chosen a new path. That is what I will do here as well and move on. The Minnesota Vikings are the most enigmatic team in the NFL. Some armchair NFL analysts (people on social media who bought a microphone and know how to post on the internet) are saying that the Vikings are the third-best team in the NFC North. They’re not calling us the third-best 5-0 team; they are saying that the Bears and Packers (both of whom we beat with Carson Wentz) are better. HA! Are We Witnessing History? This defense is special. Like really special, as evidenced by how the Vikings’ current 10-game win streak has manifested itself. Over the last 10 games, the Minnesota Vikings have scored 229 points. Historically, you have to go back to 1934 to find a 10-game winning streak where the team scored fewer points (the 1934 Detroit Lions scored 215 points). That is an astonishing statistic but speaks to the dominance that we have seen from this defense. Football is about winning games. Sure, the Vikings offense has had its struggles and is still finding its footing. Is that a circumstance of poor coaching or them being a bad offense? Or is it a result of a shift in philosophy for Kevin O’Connell? From a narrative perspective, KO is rewriting the defining story of his time as the coach of the Minnesota Vikings. He recently talked about how he has shifted his mindset from being concerned with what stats look like on paper to winning football games. This team is playing complementary football at its finest. Every season has its ebbs and flows, but we also see those differences happen over the course of multiple seasons. Right now, the defense is obviously the strength of this team. When Brian Flores’ unit is fresh, they are almost unstoppable. One thing I have noticed is just how relentless the defensive front is. They just keep coming and don’t stop until after the whistle. The defense is playing with such an intensity that it simply wears down opposing offenses and beats them down into submission. Gotta Have the Ball to Score An important factor in this success is the offense’s ability to maintain drives. So far this season, the Vikings’ are averaging the second highest average time of possession in the league at 33:38 per game. They trail only the Chicago Bears in this category. I will concede that the Vikings haven’t been very efficient when it comes to scoring touchdowns, but I firmly believe that is going to change. In fantasy football, we talk about regression toward the mean. The Minnesota offense has only scored eight offensive touchdowns in 5 games played this season, which is the 2nd fewest in the league. However, this offense is better than that, and we will start to see that number look more normal going forward. Another prevailing shift in philosophy is that this now appears to be a run-first offense, as evidenced by the aforementioned time of possession statistic. This offense is about controlling the clock and taking care of the football. It’s like we are time traveling back to the Mike Zimmer era. However, this is the Teasley/O’Connell/Flores era. We are fans of one of the premier organizations in the NFL, and I think we are going to actually see success beyond the regular season. I know, as a Vikings fan, hope is a slippery slope. A slippery slope to sadness and disappointment. There Is a Long Road Ahead The game this Sunday against the Colts will set the tone for the rest of the season. I fully expect Indianapolis, with their backs to the wall, to make this game competitive for as long as they can. I can also see Daniel Jones throwing four interceptions, which would squash a different narrative that the Vikings shouldn’t have let him leave the building. I think Minnesota wins this game in dominant fashion, and we see our offense come to life. They are going to have to, because this team has a tough schedule going forward where they are going to have to put some points on the board. It’s time for this offense to get rolling and for the defense to keep doing what it does. I can’t wait for Sunday! Until Next Skol.

title: Patriots rooting guide for NFL Week 7
summary: For the New England Patriots, Week 7 was a disappointment. The team of head coach Mike Vrabel dropped its Thursday night meeting with the Chicago Bears with a final score of 30-24, falling to 4-3 on the season and out of the current AFC playoff picture. With their game in the books, 13 others await […]
full_text: For the New England Patriots, Week 7 was a disappointment. The team of head coach Mike Vrabel dropped its Thursday night meeting with the Chicago Bears with a final score of 30-24 , falling to 4-3 on the season and out of the current AFC playoff picture . With their game in the books, 13 others await between Sunday morning and Monday night. Let’s find out who to root in all of them. Sunday 9:30 a.m. ET Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) at New Orleans Saints (2-4) : Go Saints! The Patriots do hold the head-to-head advantage over the Steelers, but a loss against the Saints would still be the preferred outcome to keep New England ahead in the standings. And yes, we know it might have a negative effect on the sixth-round draft pick acquired in the Ja’Lynn Polk trade. | NFL Network 1 p.m. ET San Francisco 49ers (6-0) at Atlanta Falcons (2-4) : Go good game! Neither team is on the Patriots’ schedule or has a draft pick in 2027 tied to the team. | FOX Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) at Baltimore Ravens (4-2) : Go Bengals! We could be rooting for a tie here, but. the odds favor somebody winning this one. In that particular case, we are going with the club that currently has fewer wins on its record. | CBS Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-5) at Carolina Panthers (3-2) : Go good game! Like the 49ers-Falcons matchup mentioned above, this one has no direct impact on New England. | FOX New York Giants (3-2-1) at Houston Texans (2-4) : Go Giants! The class NFC vs. AFC battle that has us rooting for the team not in the Patriots’ conference. It also might impact the sixth-round pick the Texans sent to New England as part of the Marte Mapu trade. | FOX Indianapolis Colts (2-4) at Minnesota Vikings (5-0) : Go Vikings! Like the game above, this one features an NFC and and AFC team going at each other. It also is a chance for the Patriots’ strength of schedule to improve. | CBS Miami Dolphins (0-5) at New York Jets (2-4) : Go Dolphins! An opportunity for some scouting, as the Patriots will head to Miami next Sunday. While a Dolphins win would give them some momentum, it also would hurt the Jets in the race for the AFC playoff spots. | CBS Cleveland Browns (4-2) at Tennessee Titans (1-5): Go Titans! Two AFC teams going against one another, so naturally we are rooting for the one that currently has the worse record. | CBS 4:05 p.m. ET Denver Broncos (4-2) at Arizona Cardinals (2-4) : Go Cardinals! Another AFC vs. NFC matchup with clear rooting affiliations. | CBS 4:25 p.m. ET Green Bay Packers (4-2) at Detroit Lions (3-2) : Go good game! The Patriots have both teams on their schedule, meaning this all-NFC North battle has no impact whatsoever on their own fortunes yet. | FOX Los Angeles Rams (2-4) at Las Vegas Raiders (3-3) : Go Rams! The Patriots would still beat out the Raiders in the standings due to their win over them in Week 5, but that doesn’t mean they should be rooted for. When in doubt, always go with the NFC team in games like this. | FOX 8:20 p.m. ET Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) at Seattle Seahawks (3-3) : Go Seahawks! Once again, we are picking the NFC side over the one representing the AFC. | NBC Monday 8:15 p.m. ET Dallas Cowboys (2-4) at Philadelphia Eagles (2-4): Go good game! Week 7 closes with a game that is not relevant from a Patriots perspective. | ESPN/ABC

title: Sunday Patriots Notes: Rookie class making an early impact
summary: The New England Patriots dropped a competitive 30-24 contest to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. After a long weekend off, they’ll soon turn their attention to the Miami Dolphins. Most of our attention on this week was on the Bears game. With little time to do so, let’s clean out the notebook from Thursday […]
full_text: The New England Patriots dropped a competitive 30-24 contest to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. After a long weekend off, they’ll soon turn their attention to the Miami Dolphins. Most of our attention on this week was on the Bears game. With little time to do so, let’s clean out the notebook from Thursday night and the week. Welcome to the latest edition of our Sunday Patriots Notes. Rookie report The New England rookie class projected largely as a developmental group following this past NFL Draft. But through the first seven weeks of the season, the group has been relied upon. The Patriots have seen their rookies play the second most amount of special teams snaps in the league this season, while the team’s first three selections have impressed. OT Caleb Lomu The Patriots’ first-round pick remains the third tackle on the depth chart behind Will Campbell and Morgan Moses. That hasn’t kept Lomu off the field, as he has seen extensive action twice as an injury replacement while additionally taking on the jumbo tight end role. Lomu has been impressive in his 160 offensive snaps, showing intriguing traits as a pass protector such as his ability to anchor and recover. He allowed just one total pressure in the two games in which he saw extensive action playing both left and right tackle. “Just trying to get ready each and every week. It’s a lot of new things for him,” Mike Vrabel said. “It’s a new league for him. Coming from college, being 21, and it’s a tough position to be able to go out there and play. I think he’s gotten better.” ED Gabe Jacas The power rusher continues to look more and more comfortable as the season continues. His performance Thursday night in Chicago may have been his best as a pro as Jacas tallied five pressures — flashing his patented bull rush on one instance to power through left tackle Ozzy Trapilo. Jacas’ raw strength and power are legit, and his emergence has helped make an edge group that seemed like a position of weakness a strength through seven weeks. TE Eli Raridon New England’s third-round pick has established himself in the offense playing 44% of the offensive snaps as the No. 2 option behind Hunter Henry. Raridon’s athleticism has translated to the pros and Josh McDaniels has done a strong job using the tight end on runaway routes to get him on the move. While the coaching staff has been impressed with Raridon’s growth as a run blocker, it’s expectedly still a work in progress for the rookie, who was at the point of attack for several run stuffs in Chicago. But the work as a receiver, and the mismatches he can create, leaves excitement for the future as Raridon becomes a bigger and bigger piece of the offense. “I think he’s tried to figure out how to block people at this level,” Vrabel said. “I think he blocks better now than what he had shown in previous exposure. I think that he’s growing and gaining confidence each and every day. He’s an exciting young player that’s fun to work with.” Maye’s performance Outside of the interception and some pre-snap issues identifying pressure, Drake Maye was excellent Thursday night as he kept the Patriots competitive with the Bears. Chicago head coach Ben Johnson left impressed. “He’s an outstanding player. It’s very hard to bottle him up,” Johnson said. “You only rush four, and he finds a way if he doesn’t see anything down the field to find an open gap and skirt on through. And then I think what’s really impressive is how he can find these little outlets and these dumps where they’re still running vertical for catch-and-run opportunities… “He’s caught his rhythm now at this point of the season and probably will continue to do that.“ Brown’s performance Following Brown’s return against the Jets, we were encouraged in his movement and separation ability in his return from a high ankle sprain. The same explosiveness did not look present against Chicago, which hopefully is a byproduct of playing two games in five days after returning from an injury that can linger. The Bears did work to take A.J. Brown out of the equation Thursday night, often clouding his side of the field and taking away his intermediate routes. But, the Patriots will need more from their No. 1 wide receiver moving forward regales. Vrabel vs. Refs Mike Vrabel was one of three head coaches — joining Aaron Glenn and Nick Sirianni — who were fined $250,000 this week for conduct towards officials. The fine could reportedly be repealed with good behavior, which perhaps influenced Vrabel’s post game words when discussing Will Campbell’s questionable false start penalty. “I don’t know. I’m not in good favor with the officiating department so I probably shouldn’t say anything.” A.J. and Hurts Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the season with blood clots. When asked about the situation this past week, Brown sent love and prayers to his former quarterback. “It’s a tough situation, man,” Brown said. “I’ve got a lot of love and respect for him, praying for him. I didn’t know how serious it was. I think all of us kind of found that out, but he’s a tough guy. He’s a tough guy, and he can handle anything. I don’t mean that lightly. I know it’s serious. But he can handle it, and I pray God continue to keep his hand on him. It’s a lot of love and respect from this way. Speedy recovery, and a lot of love.” NFLPA The Patriots elected Drake Maye as their NFLPA Voting Player Representative this past week. Maye will serve on the 32-member Board of Player Representatives and hold the team vote. “I think it’s an honor,” Maye said. “It’s an honor to represent this team, represent the Patriots and to represent the players and the players in this league. I’m going to try to gain some knowledge about how the league works and knowing that this position carries a lot of weight in this league … I know Coach Vrabel was the player rep here. Just trying to make sure that the coaches and players are doing all right.” Maye was elected along with altnerates Will Campbell, Marcus Jones and Brenden Schooler. Jolly Ranchers During halftime of the Raiders game, cornerback Charles Woods had a different request for Mike Vrabel. A grape jolly rancher. The following week against the Jets, Vrabel made sure to keep the grape-flavored candy in his pocket. He gave one to Woods in the fourth quarter and soon after, the cornerback hauled in his first career interception to help seal a Patriots victory. “I kind of like him. He’s got a little street rat in him,” Vrabel said of Woods. “The story was, he was like, ‘Coach, can I get a Jolly Rancher?’ I was like, ‘Are you serious?’ I’m like, ‘Yes.’ At halftime, it was like I was coaching one of the kids’ teams in ninth grade, 9-year-old football. I was like, ‘Yeah, sure, have a Jolly Rancher.’ “Then we won the game and then I joked about it when he got a game ball. We called him Jolly Rancher, JR now for short. Then last week I said, ‘I’m ready to go. I got your grape Jolly Ranchers.’ Put one in, and the next play, he got an interception. I was like, ‘This is crazy.’” Week ahead After enjoying the weekend off, the Patriots will return to the facility on Monday before resuming a typical in-season schedule before next Sunday’s game against the Miami Dolphins. This means Mike Vrabel media availability on Monday, off-day on Tuesday, and three straight practices plus injury reports from Wednesday through Friday. The team will then hold a final walkthrough on Saturday before departing for Miami.
author: Brian Hines

title: Patriots vs. Bears: The good, the bad, the s—t that gets you beat
summary: Ahead of his first training camp as Patriots head coach in 2025, Mike Vrabel explained that he was judging his team’s performances by three distinct categories: the good, the bad, and the s—t that gets you beat. If Vrabel looks at his team through those specific categorizations, we shall follow his lead. The New England […]
full_text: Ahead of his first training camp as Patriots head coach in 2025, Mike Vrabel explained that he was judging his team’s performances by three distinct categories: the good, the bad, and the s—t that gets you beat. If Vrabel looks at his team through those specific categorizations, we shall follow his lead. The New England Patriots are now 0-2 in prime time games this season. The second of those defeats came on Thursday night at the hands of the Chicago Bears, a 30-24 loss in what was a competitive game between two good teams. At the end of the day, though, it was the home team that ended up making more plays. With that said, let’s dive into our weekly breakdown of the good and the not-so-good from the loss at Soldier Field. The good: Pass game operation Even though his early-season version reared its head again at one point, Drake Maye looked every bit like the franchise-caliber quarterback he is on Thursday. In fact, the entire pass game operation was pretty good against the Jets: two touchdowns plus 310 net yards and 9.4 per play, and that’s not even including 26 yards on three scrambles. From top to bottom, New England moved the ball well whenever it took to the air. Of course, that was largely due to Maye. “He gave us a chance. He competed,” said Mike Vrabel. “I know he’d like to have that throw back to Eli [Raridon], but I thought he really competed. Whether that was running around and scrambling or finding good places to go with the football, he gave us a chance. I know he’d like to have that one back and he’ll learn from it like he always does. I’m glad he’s ours.” On the day, Maye completed 77.4% of his pass attempts for 321 yards, a pair of touchdowns and that interception in the end zone. Even putting that play into account, he finished with 0.34 expected points added per play — the same number as his Bears counterpart, Caleb Williams. Maye is the main man, but the operation also function the way it did because of the blocking up front. Even with guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown out (let alone Mike Onwenu), New England surrendered only 14 quarterback disruptions for a 38.9% pressure rate — the third-best mark of the season thus far. “We protected when they pressured,” said Vrabel. “I thought that was a huge key for us as they continued to pressure and put a lot of guys on the line of scrimmage. Our ability to pick it up and hit some chunk plays was really the reason we were in it in the second half.” The bad: Traditional run game “We didn’t run the ball well enough,” was Mike Vrabel’s blunt assessment after the game. And he was right, the Patriots didn’t. Excluding those aforementioned Drake Maye scrambles but including a quarterback sneak for no gain, the Patriots finished with only 44 yards on 14 carries for an average of 3.1 yards per run and -0.40 expected points added per run. As a reminder, the Bears defense had entered Thursday ranked just 25th in the NFL, giving up an average EPA of -0.057. So, what was the issue? Unsurprisingly given the circumstances, it started up front: New England’s run blocking simply was too spotty to make a consistent difference. When it worked well the results looked the part (see: Rhamondre Stevenson’s 13-yard carry in the second quarter) but when it didn’t there simply was no room for the backups to operate (see: the very next play). Given that the Patriots had to overhaul their O-line on a short week, struggles like that had to be expected. But the breakdowns were not only due to Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor entering the lineup, but across the board — including at tight end and wide receiver. One potential big TreVeyon Henderson run, for example, was unable to develop because center Jared Wilson was beat climbing to the second level; meanwhile, Eli Raridon’s run blocking continues to be a mixed bag. Add it all up, and you get the Patriots not getting anything going on the ground. The s—t that gets you beat: Big-play defense Leading up to the game, we mentioned “limiting explosive runs” as a key to the game for the Patriots. To their credit, they did that, and were only beaten twice by a team averaging close to four explosive per game entering the contest; those two plays furthermore only barely earned “big play” status by gaining precisely the 10 yards required for that classification. But while New England did a good job in that area, stopping big plays was an issue throughout the evening on Thursday: the Bears finished with 10 of them, meaning that eight happened in the passing game and on plays gaining 20-plus yards. Among those was a 58-yard catch-and-run and 24-yard touchdown, both to wide receiver Luther Burden. The Patriots struggled to defend the second-year man all game: he was responsible for four of those eight explosive passing plays, gaining 130 yards total on those. To make matters worse, three of the explosives — including Burden’s touchdown — came in third-and-long situations and only one came on first down. On average, the Bears were 11.6 yards off the line to gain on their big passing plays. Those situations do invite a vertical pass game, but this also shows how New England’s defense kept putting itself in favorable situations only to allow the Bears to nonetheless wiggle their way out of them. There are a multitude of issues why New England gave up that many big plays in the passing game. Some were just excellent execution on the offense’s part; some were apparent communication breakdowns at the second and third levels; some were the result of insufficient tackling and New England missing a combined 17 of 81 tackle attempts for a rate of almost 21%. No matter the reason, the performance in that area simply wasn’t good enough.

title: Key matchups: Saints vs. Steelers
summary: The New Orleans Saints are coming off a must-win game against the New York Giants. Coming off their big win, the Saints are now enjoying their time in Paris ahead of another probable must-win game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Gayle Benson and the Saints organization have put a lot of resources into being the ambassadors […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 18: Alvin Kamara #41 of the New Orleans Saints runs against Jason Pinnock #25 of the New York Giants during their game at MetLife Stadium on October 18, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints are coming off a must-win game against the New York Giants. Coming off their big win, the Saints are now enjoying their time in Paris ahead of another probable must-win game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Gayle Benson and the Saints organization have put a lot of resources into being the ambassadors of the NFL in Paris, and a win will certainly help. But if the Black and Gold want to go into the bye with a win, they’ll have to utilize these key matchups. Saints pass protection vs. Steelers’ star pass rushers The Saints have surprisingly held their own against some of the league’s top pass rushers through their first six games of the season. Abdul Carter, Maxx Crosby, Aiden Hutchinson, and Trey Hendrickson have combined for one sack against the Saints’ pass protection. Despite their success, they haven’t faced a group as talented as the Steelers pass rushers, highlighted by T.J. Watt. The former Defensive Player of the Year has 4.5 sacks so far this season and remains in contention for the prestigious award this season. The Saints’ pass protection has struggled this season, mostly due to blitz packages, and is facing a Steelers team that blitzes just 26% of the time. Pittsburgh is confident in their pass rushers to win one-on-one with Watt, Nate Herbig, and Alex Highsmith therefore don’t send in extra pass rushers. The key to winning the game is keeping Tyler Shough upright, and the Saints are certain to be tested in pass protection. Saints run game vs. Steelers run defense Unfortunately for the Saints offense, they’re facing a defense that’s good against the pass and against the run. While their run defense isn’t as good as their top-10 pass defense, it’s still above average, ranked 14th in the NFL. But a 14th-place ranking doesn’t tell the whole story. Pittsburgh held Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving to 2.3 yards per carry on 19 carries, Jonathan Taylor to 3.0 yards per carry, and Quinshon Judkins to 3.1 yards per carry. The Steelers’ run defense is performing exceptionally against running backs and will be facing a Saints team coming off their best rushing performance of the season. The Saints rushed for 175 yards against the Giants, highlighted by Kendre Miller, who rushed for 70 yards on 3.5 a carry. Alvin Kamara and C.J. Donaldson, however, were more efficient with their touches, rushing for 4.9 and 6.5 yards per carry, respectively. The Saints are dealing with injuries to their offensive line, with rookie Jeremiah Wright taking over for Cessar Ruiz. Wright was impressive in his NFL debut and played a big role in the Black and Gold’s rushing success. If New Orleans wants to find their third win of the season, it will have to come with more success running the ball. Saints’ pass defense vs. QB Aaron Rodgers The Saints’ secondary had their best three quarters of the season, then followed it up with an unbelievably bad fourth quarter. After intercepting Jameis Winston twice and J.J. McCarthy once, the Saints defense allowed 243 passing yards to McCarthy in their fourth-quarter meltdown, and will now face a veteran in Aaron Rodgers, who is playing good football. Rodgers has thrown for 3+ touchdowns in four of his last five games. While he has made mistakes, throwing four interceptions in that span, the veteran is playing his best since leaving the Green Bay Packers. Pittsburgh is a solid rushing team, but they rely on Rodgers to win them games. Stop Rodgers, and you have a good chance to come out of Paris with a win.

full_text: DALLAS, TX - OCTOBER 10: Texas Longhorns wide receiver Cam Coleman (8) catches a touchdown pass during the Allstate Red River Rivalry between the Texas Longhorns and Oklahoma Sooners on October 10, 2026, at Cotton Bowl Stadium in Dallas, TX. (Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images While the New Orleans Saints are preparing to take on the Steelers in Paris tomorrow morning, there are some intriguing college players to watch on Saturday who could potentially become additions to the Saints’ roster in 2027. Here are three college players to watch this Saturday. Cam Coleman, WR, Texas Yes, a wide receiver. The likelihood of this happening is very low, but Coleman is still an exciting player to watch. He will be matching up against a very talented Ole Miss team tonight at 6:30 PM on ABC. Coleman and quarterback Arch Manning are still looking to make the Texas offense more explosive, but Coleman’s combination of size, speed, athleticism, and ability to make contested catches makes him one of the best receivers in the class. Suntarine Perkins, EDGE/OLB, Ole Miss Perkins will be on the field at the same time as Cam Coleman, and if the Texas offense is sputtering, there’s a good chance it will be because of the impact Perkins is having on Arch Manning and the rest of the Longhorn offense. Perkins possesses the ability to rush the passer and play off-ball linebacker. His versatility would be a welcome addition to a Saints defense looking for a consistent complement to Chase Young, as well as a player who can operate off the ball and make plays in space. Justin Scott, DT, Miami The No. 1 team in the nation will take on Pitt at 11 AM on ESPN, and in the middle of Miami’s defense will be Justin Scott. Scott is a powerful interior defensive tackle who can play well against the run and affect the quarterback from the interior. This has been a major issue for the Saints’ defensive front this season. Not having a consistent presence in the heart of the defensive line has negatively affected the Saints’ run defense while also allowing opposing quarterbacks more time to step up in the pocket and find open receivers downfield. The Saints have a lot of issues, so adding talent at almost any position this offseason would be a breath of fresh air. Are there any players you’re excited to watch today? Share your thoughts in the comments.

title: NY Giants roster moves: Tremaine Edmunds to IR, Paulson Adebo returns
summary: The New York Giants continue to take hits on defense. The Giants have placed inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, the team’s leading tackler through six games, on injured reserve with a torn chest muscle. The Giants also announced on Saturday that starting safety Jevon Holland, who has a team-high three interceptions, has been downgraded to out […]
full_text: Tremaine Edmunds | Getty Images The New York Giants continue to take hits on defense. The Giants have placed inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, the team’s leading tackler through six games, on injured reserve with a torn chest muscle. The Giants also announced on Saturday that starting safety Jevon Holland, who has a team-high three interceptions, has been downgraded to out with a concussion. Edmunds had 50 tackles in six games. He was second behind rookie Arvell Reese in solo tackles with 34. Micah McFadden, a full-time starter at linebacker for the Giants in 2023 and 2024, will take Edmunds’ place. McFadden played in just one game last season due to a foot injury. The Giants have also lost edge defender Brian Burns, who has 16.5 sacks in 2025, and starting defensive lineman Chauncey Golston for the season. To take Edmunds’ place on the roster, the Giants are activating veteran cornerback Paulson Adebo from injured reserve. Adebo played in just one game before going on IR with a knee injury. He could start on Sunday against the Houston Texans as Greg Newsome II has already been ruled out with a concussion. The Giants also announced that tight end Theo Johnson will miss a second straight game with a neck injury. He had initially been listed as questionable. Chance for Jalin Hyatt Wide receiver Jalin Hyatt was one of two practice squad elevations for the Giants. The other was safety Raheem Layne. Hyatt, a 2023 third-round pick by the Giants, has been on the practice squad all season. He has 36 receptions in 41 career games. Layne gives the Giants protection if Tyler Nubin (neck) can’t play.

title: Survey results: Giants fans support the quarterback change
summary: The New York Giants made news this week when the team made the decision to go with J.J. McCarthy as their starting quarterback against the Houston Texans. McCarthy has only been in the building since the Giants traded a 2027 fifth round to the Minnesota Vikings for him on September 28th. Backup quarterback Jameis Winston […]
full_text: New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The New York Giants made news this week when the team made the decision to go with J.J. McCarthy as their starting quarterback against the Houston Texans. McCarthy has only been in the building since the Giants traded a 2027 fifth round to the Minnesota Vikings for him on September 28th. Backup quarterback Jameis Winston went 2-1-1 as the Giants’ starter following Jaxson Dart’s season-ending knee injury in Week 2, but the offense was simply too inconsistent with Winston under center. The hope is that the offense can find more traction and consistency with McCarthy behind center, who shares traits and a skill set with Jaxson Dart. It’s a very small sample size, but McCarthy did throw for nearly 250 yards and a touchdown in less than 12 minutes as the Giants’ starter. Perhaps even more encouragingly, the Giants’ run game also seemed to have a bit of life as well. We’ll see how much of an impact the change in quarterback can have on the Giants’ offense and the team as a whole. Right now, Vegas isn’t particularly optimistic and the Giants are 10.5-point underdogs on the road against the Texans ( per FanDuel ). Earlier this week, prior to the quarterback change, we asked whether the Giants should start McCarthy or Jameis Wisnton. The response was pretty overwhelming in favor of McCarthy. The change from Winston to McCarthy has something of the feel of starting a rookie quarterback, harkening back (a bit) to the changeover from Russell Wilson to Dart last year. McCarthy is still a young quarterback at 23, and just 255 days older than 2026 1st overall pick Fernando Mendoza. However, he isn’t exactly an inexperienced rookie despite his age and recent arrival in the Giants’ building. McCarthy does have 10 starts to his name, and has been on a Harbaugh coached team before (under Jim Harbaugh at Michigan). So he already comes in with an understanding of what the NFL game is like, has experience in sophisticated pro systems and against NFL defenses. But there’s still an element of the unknown and the hope of untapped potential that often comes with starting a rookie quarterback. And combined with the added dimension that his athleticism brings to the offense, the change from Winston to McCarthy has the potential to be exciting as well as intriguing. Perhaps because of that, fan confidence hasn’t plummeted despite the Giants’ mid-game implosion against the New Orleans Saints. Fan confidence has dipped some after holding steady at 95 percent over the previous two weeks. It hasn’t dropped as much as after the Giants’ loss to the Rams, nor as much as after losses in pervious years. Fans still seem pretty optimistic about the Giants in the long term, though the short term is becoming increasingly stressful as injuries pile up. The Giants have been in “suvival mode” since Dart was lost for the season, and that fight for survival is only becoming more desperate as starters like Brian Burns and Tremaine Edmunds are lost. Likewise, other starters like Andrew Thomas, Jermaine Eluemunor, Jevon Holland, Tae Banks, Greg Newsome II, Theo Johnson, and Tyler Nubin have all been bitten by the injury bug. And yet the Giants have shown impressive resilience and kept fighting. Hopefully McCarthy can spark the offense and upset the Texans as the Giants go into a their much-needed bye week.
