title: Draft prospects to watch for the NY Giants in Week 8
summary: Good morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 8 of the 2026 college football season! The college football landscape got put in a blender last week, with upsets galore in an already turbulent year for football. The talent landscape is more even than we’ve seen it in quite some time — […]
full_text: Tennessee defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam pressures Texas QB Arch Manning | ISI Photos via Getty Images Good morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 8 of the 2026 college football season! The college football landscape got put in a blender last week, with upsets galore in an already turbulent year for football. The talent landscape is more even than we’ve seen it in quite some time — maybe ever — and that’s not only surfacing some incredibly intriguing prospects, it’s also giving us thrilling games on a weekly basis. As usual, we’re going to look at college football through the lens of the Giants’ perceived needs and how various prospects might fit. This week we’re looking at the Safety, Defensive Tackle, and Running Back positions. Auburn vs. (18) LSU ABC – noon One thing is for sure in this game: the Tigers are going to win. LSU is trying to claw their way back into the College Football Playoff picture while Auburn wants to build on last week’s upset win over Georgia. LSU certainly boasts more NFL caliber talent than Auburn, but we should expect this to be a tough, physical showdown. But for our purposes, we’re looking at LSU’s roster, and their secondary in particular. Player spotlight: Ty Benefield (S, LSU) We mentioned Benefield way back in Week 1, and now it’s time to circle back for a closer look. Ty Benefield has great size for a modern safety at 6-foot-3, 208 pounds, and is rounding into form as a playmaker for LSU’s defense. He transferred to LSU from Boise State and brings versatility as a multi-dimensional playmaker. His size allows him to play the STAR or MONEY role as a hybrid at the second level of the defense, while also having the athleticism to be a traditional safety on the back end of the defense. So far Benefield has 30 total tackles. a sack, a tackle for loss, an interception, and two passes defensed. Benefield is currently considered a Day 2 prospect, and has the potential to be a solid second round player by the time the Draft Process is under way. South Carolina vs. (11) Tennessee ESPN – 3:30 p.m. This is a sneaky game. Tennessee is riding high after a huge upset win over Alabama last week, while the Gamecocks have been playing better after a terrible start to the season. Tennessee has the fiercest pass rush in college football, while South Carolina boasts some of the biggest freaks in college football in WR Nyck Harbor, QB LaNoriss Sellers, and EDGE Dylan Stewart. Considering the state of the Giants’ wide receiver depth chart, I want to keep an eye on Nyck Harbor, who has been flashing game-breaking ability in his second year as a full-time football player. He remains a project, but his Megatron-esque traits make him an incredibly intriguing project. That said, our spotlight is on the Tennessee defensive line. Player spotlight: Xavier Gilliam (iDL, Tennessee) Gilliam is rocketing up draft boards and has quickly become one of the — if not the — most disruptive defensive tackles in college football right now. He transferred from Penn State to Tennessee and has absolutely exploded onto the scene as a full-time player in the SEC. He currently boasts 5.0 sacks and 10.5 tackles for a loss thanks to his natural leverage and explosive first step. Gilliam has a stocky, dense frame at 6-foot-2, 305 pounds, which makes it easy for him to play with consistently great pad level. Combined with a powerful lower body and heavy hands, he’s a real headache for offensive linemen. Gilliam might not be a ginormous space-eating two-gap tackle, but his ability to blow up blockers or penetrate and disrupt have made him one of college football’s fastest risers this year. Don’t be surprised if he’s mentioned in the same sentence as Ole Miss iDL Will Echoles as the first defensive tackle drafted. (12) Kentucky vs. Vanderbilt SEC Network – 7:30 p.m. Will Stein has transformed the Kentucky football program, taking them from an afterthought that occasionally gets some good players to a real threat in the SEC. I don’t expect much of a game against Vanderbilt, and I do expect most people to tune into (19) Texas vs. (7) Ole Miss instead of this game. That said, we’ve talked about both Texas and Ole Miss enough for now and I wanted to take the opportunity to highlight what Kentucky is doing this year. Player spotlight: C.J. Baxter (RB, Kentucky) I’ll get this out of the way up front — Baxter comes with an injury red flag and his draft stock will be closely tied to his medical evaluations. However, he could certainly catch the Giants’ eye if those check out. He suffered a rib injury against Rice as a Freshman at Texas, then missed the entire 2024 season when he tore his LCL and PCL ligaments in practice. He’s since transferred from Texas to Kentucky and apparently returned to form. As we’ve covered over the last week, John Harbaugh doesn’t seem to have any one running back on the Giants’ roster that he loves . He seems to want a bellcow back who can execute the power run game Harbaugh wants to use as the foundation for the Giants’ philosophy. Baxter has a great blend of size and athleticism at 6-foot-1, 230 pounds (listed) and (prior to his injury) was being compared to Bijan Robinson for his explosiveness and power. Now, Baxter is back to full health and is averaging 5.6 yards per carry with 8 touchdowns on just 87 total carries. He understands how and when to be physical and run behind his pads, as well as when to pick out a hole to maximize his yardage. Baxter runs with solid vision and patience behind the line of scrimmage, as well as good tempo and a subtle wiggle to turn hits into glancing blows. He’s a very smooth runner with good acceleration and solid top-end speed for a big back. And while he hasn’t been asked to catch the ball much, he does a good job of locating the ball and reaching out to pluck it out of the air before turning upfield.

title: NFL Week 7 betting advice: Giants-Texans picks and props
summary: Welcome to the New York Giants betting angle, Week 7 edition! Each week, I’m giving you my three favorite wagers for that week’s New York Giants game. My one rule: I won’t ever give you wagers that are less than -120. No gimmes! For the third straight week, the Giants are underdogs to a team with a […]
full_text: J.J. gets his shot | Getty Images Welcome to the New York Giants betting angle, Week 7 edition! Each week, I’m giving you my three favorite wagers for that week’s New York Giants game. My one rule: I won’t ever give you wagers that are less than -120. No gimmes! For the third straight week, the Giants are underdogs to a team with a record that’s worse than theirs. Not only that, they’re big underdogs this time around. The 2-4 Houston Texans are laying a whole bunch of lumber — 10.5 points to be exact — to the 3-2-1 Giants. It’s the biggest line on the board in Week 7. When the Giants announced earlier in the week that J.J. McCarthy would be getting the start at Houston, the line moved by about three points. Clearly, the betting public thinks it’s more likely that we’ll get the 2025 version of J.J. than the one that provided about 250 yards of offense in less than a quarter of mop-up duty against New Orleans last Sunday. The Texans started out 0-4, but have won two straight since. Their fearsome defense hasn’t lived up to the hype, but quarterback C.J. Stroud, who completely melted down in the 2025 playoffs, has turned it around and is playing even better than he did in his excellent rookie season. As for the Giants, it’s been an adventure. They’re 0-1-1 in their last two games, both of which were very winnable. This one might not be, as the line suggests. Big Blue is banged up at a number of spots, and the Week 8 Bye looms as a time to recover. In an odd twist, the Giants will remain in first place in the NFC East through Week 7 regardless of the outcome of this game. After going 8-1 from Weeks 3-5, I went 1-2 last week. My picks are 11-7 on the season – not bad! I’m looking to get back in the win column this week. Let’s get to this week’s picks. All lines and odds are from Fanduel and are as of Friday, October 23. The line for the game is Texans -10.5, with a game total of 43.5. The line and total are both stay-aways for me, as are most Giants’ props. With the Giants changing quarterbacks for the second time this season, there are a lot of unknowns. Texans 1 st half total points OVER 13.5 (-115). I’m nervous that this game will get away from the Giants in a hurry, with Houston’s defense finally playing to its potential, J.J. McCarthy struggling in his first start, and the banged-up Giants just trying to get out alive. I can see Houston having a pretty big first half, and then going conservative in the second half with a lead. Marvin Harrison, Jr. OVER 2.5 receptions (-118). Harrison caught three balls on four targets in his Texans’ debut last Sunday in London, despite playing just 12 snaps (19% of the total). The game was also highly competitive, and Houston threw a lot. I think Harrison should be on the field a lot more this week, and while they’ve got plenty of other options in the passing game, they don’t run the ball well and there should be enough to go around. C.J. Stroud and Harrison are quite familiar from their time at Ohio State, and that’s a plus. I also think there will again be a concerted effort to get their new toy involved. Take the over. J.J. McCarthy UNDER 200.5 passing yards (-114). I know, I know. McCarthy eclipsed this total in less than a quarter last week. That gives me some pause, but that was in garbage time, against a bad defense that had pulled some of its starters. In ten starts for Minnesota last season, McCarthy only topped 200 yards twice. Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely have been beasts, and they give McCarthy a chance to exploit a Texans’ secondary that’s been a major disappointment. I don’t think that’s going to happen with any kind of consistency. The Giants’ O-line is banged up, and I expect McCarthy to be under duress from Houston’s outstanding edge rushers. I foresee a lot of bad throws when he isn’t taking off on a run or getting sacked. Those are the picks for Week 7. Good luck with your wagers! And if you play fantasy football, be sure to check out my Week 7 fantasy preview, with start/sit advice and more, right here .
author: David Hartman

title: New York Giants mailbag: J.J. McCarthy, Jon Runyan, Cam Skattebo, more
summary: Alan Backman asks: I know everyone (including me) may be over-reacting to J.J. McCarthy having 2 great quarters. But let’s take the upside for a minute. 1. Contract – How does that work? Did Giants acquire the rights to that 4 year locked deal from the Vikings? My understanding is that this contract is guaranteed. So who absorbs the guarantee […]
full_text: Alan Backman asks: I know everyone (including me) may be over-reacting to J.J. McCarthy having 2 great quarters. But let’s take the upside for a minute. 1. Contract – How does that work? Did Giants acquire the rights to that 4 year locked deal from the Vikings? My understanding is that this contract is guaranteed. So who absorbs the guarantee cost – Giants or Vikes? 2. If McCarthy continues to do well, what do you think Giants should do when Dart recovers? I assume that no matter how well McCarthy plays, Dart gets the job back. But then what ? Winston just signed a new deal. Do the Giants keep 3 QB’s going forward? Don’t get me wrong. This would be a good problem to have. If not 3 QBs, do you think the Giants would consider trading McCarthy or Winston for draft picks? Or just keep all the QBs? Ed says: Alan, McCarthy had one great quarter. Actually, he had a great nine minutes. The Giants pick up McCarthy’s rookie contract. They are responsible for the pro-rated portion of his $1.075 million base salary this season. Next season, they are respnsible for $3.775 million — $1.19 million in base salary and the rest is a $2.585 million roster bonus. They also get the fifth-year option, should they want to exercise it. Next year? Jaxson Dart is the Giants’ quarterback. They did not acquire McCarthy to compete with Dart, and I have serious doubts he can do anything to change that. They acquired McCarthy to help them try to navigate a season without Dart. Maybe, just maybe, if McCarthy plays well enough that someone out there thinks he can be a starter the Giants can flip him and get the fifth-round pick they used to get him — or better — back in a deal. To me, Winston is a great locker room presence, a leader and a big help to Dart. He is fine for a couple of games. No team, though, wants to try and get through 15 games with backup quarterbacks — which is what the Giants are trying to do. Spencer Gross asks: What do we do about our offensive line and why in God’s name did we extend Runyan? Is there an out for the contract or did we just give him some money for the sake of it? Ed says: Spencer, what would you like the Giants to do about their offensive line? Look around the NFL, there are a lot of teams with offensive lines far worse than the Giants. As it happens, the Giants happen to have one of the league’s best pass-blocking lines. Pro Football Focus ranks the Giants No. 4 in the league in pass-blocking, and fourth-worst in run-blocking. ESPN’s ‘win rate’ statistic has the Giants 16th in the league in pass-block win rate and 14th in run block win rate — basically in the middle of the league. Sharp Football Analysis says the Giants have given up pressure on 31.8% of pass plays, seventh-best in the NFL. Conversely, Sharp has the Giants at 0.8 yards rushing before contact, fifth-worst in the NFL. They are, overall, a middle of the pack line. Really good in pass protection. Not good in run blocking. Can the run-blocking get better? Sure. Sisi Mauigoa is struggling, but has played only six games. Andrew Thomas has not been healthy. Jermaine Eluemunor just missed a game. Bryan Hudson has had two good games and one bad one since becoming the starting center. Runyan? The Giants knew what he was when they gave him that extension. He’s an adequate starter, far better at pass protection than run blocking. They had to do something to get under the salary cap, and extending his contract is one of the choices they made. A closer examination of his two-year, $22 million extension shows that it isn’t as bad as it might seem. Yes, he has $19.25 million in guaranteed. The full guarantee consists of a $9 million signing bonus and his 2026 and 2027 base salaries. There is no guaranteed money for Runyan in 2028, effectively making the extension a one-year deal through 2027. The Giants can get out of that deal in 2028 with a $3 million dead cap charge and $11 million in cap savings. Matthew Mosley asks: Curious of your thoughts on JMS & Adebo? Do they possess any trade value this year, whether it be player for player swap or draft capital? JMS seems to have lost his job and it’s clear with the practice squad additions, that the Giants have zero intent on playing him. Regarding Adebo, his return could be great depth for a run in the second half of the season. However, he’s looked fairly pitiful in the action we’ve seen this year. Giants have an opportunity to win this division, but there are glaring holes that need to be filled in order to do so. Do these players present any value to the current roster or potentially another team looking for added depth? Ed says: Matthew, I think it might be possible that the Giants could move John Michael Schmitz to a center-needy team, perhaps one that has an injury at the position and needs an adequate short-term fix. I doubt he would bring more than a seventh-round pick, maybe even a conditional seventh based on playing time. I doubt that Paulson Adebo has much trade value, given his contract, injury history, and performance since he has been a Giant. An acquiring team would take on whatever pro-rated portion of his $17.25 million base salary for the rest of this season is. That’s a lot to swallow for a player who has been available for just 20 of the last 40 regular-season games, and has not played well since signing with the Giants last season. I don’t know why anyone would do it. Caleb Hoke asks: Why is everyone so up in arms about Skattebo not getting many touches? I understand the love from the fans, I like the way he runs hard. (He could, maybe, not look for contact every play.) But, as a coach, myself, there goes more into playing time than just what fans see on Sundays. While I only coach middle school and high school and it is VASTLY different from coaching the NFL (I coach kids and not adults), but the basis is, there are practices throughout the week. Film, practice, walkthroughs, etc. Could it be that Skattebo is missing something in practices that led to the “benching”? Could it be that he has missed other assignments? Could it be more than just he fumbled in key moments of games? I just think that we, as fans, get into seeing what happens on Sundays and thinking that is all there is to it. We aren’t at practices and meetings. We aren’t on the sidelines on Sundays either. We don’t know all that goes into decisions. Ed says: Caleb, since when does not knowing everything — or anything about what goes on inside a team — prevent fans from having, and loudly sharing, opinions? That’s just the nature of fandom. Skattebo’s popularity/appeal outweigh his talent/production. Fans don’t want to hear that, but it’s the truth. He is an important player for the Giants the way they are constructed, but his lack of speed and size make him a limited one. There is a reason the Giants were interested in Kenneth Walker in free agency, Jeremiyah Love in the draft, and why there is so much speculation about trying to trade for Jonathan Taylor of the Colts. Skattebo is not the equal of players like Taylor, Derrick Henry, Saquon Barkley, Walker, Christian McCaffrey, James Cook, Jahmyr Gibbs, and Bijan Robinson. Skattebo’s lack of opportunity against the New Orleans Saints was not related to anything more than his issues with ball security. The message, though, had to be sent. And, it was. Ronald Buchheim asks: After Tracy failed to block a runner and then fumbled, Harbaugh said the back would be judged by his entire body of work rather than a few recent mistakes. Then he was immediately dropped on the depth chart before being banished from the rotation almost entirely. Next he answered your question regarding Harris’s frustration about getting few touches by saying that he understands and respects the runner’s feeling but touches obviously have to be earned. Then Harris is immediately cut. Harbaugh seems quite genial, but what do you make of these falsehoods? Ed says: Ronald, in my view John Harbaugh has actually been quite good with the media. He…

title: NY Giants news: Tremaine Edmunds reportedly headed to IR, special teams issues, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get set to battle the Houston Texans this Sunday. Struggles in all three phases leave Giants feeling heat heading into matchup at Texans | The Athletic The New York Giants’ coaching staff turned up the heat this week. […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as the Giants get set to battle the Houston Texans this Sunday. Struggles in all three phases leave Giants feeling heat heading into matchup at Texans | The Athletic The New York Giants’ coaching staff turned up the heat this week. It started after Sunday’s 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints when coach John Harbaugh challenged someone from a disappointing backfield to step up and seize the top running back job. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy noted that the coaches need to look inward as the team searches for solutions to their weaknesses. One area that falls under the coaches’ purview is penalties. The Giants have been flagged for the 13th-most penalties in the league. They have the most pre-snap offensive penalties, lowlighted by consecutive false starts on running back Tyrone Tracy and left tackle Andrew Thomas to turn a third-and-8 into a third-and-18 in the third quarter against the Saints. Giants’ Matt Nagy ready to open up playbook for J.J. McCarthy’s first start | New York Post “Maybe now 20 percent of that 30 that was gone is back,” Nagy said. “For us, what does he do well? You’ve seen some of the packages he’s done, but that can become predictable. We don’t want to be predictable. Now that he’s the starter, it probably benefits us some that he’s just not always coming in to do predictable QB-driven runs.” “Just the confidence of him being able to, in practice, talk to us about the scheme, where his eyes are going in the pass game, where he’s snapping the ball with a motion or a shift,” Nagy said. “If there was a shoestring with Jameis or he got hurt, he could go in and function. Whereas the first two weeks, I had a highlighted [play] call sheet that, if something happened and he was in, these were the plays. It was probably 50 percent. Last week, it was probably 90 percent. Now this week, it’s going to be 100 percent.” Harbs Weekly: A chance to take control of the division before the bye week | Giants.com Q: A lot of times we see quarterback changes made at the bye week, which is coming up. But if something is inevitable, is it best to do it as soon as possible because now you get this week too? Harbaugh: I just never thought of it that way. I never considered whether the bye week is coming up and that’d be a better time. To be honest with you, it never even crossed my mind. I’m just thinking about what was the best thing for the next game and was he ready. It really wasn’t all that. I mean, it’s good to think about. Now that people have brought it up, I’m like, I didn’t really care about that. Harbaugh on the release of Najee Harris John Harbaugh explains why the Giants cut Najee Harris: "It was more about, 'Alright, we're going to set a course.' It's hard to carry four backs. I just felt like, in this situation…nothing against what he did." https://t.co/8CPrezderd pic.twitter.com/HWW5OMtF4B — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 23, 2026 Cam Skattebo set to return to Giants RB mix after being ‘ taught a lesson’ | ESPN.com “It’s been good, you know. I think I got taught a lesson,” Skattebo said. “I don’t know if that’s from them or from myself, but I kind of had to step back and look at it and figure out why I was doing the things I was doing, what was happening. Came to practice, corrected those things, worked on them. Ready to go back out there and play ball.” The second-year running back knows he still has to prove it on the field. “I didn’t do anything yet,” Skattebo said. “I took care of the ball during practice, and whatever my role is on Sunday is going to be my role and I’m going to give it everything I’ve got.” Colts’ Jonathan Taylor to Giants? Why Cam Skattebo knows he shouldn’t rule it out | NJ.com Giants coach John Harbaugh wants a dominant, single-back running game, as he chases an unlikely NFC East title this season. Really, that also is Harbaugh’s broader vision for his offense in East Rutherford. So Cam Skattebo — who entered his second year as the Giants’ much-hyped but largely unproven No. 1 back — knows he can’t and shouldn’t rule out Harbaugh trading for the Colts’ Jonathan Taylor (a New Jersey native) prior to the Nov. 10 deadline. New York Giants’ skill players call for improved run-game execution | USAToday.com Nabers said the offense must do a better job establishing the run so defenses cannot simply play the pass on every down. “Yeah, I mean, we’ve got to do a better job on offense of getting the ball — I mean, making sure we want to run the ball well, finding good runs for the running back that just hearing their thoughts on what runs that they like, too,” Nabers told reporters on Thursday. “Trying to do a better job of asking them, asking the O-line of what specific runs that they like, where they feel like we can gain a lot of yards off of to just help the whole offense.” Interesting stats since the change at center Giants center comparison after 3 starts each: ⚫️Giants RBs averaged more yards per carry (3.69) behind John Michael Schmitz in Weeks 1-3 than they did in Weeks 4-6 behind Bryan Hudson (3.1) (my data) ⚫️Schmitz's QB pressure percentage (6.2%) is lower than Hudson's (7.1%), too,… — Pat Leonard (@PLeonardNYDN) October 22, 2026 The 10 best NFL player matchups to watch in Week 7 | PFF New York Giants WR Malik Nabers vs. Houston Texans CB Derek Stingley Jr. Nabers hasn’t taken long to already look as sharp as ever after tearing his ACL. His 81.7 overall PFF grade is the 10th-best among qualified wideouts, and his 23 first downs secured are tied for sixth. The third-year pro has also produced 2.88-plus yards per route run in three games, including in Week 6 against the Saints. The 2026 season has not been a lockdown one yet for Stingley. The All-Pro has permitted a 101.8 passer rating into his coverage — the 15th-worst among qualified cornerbacks — allowing 40 or more yards in three of his six outings. On top of that, Stingley’s 16.1 yards per reception given up are the fourth-highest at his position. The Texans have primarily played zone coverage in 2026, which may lend the upper hand to Nabers. His 78.3 PFF receiving grade against such softer looks is the sixth-best among receivers with 12 or more targets in zone. Meanwhile, Stingley ranks as the 26th-graded corner in zone with a 66.1 PFF coverage grade. They also signed linebacker Jaden Keller to the active roster and elevated offensive tackle Brant Banks and linebacker Troy Reeder from the practice squad. Kiko Mauigoa is a 23 year old, 6” 2”, 233 pound second year linebacker out of the University of Miami. He played just 26 snaps this season, all on special teams, without registering any stats. Brant Banks is a 26 year old, 307 pound second year offensive tackle out of Rice. He was signed as an undrafted free agent by the Green Bay Packers in 2025 and played two games for them last year, playing a total of six snaps for the Packers, all on special teams. The Packers released Banks in August, 2026 and the Jets signed him to the practice squad. He has yet to play a snap in the NFL in 2026. Troy Reeder is a 32 year old, 6’ 3”, 245 pound linebacker out of Delaware. He was originally signed as an undrafted free agent in 2019 by the Los Angeles Rams. Reeder spent his entire NFL career with the Rams through the 2025 season. In July 2026 the Detroit Lions signed Reeder, and he was with the Lions through their 2026 training camp before the Lions released him prior to the start of the 2026 season. Reeder was signed to the Jets practiced squad in early September and has been elevated to the active roster a couple of times since then. Reeder has played 85 snaps in four games with the Jets, all on special teams. He has recorded four tackles this season. Jaden Keller is a 23 year old, 6’ 3”, 235 pound linebacker out of Virginia Tech. He went undrafted in 2026 and the Jets signed him as an undrafted free agent before releasing him prior to the start of the regular season and adding him to the practice squad. Keller made his NFL debut three weeks ago when the Jets elevated him from the practice squad. In three games with the Jets Keller has played 60 snaps, all on special teams, and recorded one tackle.

title: Three Things I’m Looking at in the Jets vs. Dolphins Game
summary: Another Sunday, another Jets game every fan dubs “must-win.” I understand that we’re trying to watch competitive Jets football, but I think you guys are really misusing and abusing that term. The fanbase is usually toxic, but this year has been especially tiring to see all the flip-flopping from week to week depending on the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 07: De'Von Achane #28 of the Miami Dolphins carries the ball for a touchdown against the New York Jets during the first quarter at MetLife Stadium on December 07, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images Another Sunday, another Jets game every fan dubs “must-win.” I understand that we’re trying to watch competitive Jets football, but I think you guys are really misusing and abusing that term. The fanbase is usually toxic, but this year has been especially tiring to see all the flip-flopping from week to week depending on the game’s result. Fun fact: the Jets can lose this game and still make the playoffs. The Jets can win this game 40-0 and still miss the playoffs. That’s not to say this game is unimportant; I’m just trying (failing) to cleanse my eyes and ears of the “must-win” narrative every week. My favorite NFL team is facing my least favorite NFL team, and I’m hoping to see a thrashing. Good teams beat bad teams; I think we all know this. It may be less apparent, however, that good teams almost always have winning records against their division. It’s the easiest way to beef up your record: six guaranteed games every year against an opponent you know. Unfortunately, Aaron Glenn is 0-7 in such games. The previous Head Coach, Robert Saleh, was also 0-6 in his first year with the Jets, but in his first AFC East game, he thrashed the Dolphins 40-17 in what was the Jets’ first win by multiple scores in over two seasons at that point. These talented Jets have already won by multiple scores this year, so that monkey isn’t on their back, but the last time the Jets beat a divisional opponent was Aaron Rodgers’s swan song against the Dolphins in Week 18 of the 2024 season. These Jets and Dolphins look totally different today than they did in that matchup, but the indisputable truth is that the 2026 Jets have more talent on both sides of the ball than the 2026 Dolphins. Perhaps that’s why you feel this is a must-win? I wonder if the Rams had that same energy last week, knowing they were much more talented than the Arizona Cardinals, who eliminated me in my Survivor Pool. The Jets should win – let’s expect a win. I’ll be the first to admit, though, that I won’t be surprised if Miami gets their first win this week. Coaching is the most underappreciated aspect of winning, and I think we can all agree that the Jets’ coaching hasn’t been up to par. Whether you blame a coordinator or the head coach is up to you, but we all agree there’s plenty of room for improvement. Can Jeff Hafley finally win his first game in six tries, now that he’s finally facing a struggling coaching staff instead of the likes of Andy Reid, Kyle Shanahan, and Kevin O’Connell? Let’s discuss: The Return (Part II) I was so excited last week to see Omar Cooper Jr. return to the lineup after an electric first drive in Week 1. I started last week’s three things with my excitement, and I was so curious to see how he’d be used. He exceeded my most optimistic predictions with six catches, 103 yards, and one touchdown on seven targets. He was easily the most productive WR on the field and rightfully earned Rookie of the Week honors. This week we’ll have the pleasure of seeing Adonai Mitchell back on the field for the Jets. I’m not sure a 100-yard game is in his immediate future, but he’s had 60+ yards in both of his healthy games this season and reportedly has chemistry with Geno Smith that dates back to the summer. For the first time since the first drive of the season, Frank Reich will have his original WR trio of Wilson, Mitchell, and Cooper Jr. on the field at the same time. If there was ever a time to unleash the playbook and all the plans they’ve had for months, this would be it. With Breece Hall possibly back, the sky truly becomes the limit. This offense is overflowing with playmakers, with multiple options at each skill position who can take over a game. In five games, Miami has allowed 24 or more points four times. In those four games, all four opposing QBs threw for at least two touchdowns, and the fifth (Kyler Murray) had 247 yards with no turnovers. It’s worth noting Murray was without his top option, Justin Jefferson, for this game. Geno Smith and Frank Reich will have every player at their disposal, a full-strength roster to try to dominate this barren Miami defense. The only game this season the Jets have scored 24+ points or had Geno throw multiple touchdowns was the 31-24 loss in Detroit, which fired up the fanbase about the Jets’ offensive potential. The Jets haven’t even surpassed 20 points since, 4th worst in the league during this span. Simply put, there’s no excuse to not turn it around this Sunday. Against a team that regularly surrenders 24 points and 2+ pass touchdowns, I’m expecting these Jets to score 24 points and throw 2+ pass touchdowns. A big part of Geno’s sole performance of this nature was Kenyon Sadiq’s seven-catch, 103-yard game, capped by a beautiful horizontal TD. He has three catches for 15 yards in the three games since (avg. 1 catch for 5 yds per game). The Dolphins have been especially leaky to tight ends, surrendering touchdowns to George Kittle, Travis Kelce, Mike Gesicki, and Tanner Hudson. The other tight ends they faced were Michael Mayer (who led his team in catches and targets) and T.J. Hockenson, who turned back the clock with 13 catches and 119 yards against the Dolphins. That’s more catches and yards than he has in all his other games combined ! In his other four games played, he has 10 catches and 83 yards. 24 points. 2+ pass touchdowns. Adonai Mitchell yards. Kenyon Sadiq (or Mason Taylor) touchdown. Wow, maybe we should do a parlay? Road Block If the Miami Dolphins have any hope of winning, they’ll need to run the ball. This is their greatest strength to date: they’re currently 8th in the NFL in rushing yards per game (126.6) and 5th-highest in yards per attempt (4.9). The issue is that they fall behind so early that they have to abandon the run and try to make up ground in the passing game. Do you see why the Jets might be the perfect “get right” game for them? Facing a team that hasn’t scored more than seven points in the first half since Week 1 vs. the Titans is a great way to keep hammering Plan A and potentially even win the time-of-possession battle. They might not have to abandon the rushing game and can use it to keep the Jets offense off the field. Malik Willis already threw for a Justin Fields-esque 85 passing yards on a 52.5% completion percentage against the Vikings, but that was surprisingly the closest they came to a win, thanks to 100 yards and a touchdown from Ollie Gordon II. Gordon has scored in each of the last three games and is averaging 76.3 rushing yards per game during that time. The Jets were destroyed by Chicago RB Kyle Monangai for 146 yards and 2 scores, just allowed random Patriots RB Corey Kiner to average 5.2 ypc on 11 carries last week, and I won’t mention the acts of Jahmyr Gibbs in Week 3. If I’m Jeff Hafley, the blueprint is clear: use Willis and Gordon’s legs to move the ball downfield, ice the Jets offense, and put up points after excruciatingly long drives. Of course, the Jets can end this by finally being the explosive offense they are on paper, but if not, what can the defense do to stop the run game? They allow the 10th most rushing yards per game (123) in the league, and outside of Gibbs, they haven’t even faced the toughest running backs on the schedule yet. James Cook twice, Kenneth Walker(!!), Ashton Jeanty; there will be plenty of mountains to climb in the future. Can they climb this hill named Ollie Gordon II? The same guy who ran 100 yards on the 5th-best run defense, the Minnesota Vikings. 2-Minute Warning Let us not forget it was a little writer named James Wudi who pointed out the ineptitude at 2-minute execution on this incredible site before CBS put up an equally damning graphic about getting…

title: Previewing the Jets’ opposition: Miami Dolphins
summary: The Miami Dolphins has won six out of the last seven, 10 of the last 12 and 14 of the last 17 against the New York Jets. However, they enter Sunday’s clash at MetLife Stadium as a winless underdog. Let’s break down the Dolphins’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks The Dolphins had a strange […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 07: Jordyn Brooks #20 of the Miami Dolphins in action during the NFL 2025 game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on December 07, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey."" (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins has won six out of the last seven, 10 of the last 12 and 14 of the last 17 against the New York Jets. However, they enter Sunday’s clash at MetLife Stadium as a winless underdog. Let’s break down the Dolphins’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks The Dolphins had a strange approach to the offseason, primarily heading into a rebuild as they traded guys away and looked to shed salary. This is a team that had six pro bowlers in 2023, but now all six are off the team. However, they coupled that approach with the signing of the biggest prize in this year’s free agent quarterback market when they signed Malik Willis to a three-year deal. Willis is getting a chance to be a full-time starter for the first time and he’s had mixed results due to the lack of a supporting cast around him. So far, he’s completed just 56 percent of his passes with two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and four interceptions. The backup to Willis is Kyle McCord, who has never thrown an NFL pass. Offensive Line Despite making so many other changes, Miami retained most of their offensive line and built on the foundation already in place by drafting Kadyn Proctor in the first round and putting him into the starting line-up at left guard. The rest of their starters were all also starting for them last year, although former first round right tackle Austin Jackson only started the first game and the last five due to injuries. The other three starters are center Aaron Brewer, left tackle Patrick Paul and right guard Jonah Savaiinaea. Savaiinaea struggled badly as a second round rookie last season and he was knocked out of the last game due to injury with Jarrett Kingston filling in for him the rest of the way. Miami’s starting tackles have given up five sacks and eight penalties between them so far this season. The other backups include Andrew Meyer – who started a game at center last year – and sixth round rookie DJ Campbell. Chukwuebuka Godrick and Caedan Wallace round out this group. Running Backs Miami’s plans for the year further shifted towards rebuild mode when they lost their star running back De’Von Achane to a torn ACL early in the season. The starter is now Ollie Gordon II, who – to his credit – is averaging five yards per carry with three rushing touchdowns. Jaylen Wright is the main backup, but Miami also has rookie Kaytron Allen as the number three. Allen was drafted in the sixth round by the Commanders but did not make their roster. Another rookie, the undrafted DJ Herman, is also on the roster as a fullback. Pass catchers With Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle now gone, Miami is hoping that Malik Washington can develop into a true number one receiver. He has 29 touches in the first five games, but less than 300 yards and no touchdowns. Tight end Greg Dulcich is the only other Dolphins player with double digits in catches. In order to find Willis some passing game weapons, Miami went pass catcher heavy in the middle rounds of the draft. Receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas were selected along with tight end Will Kacmarek in the third round and then another receiver, Kevin Coleman, and another tight end, Seydou Traore, were picked in the fifth. Out of all of these, the Jets may view Bell as the biggest threat as they had Malik McClain operating as him during the week on the scout team, presumably in an effort to try and replicate his combination of size and athleticism. Bell had a nice game against the Chiefs with four catches but otherwise only has two other touches all year. Those two touches gained 25 and 26 yards though, so he may be a chunk play threat. Douglas is also a threat. He caught five passes for 94 yards in his NFL debut in the opener, but then got hurt in week two and hasn’t played since. He’ll make his return on Sunday. Further depth comes from receivers Jalen Tolbert and Jared Wayne, and from tight end Justin Joly. Defensive Line Miami’s defense got a boost in the game before the bye week with the return of last year’s first round pick Kenneth Grant at defensive tackle. Grant had been dealing with a toe issue but should now see his playing time increase alongside Zach Sieler. Sieler has been a thorn in the side of the Jets for several years with eight sacks in his past six games against them. Miami has won 10 of 12 games over the Jets with Sieler in the line-up. With Grant out, Jordan Phillips and Zeek Biggers had been sharing the workload alongside Sieler, who has a team-high two sacks. Miami’s best edge rusher is Chop Robinson, but the former first rounder’s production has been inconsistent. He had three sacks in four games towards the end of last year but only has one in five since then. The other starter on the edge is Josh Uche with Malik Herring as the main backup. Robert Beal Jr. and undrafted rookie Rodney McGraw are also on the roster, but Beal has been listed as doubtful with a hamstring issue. Linebackers At linebacker, Miami is getting excellent production from their second round pick, Jacob Rodriguez, who has 57 tackles and an interception in his first five NFL games. Rodriguez starts alongside last year’s leading tackler, Jordyn Brooks, with Willie Gay also getting plenty of reps. Gay is questionable with an illness, but did return to practice on Friday. Shaka Heyward and Jackson Woodard are the other backups with fourth round pick Trey Moore on injured reserve. Defensive Backs Miami’s depth is slightly compromised in the secondary, as fourth round safety Kyle Louis and veteran safety Ronnie Harrison are both on injured reserve. In addition, cornerback Darrell Baker remains on the PUP list. Louis did return to practice this week so could be activated for Sunday. He’s officially questionable. The starters right now at safety are Dante Trader Jr. and fifth round rookie Michael Taaffe. Trader leads the team with three pass breakups but the rookies Taaffe and Rodriguez have been inconsistent tacklers, combing for 14 missed tackles in the first five games. At cornerback, the top three are JuJu Brents, Jason Marshall Jr. and Chris Johnson. The first round rookie Johnson has been the primary slot corner. Brents leads the team with four defensive penalties. Further depth comes from safeties Zayne Anderson and Julius Wood, and cornerbacks Marcellas Dial and Reese Taylor, although Taylor has been ruled out due to injury. Miami also has former Jet Jaylin Simpson, who can play safety or corner. Special Teams The Dolphins just made a change at placekicker with another ex-Jet, Riley Patterson, having been released earlier this week after missing three kicks in five games. Zane Gonzalez was added to the practice squad to take over from Patterson. The veteran Bradley Pinion is the Dolphins’ punter, but his net average is below 40 yards per punt so far this year. In the return game, Washington is dangerous but hasn’t done much this year as his focus has shifted more onto the offense. Wright, who is listed as the backup kickoff returner, had a 79-yard return earlier this season. Coleman is listed as the backup punt returner. The Dolphins also recently released wide receiver Ryan Miller, who had been a primary gunner. Simpson and Dial would be options to handle this role on Sunday. So far this year Woodard and Simpson have been productive in coverage.

(Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! If the Eagles go 0-3 in three straight division games coming up to drop to 2-7 overall, it’ll be safe to say the season is over … if it’s not already. If the Eagles reach that point, it’s hard not to think Howie Roseman will be selling. But it’s hard to envision a full on fire sale. He’s not going to trade players unless the price is right. Roob’s Observations: Why a Howie Roseman trade deadline sell-off is unlikely – NBCSP WHY MAJOR HOWIE MOVES ARE UNLIKELY: I keep hearing about all the players Howie is going to unload before the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10. Guys like Saquon Barkley, Moro Ojomo, Zack Baun, Riq Woolen, Landon Dickerson and Dallas Goedert. Basically, older players who may not fit into the Eagles’ future or players on the final year of their contract situation who may be unsignable. Don’t count on it. While a sell-off is possible if this thing continues to spiral, there’s two important things to remember. First of all, you’re never going to trade a player for less or equal what he might bring you in the comp pick equation. Moro Ojomo for example is probably going to bring you a 3 rd -round comp pick and you’re not going to get a 2 nd -rounder for him. Howie Roseman values picks the same whether they’re a year later, so he’d rather have a comp 3 rd -round pick in 2028 than a 4 th -round pick in 2027. The second thing to remember is that in the current NFC East landscape, there’s a chance the Eagles will still be in the playoff race when the trade deadline arrives on Nov. 10. They have the Cowboys, Commanders and Giants before the deadline, combined record 6-10-1. And 0-7-1 vs. teams with a winning record. So as grim as things look right now, they look just as grim for everyone else in the division, and if the Eagles win two of these next three Howie isn’t going to start selling off pieces at 4-5. He owes it to Jeff Lurie and the players and coaches and the city to keep the team intact if the Eagles are in contact with the division leaders. And the way things are going, it’s going to be hard not to be. Nobody likes to make trades more than Howie. But he likes to be in the playoffs even more. And he’s not going to unload any significant pieces while the Eagles still have any chance to win the division. Eagles Film Preview: Cowboys offense surprisingly difficult to project – BGN The Cowboys were a surprisingly difficult offense to break down this week. I watched the Texans game and saw an offense that could protect its quarterback and find plenty of ways to get the ball to its best players. Then I watched the Packers game and wondered where all of that had gone. This is still a talented offense, and I can’t shake the feeling that it will come together at some point. However, I thought the Cowboys were more creative last year, and their coaching staff isn’t getting enough from this group right now. With everything going on with the Eagles’ offense, the defense needs to play well if this team has any chance. There are opportunities to disrupt the Cowboys, but there is also enough talent here to make this a very uncomfortable matchup. Five Eagles thoughts: Jalen Hurts’ future, Tanner McKee’s present, and exploring a trade-deadline selling scenario – PHLY Eagles Saquon Barkley: This is possibly the trickiest one. There’s a compelling argument for getting value for Barkley if the season truly goes sideways. He’s 29 years old and still the type of player a real contender would likely view as the final piece for a title push. Do the Eagles view him as an important part of a potential turnaround in 2028 and beyond? He’s under contract through 2029 if so, but getting out of a significant investment at the running back position makes some sense to me. I’d say yes, but certainly not for a discount. Dallas Goedert: Leaning yes. He’s only under contract through this season and has been seeking a better deal for multiple years now. If a contending team offers an early-Day-3 pick, wouldn’t it make sense to clear the way for Eli Stowers to get some developmental snaps? NFL Week 7 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more – ESPN Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers — Tanner McKee, QB, Philadelphia Eagles (4.6%). McKee is an intriguing sleeper with quarterback Jalen Hurts out for the season (blood clots). He threw for 215 yards and a touchdown against the Panthers last week and now faces a Cowboys defense that has allowed 21.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks (fifth most in the league). Dallas has also given up 11 passing touchdowns this season. McKee attempted 45 passes last week, and he has the targets to reach the end zone with DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert (both questionable to play). He’s worth considering in deeper single-QB leagues and as a QB2 in superflex formats. NFL Week 7 picks: Upset and score predictions, matchup breakdowns for every game – NFL.com Why Bobby picked the Cowboys: Because Dallas simply has to win. The Eagles surely feel the same way, but they aren’t nearly as close to full strength as the Cowboys — and probably won’t be for the rest of the season now that Jalen Hurts is out due to blood clots. For as bad as the past two weeks have been for the Cowboys, they feel like a safer pick to turn things around in a division that is wide open. Dallas has been disappointing, but the Eagles have been in such disarray during the month of October that offensive lineman Jordan Mailata reflected on Week 5 as the “week from hell,” only to realize midweek last week that he “might have jumped the gun” describing it as such after problems continued to pile up. Since then, the Eagles lost their fourth straight and the aforementioned news on Hurts dropped, so be on the lookout for Mailata’s latest re-evaluation of how low things can go. In a battle between Tanner McKee and Dak Prescott, I choose Prescott, who is due for a turnaround performance. He’s too good and surrounded by too many weapons to stay in a rut. Considering the Commanders are on a bye and the Giants are facing a resurgent Texans squad, the NFC East’s winless stretch could very well run from Oct. 5 through Oct. 25, rectified at long last by Dallas in prime time. From Cowboy to Eagle, Joe Milton III finds himself on the other side of the rivalry – PhiladelphiaEagles.com “I definitely learned a lot over there,” Milton said. “Development-wise, it’s going great. It’s amazing. I love to learn. Taking notes again and learning the new offense.” Part of the Cowboys’ practice squad this year, Milton was surprised when his agent called him before practicing last week and said that the Eagles wanted to sign him. “Just because it is a rivalry and it was just like, ‘Dang, no way.’ My agent called me and mentioned it to me. … I went to practice like it was a normal day and tried to operate under a Dallas Cowboy at the time,” Milton said. ”I went home, but really when I got in my car, everything’s just changed. I was just like, ‘What am I going to do? Am I going to stay on the practice squad or should I show up for my opportunity?’ I’m here.” NFLPA has yet to launch “full investigation” of Jalen Hurts situation – PFT Hurts has a potential lawsuit against the doctors who provided his care, independent of any more limited rights against the Eagles or the league. While it could get complicated — especially if Hurts may have to file a lawsuit in the U.S. and in England — a “superficial” blood clot in his leg resulting from being cleated during the Week 4 game against the Rams became a deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in each lung. It’s fair for…

full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: DeVonta Smith #6, Makai Lemon #9, and Dontayvion Wicks #13 of the Philadelphia Eagles look on against the Carolina Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their third and final injury report of the week on Saturday in advance of their Week 7 Monday Night Football game against the Dallas Cowboys. The Eagles ruled four players OUT: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Nolan Smith, and Michael Carter II. Smith missed practice all week due to a hamstring injury while Wicks missed practice all week due to an ankle injury. The Eagles being without their top two wide receivers certainly isn’t ideal. The team will roll with Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore, Hollywood Brown, and Britain Covey. The Cowboys’ defense is so bad that these players could still have chances to succeed on Monday night. Smith missed practice all week while in the concussion protocol. He might be able to return in Week 8. Carter II has been unavailable since getting injured in Week 5. The Eagles will go with Andrew Mukuba and Cooper DeJean as their top two safeties in base packages with Kenny Moore playing on the back end of the defense in nickel formations. The Eagles ruled seven players QUESTIONABLE: Saquon Barkley, Landon Dickerson, Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Eli Stowers, Grant Calcaterra, and Jakorian Bennett. Barkley was full go on Saturday after being limited on Thursday and Friday. It sure seems like he’s going to give it a go on Monday night. Dickerson was a full participant in Saturday’s practice. Seems like the Eagles will activate him from injured reserve to start at left guard. If so, it will be interesting to see how he fares after he really did not look great in Week 1. Greenard did not practice on Friday or Saturday after being listed as limited on Thursday. He talked about being a game-time decision. Even if Greenard does suit up, he’ll likely be on a pitch count. Not great. Hunt was limited in practice all week. With the Eagles looking thin at edge rusher, it would be nice if he can play. We’ll see. The Eagles have until 4:00 PM Eastern on Monday to activate any or all of Dickerson, Stowers, Calcaterra, and Bennett from injured reserve in order to play against the Cowboys. The team has some open roster spots to fill, so, we’ll see how they handle things. Players notably listed without a game status : Dallas Goedert, Drew Kendall, Zack Baun, Hollywood Brown, Jihaad Campbell, Jalen Carter, Britain Covey, Jordan Davis, Arnold Ebiketie, A.J. Epenesa, Fred Johnson, Willie Lampkin, Moro Ojomo, and Tyler Steen. All of these players were listed on the injury report this week. Goedert was full go on Saturday after not practicing on Thursday and Friday. With DeVonta and Wicks out, at least Tanner McKee will have the Eagles’ top tight end available to him. Kendall is set to return to the starting lineup after missing two games. The starting offensive line will look like: LT Jordan Mailata, LG Landon Dickerson (or Willie Lampkin), C Drew Kendall, RG Tyler Steen, RT Markel Bell. With Nolan Smith out and both Greenard and Hunt questionable, the Eagles only have two edge rushers sure to play on Monday: Ebiketie and Epenesa. title: Eagles Film Preview: Cowboys offense surprisingly difficult to project
summary: Each week, I’ll publish two film-room previews: one focusing on the offense and one on the defense. These are primarily film-based, focusing on the schemes, tendencies, and matchups that could shape Sunday’s game, with all statistics coming from the Fantasy Points Data Suite. I also record a video version for Patreon, where I break down […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 05: CeeDee Lamb #88 of the Dallas Cowboys drops a pass as Quinyon Mitchell #27 of the Philadelphia Eagles defends during the second half of an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 5, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Each week, I’ll publish two film-room previews: one focusing on the offense and one on the defense. These are primarily film-based, focusing on the schemes, tendencies, and matchups that could shape Sunday’s game, with all statistics coming from the Fantasy Points Data Suite . I also record a video version for Patreon , where I break down the plays in greater detail and where you can further support my work. The Cowboys were a surprisingly difficult offense to break down this week. I watched the Texans game and saw an offense that could protect its quarterback and find plenty of ways to get the ball to its best players. Then I watched the Packers game and wondered where all of that had gone. This is still a talented offense, and I can’t shake the feeling that it will come together at some point. However, I thought the Cowboys were more creative last year, and their coaching staff isn’t getting enough from this group right now. With everything going on with the Eagles’ offense, the defense needs to play well if this team has any chance. There are opportunities to disrupt the Cowboys, but there is also enough talent here to make this a very uncomfortable matchup. Pass Game Everything starts with CeeDee Lamb. He remains an outstanding receiver, and the Cowboys are using him outside more frequently this season. He has aligned outside on approximately 61% of passing snaps, but that doesn’t mean he stays in one spot or runs a limited selection of routes. Against the Texans, Lamb caught 17 of his 21 targets (!) for 189 yards and a touchdown, with 72 yards coming after the catch. His targeted routes included outs, hitches, screens, crossers, a corner, a post, and several other concepts. They found him underneath, across the field, and at intermediate depth. That version of this offense is difficult to defend because Lamb can win in so many different ways. The Eagles cannot treat him as the responsibility of one cornerback. Some snaps will have him outside against an Eagles corner, while others will have him move inside and test the communication between the nickel, linebackers, and safeties. After some of the communication problems we have seen from the Eagles recently, that worries me. Lamb is too good at finding space to give him free releases into areas nobody has properly accounted for. Cowboys’ Offense All22 Thread. 1) They have been disappointing by their standards, but I still think they have the talent to be very good. CeeDee Lamb plays outside a lot this year (highest rate of his career), and he is as good as ever. Dak hasn't played well the past 2 weeks,… pic.twitter.com/H64VwO6BVU — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 23, 2026 The Cowboys are a true 11-personnel shotgun offense. In some ways, watching them feels like going back five years, before seemingly every offense started building around condensed formations, constant motion, and an extensive under-center package. They use 11 personnel on 73.3% of their snaps, the third-highest rate in the league, and they want to spread the defense out and let Dak Prescott distribute the football. Their pass rate over expectation leads the league, and they throw on approximately 68% of first-and-10 situations. This passing game is the foundation of the offense. Their route combinations have a strong vertical element, even though much of Prescott’s production comes on shorter throws. They want receivers to push defenders downfield, create space underneath, and force the secondary to communicate. Lamb’s presence can also open opportunities for others. In the example below, the attention he receives helps Jake Ferguson escape downfield on a wheel route. Ferguson hasn’t produced much yardage this season, but the Eagles still need to account for him when their attention shifts toward the receivers. 2) This is a true 11-personnel shotgun offense. It feels like a throwback to what every offense ran 5 years ago. You can see the attention that Lamb draws here, and Ferguson sneaks out on the wheel route downfield. They want to spread the defense out, throw on 1st down, and… pic.twitter.com/x7S9GexETf — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 23, 2026 Prescott hasn’t played particularly well over the past two weeks, but I still think he is a very good quarterback. His understanding of the position shows up in the small details. He can identify favorable matchups before the snap, manipulate underneath defenders, and create throwing windows with his eyes and body position. If the Eagles show him exactly what they intend to play, he is capable of picking them apart. The empty formation example below is excellent. Prescott shapes his body as though he is throwing the short route to the flat, draws the cornerback forward, and then hits the corner route behind him. George Pickens finishes the play by showing his ability to elevate and attack the football. Pickens hasn’t been at his very best this season, but he is an outstanding second receiver who can win vertically even when the coverage is competitive. He has aligned outside on approximately 93% of passing snaps, and in the film I watched, he usually lined up to the left. The Eagles have to respect his ability to finish at the catch point when deciding how much coverage to send toward Lamb. 3) Dak is still a high-level pre-snap QB, and if you don't confuse your coverages, he can throw it all over the place. Here they are in empty, so the defense expects the short route to the flat, but Dak uses his body position to fake the short throw, drawing up the flat… pic.twitter.com/DU6j7ADh5c — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 23, 2026 How aggressively should Vic Fangio pressure Prescott? This is where the contrast between the games becomes fascinating. The Packers had considerable success attacking the Cowboys’ protections, but their season-long numbers still suggest caution. The Cowboys rank eighth in EPA against the blitz at +0.13 per play. Prescott usually understands where his answers are and gets the football out quickly enough to punish defenses for removing players from coverage. Personally, I would be selective. If Fangio brings pressure, the disguise needs to be convincing, and the rush needs to arrive quickly. I wouldn’t want linebackers starting from depth and announcing a delayed pressure that Prescott has time to recognize. The Eagles need to threaten the protection, make him uncertain about who is coming, and close off the immediate answer. Simply sending an extra defender and hoping for the best could leave Lamb or Pickens with a very favorable opportunity. 4) It's hard to know how to play the Cowboys' offense because the Packers had a lot of success blitzing Dak. However, historically (and for most of this season), I would be very cautious about blitzing Dak a lot. As I said above, Dak is a veteran QB who is excellent at getting… pic.twitter.com/chs8EIhIKG — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 23, 2026 The Packers showed that Prescott can still be caught out by coverage rotation. Jonathan Gannon, of all people, did an excellent job disguising the picture and getting Prescott to throw into coverage he hadn’t properly confirmed. On the interception below, the weak safety drops into the throwing window, but Prescott commits to the post without accounting for him. It is a good defensive disguise and a poor decision by the quarterback. That is the balance with Prescott. He is experienced and technically excellent, but he will still attempt difficult throws over the middle and give defenders opportunities to make plays. His completion percentage falls from 75% when kept clean to 47.4% under pressure, while his yards per attempt drops from 7.6 to 4.6.…

summary: Given the Eagles’ current disposition, it feels like we might already be looking ahead to the offseason. With the NFL Draft being a never-ending source of hope for the future, there is good reason to watch college football every weekend for the rest of the season. Here are some players I’m keeping a close eye […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA OCTOBER 17: Darian Mensah #10 of the Miami Hurricanes celebrates with fans after teammate Malachi Toney scores a touchdown against the Florida State Seminoles at Hard Rock Stadium on October 17, 2026, in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Michael Pimentel/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Given the Eagles’ current disposition, it feels like we might already be looking ahead to the offseason. With the NFL Draft being a never-ending source of hope for the future, there is good reason to watch college football every weekend for the rest of the season. Here are some players I’m keeping a close eye on this week. All listed times Eastern . Darian Mensah, Quarterback, Miami v. Pittsburgh (12 PM on ESPN): It is highly possible, if not likely, that the Eagles will be in the quarterback market this spring. If they are, this is a great class to need a quarterback in. For my money, Darian Mensah has emerged as the QB1 in this group midway through this season. Mensah, on his third team in three years, has gotten better every season as a quarterback. He is decisive with a strong arm and great accuracy. Last week was the first time he and Miami faced any adversity all season and Mensah responded by delivering in the clutch to keep the Canes unbeaten. Pittsburgh is a feisty squad that has a great habit of pulling off upsets. Mensah will need to stay locked in to keep his Heisman campaign afloat and Miami unbeaten. Kingston Lopa, Safety, Cal v. SMU (12 PM on CW): If the East Coast could stay up a bit later, Kingston Lopa would be a household name. He has linebacker build at 6’5” and 210 pounds but he moves and covers like a safety. With five interceptions midway through the season, Lopa is one of the best playmaking defenders in the country. SMU’s offense has big play potential on any snap, meaning Lopa will need to be at his best against the pass and the run. KJ Duff, Wide Receiver, Rutgers v. Northwestern (12 PM on Peacock): The best receiver in the country not named Jeremiah or Malachi might be in New Brunswick, New Jersey. KJ Duff is massive at 6’6” and 225 pounds. His size allows him to dominate above the rim, but he is a great athlete that can separate downfield. If he played in a more stable offense, Duff would be a household name outside of the Northeast. Duff is coming off a dominant game where nine catches and two scores helped Rutgers beat Maryland in a rivalry game. Now he faces a much tougher test in Northwestern. Can he stay hot and show everyone he can ball out on a bigger stage? Greg Johnson, Guard, Minnesota v. Iowa (3:30 PM on FS1): Let’s talk big boys. The Eagles need ‘em and college football has ‘em. Greg Johnson is a massive, mauling guard for a scrappy Minnesota offense this year. Now the Golden Gophers have a shot at taking down a ranked Iowa squad. Johnson will have his hands full with a physical Iowa defensive line, but he can further prove himself as one of the best linemen in the country. Wayshawn Parker, Running Back, Utah v. Houston (10:15 PM on ESPN): Another Eagles need is getting younger and more explosive in their backfield. While Howie Roseman has never valued running backs enough to draft them higher than the second round, Wayshawn Parker strikes me as a Day Two player who could come in and contribute immediately. Parker has a strong blend of toughness, vision, and explosiveness. He was underutilized in the Utah passing game through his first two years, but has really shown out as a true three down back in his junior season. He’s a do-it-all player who will get to show out against a tough Houston team this weekend.

title: Steelers vs. Saints: Week 7 game picks
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers will kickoff the Week 7 Sunday slate with the NFL’s first game in Paris when they take on the New Orleans Saints. Pittsburgh is coming off its biggest fourth-quarter comeback win in 34 years in a win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and the Saints got their second win over the New […]
full_text: (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers will kickoff the Week 7 Sunday slate with the NFL’s first game in Paris when they take on the New Orleans Saints. Pittsburgh is coming off its biggest fourth-quarter comeback win in 34 years in a win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and the Saints got their second win over the New York Giants. Will the Steelers make it three straight wins or will New Orleans get one game closer to .500? Our staff weighs in with our picks. Ryland Bickley : Are the Steelers the better team here? I think so. But international games can put teams in a funk, and we’ve already seen prominent Steelers such as Aaron Rodgers and DK Metcalf talk about their frustrations playing overseas. And while the Saints are 2-4 this year, there’s more talent than the numbers show. Chris Olave is going to be a challenge for the Pittsburgh secondary. I’m expecting a bit of a shootout, with New Orleans eking out a win. Saints 31, Steelers 28 . Ryan Parish : Once again the Steelers should be considered the favorites here. Their zone tendencies on defense align well with the weakness of opposing quarterback Tyler Shough, and the Saints don’t have a good running game to serve as a counterpunch. The New Orleans defense is also abysmal and susceptible to the underneath throws Rodgers favors. But I will not bust a good bit when it’s been working. So I must again pick against Pittsburgh. Saints 17, Steelers 14. Joey Bray: When the schedule came out, I had picked the Steelers to lose this game. The Saints have not looked like the team I thought they would be at least to this point. While they are still alive in the “gauntlet” that is the NFC South, they have real issues defensively and no semblance of a run game. The Steelers are the better roster on paper and are playing with some confidence after their 4-2 start. Things get weird in international games, but I have a hard time believing this Saints defense will have enough to stop Jaylen Warren in the run game and the short passing attack with Germie Bernard. I’ll take Pittsburgh to win a close one in Paris. Steelers 26, Saints 23. Mike Nicastro : The Steelers have a chance to get to 5-2 against a Jekyll and Hyde Saints team that’s already defeated their division rival Ravens. Tyler Shough will challenge the Steelers secondary, as Chris Olave and Juwan Johnson are both strong weapons that can attack the middle of the field. Prior to the season I thought this would be a loss, but it feels like the Steelers have a habit of winning ugly, and this is another game where that I anticipate going down to the wire. The difference will be the Steelers run game versus the Saints lack thereof. I anticipate Jaylen Warren getting back on track with over 100 all purpose yards and a score. Boswell bangs home the game winner late. Steelers 24, Saints 21. Jason Aponte : The Saints defense provides an opportunity for the Steelers to jumpstart their offense from the opening kickoff. In particular, New Orleans’ secondary is vulnerable. The saints can be pesky offensively, but look for the Steelers to make enough plays on defense and return to the States with another win. Steelers 27, Saints 20. Jarrett Bailey: The Steelers should be able to run all over the Saints’ run defense. However, they haven’t shown the propensity to run the ball, as they rank 31st in run percentage. New Orleans’ passing game is one to pay attention to. Tyler Shough has 12 touchdowns and north of 1,400 yards on the year. I’d love to sit here and say I see the Steelers rattling off four straight wins ahead of the bye, but I don’t see them as that tier of team. Hopefully I’m wrong, but I’ll take New Orleans to win. Saints 26, Steelers 23. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! title: Steelers keys to victory vs. Saints: Get Jaylen Warren the ball
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers will be looking to get to 5-2 on the season when they face the New Orleans in Paris on Sunday. That 5-2 number is a huge one, as 80 percent of teams that start 5-2 have made the playoffs since the league expanded the playoff field to 14 teams, per Zach Smith. […]
full_text: (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers will be looking to get to 5-2 on the season when they face the New Orleans in Paris on Sunday. That 5-2 number is a huge one, as 80 percent of teams that start 5-2 have made the playoffs since the league expanded the playoff field to 14 teams, per Zach Smith . That number drops to 57 percent for teams that are 4-3. A Steelers win would also put them in prime position to head into their Week 9 bye week atop the AFC North, as they will face the Cleveland Browns in Pittsburgh in Week 8. But first, they have to take care of business in France against the 2-4 Saints. Here are the keys to victory for Week 7. Run the ball a ton The Steelers are good at running the ball. Since Week 3, they are fourth in the league in EPA per rush, per Sumer Sports . However, despite being so good when they run, they are only running on 32.8 percent of snaps, which is second to last in the league. They throw the ball on just over 67 percent of snaps – the second most in the league. The Saints’ defense is the worst unit in the NFL in EPA per rush, and they are allowing the third-most rushing yards per game. Don’t make this a game where you spread the ball out – pound the ball with Jaylen Warren and control the clock. Find a way to succeed vs. single-high coverage No quarterback in the NFL has faced more single-high looks than Aaron Rodgers, and no one has a lower EPA per play when facing single-high coverage than Aaron Rodgers (min. 25 dropbacks). The Saints show single-high at the second-highest rate in the NFL, behind only the Browns. Plays over the middle will be open, the Steelers just need to be able to make them. Win the battle on third down In many metrics, the Steelers are the NFL’s worst team on third down. They rank last in EPA and success rate, and are 28th in third-down conversions. And it’s not as if they are at the bottom of the league in terms of how long their average third down is. Per Sumer Sports, their average third down distance is 6.96 yards, which is 13th in the NFL. For comparison, the Philadelphia Eagles average third-down is a league-high 8.37 yards. The Saints’ defense ranks 24th in success rate on third down, so if there was a week to get their third-down woes turned around, it’s this week. Let us know what you think in the comments . full_text: The Seattle Seahawks (3-3) find themselves in a position where the goal is to make the playoffs, let alone get back to the Super Bowl. Two straight losses off the back of poor offensive showings have the reigning Super Bowl champions in a dangerous zone. Meanwhile, Super Bowl 60 MVP Kenneth Walker III is having the time of his life with his new team, the Kansas City Chiefs (5-0). The class of the AFC comes into town looking to stay undefeated, with Walker as much of a catalyst for their success as the great Patrick Mahomes. Any thought of the Seahawks having Zach Charbonnet available was squashed on Friday when he was ruled out despite no injury setback. That means Seattle’s struggling run game will continue to feature Emanuel Wilson, George Holani, and presumably Velus Jones Jr. Their passing game has been lackluster outside of the usual throws to Jaxon Smith-Njigba from Sam Darnold, whose seven interceptions have caused plenty of concern and questions over his starting job . Seattle’s defense remains elite, although the red zone has been a problem and the run defense is facing its stiffest test all season… and he so happens to be a familiar foe. Seattle’s three losses have been by a combined eight points, but the turnover differential has been a whopping -7 in those defeats. Can the Seahawks take care of the ball for once? title: Seahawks safety Ty Okada fined for 2 infractions less than a minute apart vs. Broncos
summary: The Seattle Seahawks are coming off another tough loss, and to make matters worse, a couple of players have been fined for uncalled offenses against the Denver Broncos. In the case of Ty Okada, he got the unwanted daily double. The starting safety received not one, but two fines for plays that happened inside of […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks are coming off another tough loss, and to make matters worse, a couple of players have been fined for uncalled offenses against the Denver Broncos. In the case of Ty Okada, he got the unwanted daily double. The starting safety received not one, but two fines for plays that happened inside of a minute of game time in the opening quarter. He was docked $6,361 for an illegal use of helmet while tackling Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. It certainly wasn’t that obvious watching it in real time or even on replay. His second $6,361 fine for what the league deemed was a tripping attempt on Broncos running back RJ Harvey. Perhaps if Harvey had immediately gone down there would’ve been a penalty called live, but there was none. Seahawks safety Ty Okada was fined twice following the loss against the Denver Broncos. The first fine in this video is illegal use of helmet while tackling Jaylen Waddle. The second one is what the league deemed a tripping attempt on RJ Harvey. The fines are $6,361 each. pic.twitter.com/8hIrKctwlM — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 24, 2026 Meanwhile, defensive end Mike Morris got his own fine ($6,808) for lowering his helmet illegally while doing a clean-up tackle on Troy Franklin. Seahawks defensive end Mike Morris was fined $6,808 for illegal use of helmet while tackling Troy Franklin. pic.twitter.com/1P43xn8bUt — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 24, 2026 It should be noted that lowering the helmet is not one of the infractions that the league has keyed in on as a suspension-worthy offense if it happens three times in a season . Lastly, there was one Broncos player fined for a hit that came at a critical point in the contest. With under a minute left in regulation, Sam Darnold was drilled by Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton on a late rush. Darnold was noticeably slow to get up after taking a vicious hit, which didn’t result in a roughing the passer penalty. It did, however, prompt a $23,882 fine from the league for illegal helmet use. They almost never call these helmet penalties in-game, but I suppose this conceivably could’ve been called roughing the passer in the moment. The NFL fined Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton $23,882 for illegal use of helmet when he jacked up Sam Darnold at the :52 mark of the 4th quarter. They almost never call illegal use of helmet penalties so I'm hesitant to say "uncalled roughing the passer" but it's still notable. pic.twitter.com/JE7xVuVcHK — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 24, 2026 These fines can be appealed. If any of these fines is upheld then the players will lose that money from their next game check, otherwise they’ll be notified of a rescinding in case of a successful appeal.
