title: NFL Week 7 predictions: Upsets, fantasy sleepers, stat lines, TD scorers, more
summary: Touchdowns for Tucker Kraft and Germie Bernard? Cardinals pull another upset? Revenge game for Trey Hendrickson? Let's predict 15 things for Week 7.
full_text:
Week 7 of the  2026 NFL season is underway after the Bears beat the Patriots 30-24 on  Thursday night . But what will happen in the remaining 13 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

 First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

 Can the Cardinals pull off an upset for the second straight week? What could Packers tight end Tucker Kraft 's stat line look like against the Lions? Is Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee a sneaky play in fantasy? And how many sacks will Ravens edge rusher Trey Hendrickson have against his former team?

 Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Upset picks | Projected stat lines 
 Fantasy sleepers, surprises 
 TD scorers | Other predictions 

 
 

 Maldonado predicts two upsets 
 

 Arizona Cardinals +4.5 (+195 moneyline) vs. Denver Broncos 

 The Broncos haven't shown they can pull away when ahead this season. Denver is averaging only 3.4 yards per carry (third lowest in the league), and quarterback Bo Nix has thrown for just 230 yards over the past two games combined. Despite a strong showing against the Rams , Arizona's pass defense has given up plenty of explosive plays in 2026. But Denver rarely throws downfield to take advantage.

 The Broncos' defense should be a tough matchup for Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett , so I'm not expecting a big offensive day from the Cardinals. But this matchup looks like it will be decided by a field goal, and Arizona could come out on top.

 
 

 

 Kansas City Chiefs +2.5 (+120 moneyline) at Seattle Seahawks 

 Kansas City has the defense to keep this close even if Seattle slows down QB Patrick Mahomes . The Chiefs create pressure on nearly 39% of dropbacks, and QB Sam Darnold has completed only 38% of his throws under pressure this season. Seattle's struggles with run blocking could leave him handling too many difficult passing downs.

 Offensively, running back  Kenneth Walker III faces a tough rushing matchup against his former team, but Seattle has had issues covering RBs as receivers. That gives Kansas City another way to move the ball and win this outright.

 

 

 Walder predicts three stat lines 
 

 Tucker Kraft , TE, Green Bay Packers : 9 targets, 7 receptions, 87 receiving yards, 1 TD 

 Kraft has the benefit of going against a Lions defense that has allowed 27% of its targets to opposing tight ends, the second-highest rate in the league. But it gets better. Based on player tracking data from NFL Next Gen Stats, Detroit linebackers Malcolm Rodriguez , Derrick Barnes and Jack Campbell all bite on play-action more than average . The Packers haven't used play-action a ton this season, but Kraft could be the beneficiary whenever they do Sunday.

 
 

 Ted Hurst III , WR, Tampa Bay Buccaneers : 6 targets, 4 receptions, 79 yards, 1 TD 

 I've had my eye on predicting a breakout game by Hurst for a few weeks now, and I think it will finally happen  against the Panthers . Hurst has a vertical route profile, running either a go route or deep fade on 21% of his routes -- 11th-highest rate among wide receivers with at least 60 routes this season. That means high variance and high upside in any given week.

 So why a big game this Sunday? Well for starters, there seems to be a good chance quarterback Baker Mayfield will be back from his thumb injury . Emeka Egbuka is also out, which should lead to even more targets for Hurst. The Panthers also have backup cornerbacks in both outside spots. And on top of all that, Carolina plays an above-average amount of single-high coverage, which helps with deep outside shots.

 
 

 Zach Allen , DL, Denver Broncos : 2.0 sacks, 7 pressures, 25% pass rush win rate 

 Allen is off to a hot start this season with 4.5 sacks and a 19.6% pass rush win rate that's tied for sixth best among interior rushers. Now, he gets a perfect matchup against the Cardinals ' interior offensive line.

 Allen figures to face right guard Jon Gaines II more than anyone else, and Gaines ranks last in pass block win rate out of 71 qualifying guards. The rest of the interior isn't much better: Left guard Isaac Seumalo and center Hjalte Froholdt have 12th-percentile and sixth-percentile pass block win rates, respectively, at their positions.

 

 

 

 Moody predicts three fantasy sleepers 
 

 Keenan Allen , WR, Indianapolis Colts (rostered in 42.4% of ESPN leagues) 

 Allen is worth considering for fantasy managers navigating bye weeks. He has averaged 9.6 targets and 14.7 fantasy points over the past three games, becoming one of Daniel Jones ' most reliable targets with Alec Pierce on IR ( heel ). The Vikings are a tough matchup , but their aggressive blitzing could lead to more quick throws, which suits Allen's game. His touchdown upside is limited, though the consistent targets make him a viable flex option.

 
 

 Malik Washington , WR, Miami Dolphins (36.6%) 

 Washington has seen at least five targets in every game this season, including eight or more in three contests. He has also scored at least 11 fantasy points in three straight games. Miami hasn't been able to do much downfield, but Washington showcases reliability on shorter throws. That should help him against a Jets defense that plays a lot of Cover 2 to limit big plays.

 Washington should see enough targets to provide a decent fantasy floor, with more upside if he scores his first touchdown of the season.

 
 

 Tanner McKee , QB, Philadelphia Eagles (4.6%) 

 McKee is an intriguing sleeper with quarterback Jalen Hurts out for the season ( blood clots ). He threw for 215 yards and a touchdown against the Panthers last week and now faces a Cowboys defense that has allowed 21.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks (fifth most in the league). Dallas has also given up 11 passing touchdowns this season.

 McKee attempted 45 passes last week, and he has the targets to reach the end zone with DeVonta Smith  and Dallas Goedert  (both questionable to play). He's worth considering in deeper single-QB leagues and as a QB2 in superflex formats.

 

 

 

 Bowen predicts three touchdown scorers 
 

 Amon-Ra St. Brown , WR, Detroit Lions 

 After scoring at least one touchdown in his first three games, St. Brown hasn't reached the end zone in his past two. However, he is still averaging 11.4 targets per game. And some of those looks are in scoring position, with at least one end zone target in both Week 4 and Week 5. Let's take St. Brown to score at Lambeau Field.

 
 

 Germie Bernard , WR, Pittsburgh Steelers 

 Bernard, who scored his first touchdown as a pro in the Steelers' Week 6 win over the Bucs, has seen a recent bump in volume. Over the past two games, he has caught 17 of 21 targets.

 Bernard can get loose from slot alignments or uncover as the underneath outlet for quarterback Aaron Rodgers . And I like this Week 7 matchup versus a Saints defense that has given up 10 touchdown passes on the season (tied for 10th most in the NFL).

 
 

 Kyler Murray , QB, Minnesota Vikings 

 Murray hasn't rushed for a touchdown with the Vikings, but he has had 16 attempts over the past two weeks for 67 yards. I'm looking at a second-reaction play to score Sunday , when he can get outside of the pocket as a runner in the red zone. And the Colts have allowed six rushing scores this season, tied for seventh most in the NFL.

 

 

 Solak makes four more predictions 
 

 Ravens edge rusher  Trey Hendrickson will get two sacks 

 Hendrickson faces his old team for the first time this season, and he has never had a chance to sack Bengals QB  Joe Burrow in his career -- you can bet this means something extra to him, even if he won't admit it . Hendrickson will also…

title: NFL execs, coaches rank the league's top five MVP candidates entering Week 7
summary: Brock Purdy? Josh Allen? Or maybe even a non-QB? Sixteen execs and coaches voted on the top five contenders for the MVP award through six weeks.
full_text:
We're already one game into Week 7 . And with more than a third of the 2026 NFL regular season  officially behind us, it's time to start taking the temperature of the MVP race. Which players are making a memorable impact with their play?

 We polled 16 NFL front office executives, coaches and personnel people with a simple question: Who is your league MVP through the first six weeks? From there, we were able to form a top-five list. One coach joked that MVP is basically a quarterback-only award so there's no need to list players at other positions. And yes, there are two early QB favorites. But our ballot shows just how wide open this race is this season, with multiple running backs and even a wide receiver landing in our top five.

 There is still a lot of time to shift things, but here is where a sample of people around the league feel things stand right now.

 

 

 1. Brock Purdy , QB, San Francisco 49ers -- 6 votes 
 Stats: 69.6% completion rate, 1,460 passing yards, 14 passing TDs, 2 INTs; 156 rushing yards, 1 rushing TD

 The case for Purdy: Purdy leads the NFL with an 83.1 QBR and is tied for the league lead with 14 touchdown passes. He also has just five sacks on the season, and his effectiveness as a runner has made him even more difficult to defend. But Purdy's superpower is his accuracy. He has a 5.1% completion percentage over expectation, per NFL Next Gen Stats, and he completes an NFL-high 88% of his passes to open receivers (3-plus yards of separation).

 The 49ers look like the NFL's best team at this stage with a 6-0 record, and it's largely because Purdy is having the best season of his career. He has helped San Francisco overcome an NFL-high 22 players being placed on injured reserve. As one AFC assistant general manager said, " Josh Allen is the easy answer. But my pick is Brock Purdy because of impact in that scheme despite all their injuries. He just finds a way to win. His numbers and the way he does it may not be as gaudy as Allen, but he's very valuable."

 

 He has had his MVP moments, too. Purdy's Week 2 performance vs. the Dolphins was the best QBR performance by any QB this season, with a near-perfect 99.7 rating. At one point, he completed 18 consecutive passes. He was the first QB in NFL history to throw for 250-plus yards with a 90% or higher completion percentage while also adding 30-plus rushing yards.

 Purdy's best pass of the season came a few weeks later -- a 55-yard deep connect with receiver Mike Evans vs. the Commanders on Monday to cap Week 6. Pressure was swarming fast, but he stuck in the pocket and delivered a dime to Evans.

 A common theme in talking to executives about Purdy is how he has redefined his narrative from being a system QB who is just a product of Kyle Shanahan's scheme to now seeing his unique feel for playing the position. "It looks easy and instinctual for him," one NFC coach said.

 Another AFC personnel director who selected Purdy said, "When you accept that all QBs need a system and support, it levels the playing field. MVP is who is playing the best, not just talent, so [Patrick] Mahomes, Allen and Matt Stafford can't win every year." Maybe this is Purdy's year.

 The case against Purdy: Purdy is only 14th among QBs in yards per game. He has been efficient but lacks the consistent explosive flash this season that we've seen from other contending quarterbacks, like Allen.

 There's also strength of schedule to consider. It doomed Drake Maye last season, as the Patriots played a relatively easy slate. And while the 49ers are in the tough NFC West, they have played just one team that currently has a winning record -- the 4-2 Broncos -- and aren't set to play one above .500 again until Week 11 (vs. the Vikings). Could the injuries catch up to the 49ers as the schedule tightens in the second half? The defense and receiver room have been decimated; San Francisco -- and Purdy -- seemingly can't afford many more blows.

 
 

 2. Josh Allen , QB, Buffalo Bills -- 4 votes 
 Stats: 66.7% completion rate, 1,504 passing yards, 9 passing TDs, 4 INTs; 240 rushing yards, 8 rushing TDs

 The case for Allen:  No one makes football look like a backyard football game quite like Allen, and he might be the most dangerous dual-threat playmaker in football with an NFL-high 17 total touchdowns. Is there a "fun to watch" factor in MVP voting? Because Allen would surely get a boost there.

 

 But this award is really about value, and it's easy to picture the Bills as a non-playoff team without Allen at the helm. His defense has performed worse than any candidate on this list -- Buffalo has given up 29-plus points in five of its six games. But the Bills are still 5-1 largely because of Allen's play on the other side of the ball.

 The way Allen performed late in their 37-34 OT victory over the Rams  is the most memorable MVP moment of any QB performance this season. Allen did it primarily with his legs, rushing for career-high 121 yards -- including 91 in the fourth quarter and overtime. Allen had a 93.3 QBR in that win. As one NFC defensive coach said, "It's gotta be Josh Allen right now. He won the game vs. the Rams by himself!! Damn he's good!!"

 Coach Joe Brady has empowered Allen to be himself as a loose playmaker more than ever, and so far, the reward has outweighed the risk. Allen's "no, no, nooo ... yes!" shovel touchdown pass to Keon Coleman in last week's win over the Raiders is a perfect example of him putting on his superhero cape to save the day in unorthodox and often wild ways.

 The case against Allen:  Although Allen makes memorable plays, his completion percentage and passing yards per game rank toward the back end of the top 10 among QBs. Allen has referenced working through mechanical tweaks in his throwing motion. And if he ultimately loses the award to Purdy, the slight edge in accuracy could be the difference.

 And while Allen's aggressiveness is a fun asset, it occasionally burns him into making a bad turnover -- like he did in throwing an interception into double coverage in Week 4 loss to the Patriots . Allen will have to keep the turnovers down to win this award.

 
 

 3. Kenneth Walker III , RB, Kansas City Chiefs -- 3 votes 
 Stats: 106 rushes, 665 rushing yards, 6 rushing TDs; 14 catches, 95 receiving yards, 2 receiving TDs

 The case for Walker:  Walker leads the NFL by far with 52 broken tackles, per NFL Next Gen Stats, breaking a tackle on a league-high 43% of his touches. But it's not just power. Close your eyes, critics of Walker's speed: According to Next Gen Stats, he has reached 15-plus mph on 23 different carries this season (tied for the second most in the league) and has two of the four running plays leaguewide to hit 21-plus mph. It has helped him to a healthy 6.3 yards per carry on the season.

 Walker said coach Andy Reid had a summer conversation with him stating the belief that Walker could be a three-down player and prove that he was more than the bruiser back he had been stereotyped as due to limited receiving reps. Walker has become a reliable passing game playmaker, forcing defenses to remain honest in their defensive scheme.

 

 And Walker's destruction has really forced defenses to completely change how they play the 5-0 Chiefs. An AFC wide receiver coach who picked Walker said, "Biggest thing is he's taken off so much load from Mahomes coming off injury. He's the center of their offense right now. He's been the best free agent pickup in [the] whole league."

 The case against Walker: The last non-QB to win MVP was Adrian Peterson , who rushed for more than 2,000 yards and came just 8 yards from the single-season rushing record in 2012. Despite his excellent start, Walker shares a backfield with Patrick Mahomes, who will likely garner more MVP love and offensive workload share as the season goes on and is more removed from his ACL surgery .

 Chiefs coaches have also been open about decreasing Walker's workload and giving more touches to rookie Emmett…

title: NFL Week 7 betting guide: the value bets to make on lines, props and anytime TDs
summary: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 7 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
full_text:
Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: find betting value.

 Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. Also included are fantasy projection creator Mike Clay's top predicted anytime TD scorers for Week 7.

 From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. Let's get into it.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 Jump to: 
 Bowen's favorite bets 
 Solak's plays  | Walder's props 
 Clay's TD projections 

 

 

 Bowen's favorite bets 
 Heading into Week 7 of the NFL Sunday slate, I'm going to try some different things in this space. Yes, I'll still have some game picks in here that we need to hit on, but I'll also move around the league a little more. Spreads, totals, props, etc. -- with the same analysis based on the numbers and the game tape. Plus, I'll have more bets to play.

 We'll start in Detroit, where I see two offenses with explosive-play ability -- playing indoors and on a really fast track -- pushing past the total.

 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions 
4:25 p.m. ET on Fox, Ford Field, Detroit

 

 Total points OVER 53.5 (-110) 

 Let's see if the Lions made some defensive adjustments over the bye week (such as playing less man coverage). This unit has given up 29.6 points per game, and the Packers will have matchup advantages with Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Plus, Josh Jacobs returns to the Green Bay backfield. While I do think the Packers defense has played really good football over the past three weeks (11.5 PPG), limiting Jared Goff , Amon-Ra St. Brown and  Jahmyr Gibbs  is a different test. The Lions are scoring 32.8 PPG for a reason. This has the makeup of a shootout in the controlled environment of Ford Field.

 More bets to consider 

 Two-team, 6-point teaser: Vikings -0.5 vs. Colts , Broncos - Cardinals UNDER 49.5 (-143) 

 Getting the Vikings down to basically a moneyline play is a win. Brian Flores' defense is the story here, too. The Vikings lead the NFL in blitz rate (67.6%), and they are allowing a league-low 12.8 points per game. That's trouble for a Colts offense lacking a vertical element in the pass game. And with Daniel Jones ' reduced mobility due to his Achilles injury in 2025, Flores can heat up the pocket.

 Pushing the Denver-Arizona number up to 49.5 feels like a smart play here to get the Vikings number we want, as a straight moneyline bet on Minnesota would cost -278. Both teams rank in the bottom 10 in offensive scoring. The Cards aren't a vertical offense with Jacoby Brissett at quarterback, and Bo Nix is playing subpar football. This feels like a low-scoring game to start with, and we're pushing the number up by 6

 Atlanta Falcons +3 vs. San Francisco 49ers 

 The 49ers travel cross country for this one -- after playing the Monday night game -- and Mike Evans could be down due to Achilles tendinitis. Atlanta also features a defense that is top five against the run, has produced four sacks in back-to-back games and has taken the ball away in four straight. Let's take the Falcons as a home underdog to cover.

 Bijan Robinson rushing + receiving yards OVER 112.5 (-112)

title: Will Niners have edge with ex-Falcons coach facing Penix?
summary: With all of the familiarity between Morris and the Falcons, Sunday's game should come down to execution.
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Bijan Robinson has maintained a close relationship with Raheem Morris. It makes sense. Morris was the Atlanta Falcons ' head coach for two of the first three seasons of Robinson's career.

 On Sunday, the two men will meet again under different circumstances.

 Robinson will be helping to lead the Falcons' offense as one of the top running backs in the league. Morris, who has called Robinson the best player in the NFL multiple times, will be back in Atlanta as the San Francisco 49ers ' defensive coordinator. Morris was fired as Atlanta's coach in January after back-to-back eight-win campaigns.

 Robinson said he spoke to Morris just a few weeks ago, and he's relishing the chance to face off against a man he calls a "father figure" to him.

 "He's always going to be family to me no matter if we compete or not," Robinson said. "But yeah, man, he still talks to all of his players, because that's just who he is."

 Morris is glad Penix has recovered from the torn left ACL that ended his season last year on Nov. 16.

 "He's back healthy and he's probably everything that you thought and hoped for as far as being a play-action passer, a guy that can push the ball down the field, can make all the throws, go through the whole process," Morris said. "Just one of those guys that I have a lot of appreciation for and love for."

 The Falcons players on offense who have been here the past several years will be going up against a defense run by a man who knows them all too well.  And that 49ers defense has been potent regardless of opponent familiarity. San Francisco is allowing the fourth-fewest points per game (18.3) and the fifth-fewest yards per game (300).

 Atlanta (2-4) must perform against Morris and the undefeated Niners or risk losing three straight games and moving to 0-4 at home. A fifth loss in the first seven games is not how the Falcons wanted to start off under new head coach Kevin Stefanski.

 The Falcons' biggest issue on offense is one the Chicago Bears exploited last week in a 31-23 Falcons loss. The Bears pressured quarterback Michael Penix Jr . 46.2% of the time, the highest rate Penix has faced this season. Chicago sacked Penix five times and blitzed on more than half of his dropbacks.

 The results were not good. For the season, Penix has the worst EPA per dropback under quick pressure in the NFL (-1.17). He is 3-of-15 for 17 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions in those scenarios.

 With no pressure at all, Penix has the fourth-best EPA per dropback in the league (0.40). So, it is imperative that the Falcons figure out how to better protect him.

 "Any game you go into, you want to protect your quarterback," Stefanski said. "And I think you protect your quarterback literally with the protection, but also you protect the quarterback with how guys get open, how we get the ball out of our hands, how we run the ball, all those type of things."

 

 No defensive coordinator knows Penix better than Morris. He was part of the regime that drafted Penix and was a major proponent of the QB for two years. How much does that come into play during the week? A little bit.

 Falcons defense coordinator Jeff Ulbrich, who has a long history with Morris, said he will speak with offensive coordinator Tommy Rees about Morris and his scheme. Stefanski calls situations like this "overblown."

 "Of course, Raheem has great insight into our personnel, and our coaches have great insight into Raheem and he knows that," Stefanski said. "So, I think you can get into, 'Well, he knows that we know that they know,' and I don't think it's as useful as it may seem. Now having said that, of course, anytime we're playing against a coach or a player that someone has knowledge on, you sit and you talk to your players, and you talk to your coaches and you try to get as much insight on people as possible."

 Penix, for his part, said he is looking forward to the chess match with his former head coach.

 "It's going to be exciting," Penix said. "It's going to be good to be able to see him again, but we got to find a way to obviously put points on the board against the defense."

 Contributing: Nick Wagoner

title: Why Derrick Henry has taken Jets RB Braelon Allen under his wing
summary: After Henry saw Allen wearing his shirt in college, he reached out to him, and the two running backs have kept in touch since.
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- A look at what's happening around the New York Jets :

 1. King advice: When elevated to the starting role in Week 4, running back Braelon Allen received a text from friend and mentor,  Baltimore Ravens  running back  Derrick Henry , who encouraged him to seize the opportunity. Allen has done that, rushing for 253 yards during  Breece Hall 's three-game injury absence -- fifth most in the NFL over that span.

 "Don't give no credit to me; he's his own man," Henry told ESPN. "I'm trying to be someone who can help him out in any way I can give advice.

 "But, yeah, he's just a big, physical kid. I call him 'Manchild,' and I was able to catch a little bit of clips from the games he's played. He's doing a heck of a job being in that starting role and always knew he'd be ready for it, so I'm happy for him."

 

 Their relationship goes back five years. As a freshman at Wisconsin, Allen posted a photo of himself wearing a Henry shirt. Henry saw it, reached out and they became friends.

 They train at the same Dallas facility during the offseason, and they talk at least once a week during the season. There's a 10-year age difference -- Allen is 22, Henry 32 -- but their playing style is similar: They're both big, bruising and deceptively fast.

 The Ravens star is listed at 6-foot-3, 252 pounds; Allen is 6-1, 235, though he said his current weight is 242.

 "He runs hard, runs behind his pads, isn't willing to go down that easy," said Henry, the ninth-leading rusher in NFL history. "So, yeah, he's going to keep getting better and better."

 Allen said of Henry: "In my shoes, he's really the best you can get in terms of a guy, a connection, someone that can mentor and guide me through the process of my career. He's been great. I try to get every little nugget that I can about what he does. He doesn't slow down. I want to have a long career, too, so I try to soak up as much as possible."

 When Hall returns from his injury, which could be Sunday against the Miami Dolphins , Allen will return to his role as the RB2. Coach Aaron Glenn made it clear that Hall remains the starter, adding that Allen will continue to get carries after averaging 4.2 yards per carry this season.

 

 2. Two minutes of chaos: In the 2024 season finale, Aaron Rodgers threw a 13-yard touchdown pass to Allen Lazard with a minute left in the second quarter.

 Here we are, 658 days later. The Jets haven't scored a touchdown in the final two minutes of the first half since -- outscored 100-6 in 23 games under Glenn.

 "Oh, damn," an opposing personnel scout said. "Holy cow, that's poor time management."

 It might seem like nitpicking because we're talking about only two minutes out of a 60-minute game -- four minutes, if you want to include the end of the fourth quarter -- but it shines a light on a team's ability to execute in a high-leverage situation. They can be momentum swingers, too, and we all know every point matters in the NFL. To wit: Glenn is 4-8 in one-score games.

 Other factoids:

 
 The Jets have gone 15 straight games without scoring in the final two minutes of the second quarter. They've been outscored this season 20-0. Since 2000, only one team went scoreless for an entire season -- the 2021 New York Giants , who finished 4-13. "I didn't know that," said Jets practice-squad receiver Sterling Shepard , a member of the Giants that year. "That's a wild stat." 
 The 2021 Giants' point differential was minus-79, which ranks 862nd out of 862 teams since 2000. At minus-74, the '25 Jets were 861st. 
 There have been ample opportunities this season for the Jets, who had a two-minute drive in five of their first six games at the end of the first half. Not once did they get close enough to even try a long field goal. If you want to include the last two minutes of the fourth quarter, they've been outscored under Glenn 119-49 including 23-3 this season. 
 Geno Smith has been one of the better two-minute quarterbacks since 2022 (ninth out of 37 qualified passers in QBR), which makes the Jets' hurry-up follies even more confounding. 
 

 3. The Rodgers curse? An interesting postscript:  A few seconds after Rodgers' TD to Lazard, Jets safety Ashtyn Davis made his second interception of the game, a win over Miami in Rodgers' final game as a Jet. It would be the Jets' last interception until this season, Week 4, a historic drought of 20 games.

 4. Daring Darren: The Jets have three games before the NFL trading deadline (Nov. 10). The outcomes likely will determine if they're buyers, sellers or bystanders.

 They have a few players that might interest other teams, including two former starters now in backup roles -- cornerback Nahshon Wright and safety Andre Cisco , both on one-year contracts. Wright has been a healthy scratch for the last four games.

 Edge rusher Will McDonald IV could intrigue teams, as he did last year. Problem is, injuries have hurt the depth at that position, a reason for keeping him. McDonald is signed through 2027 ($13.8 million guaranteed), but he's no longer an every-down player.

 It's hard to imagine general manager Darren Mougey, an aggressive trader, not doing anything.

 

 5. Friday fashion: Defensive tackle Harrison Phillips showed up to the first Friday practice wearing a buttoned-up polo shirt under his jersey. The fad grew from one player to a few to a dozen or so, and now about 20 to 30 players and some coaches are doing it.

 It's a tone setter, according to Phillips, who wanted to create a business-like vibe on the shortest and lightest practice of the week.

 "The idea is that, even though it's a fast Friday and it's the job, and we're taking the physical [aspect] out of practice, mentally we're still at work and we're still intense mentally," Phillips said.

 Phillips said he started the tradition on one of his previous teams because the Friday practices got too lackadaisical and it was "rubbing me the wrong way." He wouldn't identify the team, but he had only two previous stops, the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings .

 So he started to dress for success, and he brought it to the Jets.

 6. Packing a punch: The "Peanut Punch" is gaining popularity around the league. Linebacker Jamien Sherwood executed a textbook punch last Sunday, racing 40 yards downfield and using a top-to-bottom striking motion to dislodge the ball from New England Patriots wide receiver DeMario Douglas .

 Sherwood said there's an art to perfect aim, that swinging wildly can be dangerous. He said he learned a hard lesson in 2024, fracturing a small bone in his hand during practice when he missed his target and crashed his fist into a teammate's helmet.

 "You have to be very intentional," said Sherwood, adding that fellow linebacker Marcelino McCrary-Ball has the best technique on the team. The Jets have 10 forced fumbles, second in the league. The "Peanut Punch" is named after its creator, former Chicago Bears cornerback Charles (Peanut) Tillman.

 

 7. Super power: The Jets have a league-high five unblocked sacks, including two by rookie David Bailey , per Next Gen Stats. That's a credit to Glenn and his ability to create confusion with his pressure schemes.

 8. Yo, bro: In the Jets' defensive meeting room, they're calling it the "Slowik Bowl." The Jets' safeties coach is Ryan Slowik, 45. His younger brother, Bobby, 39, is the Dolphins' offensive coordinator.

 9. Epic: For those looking ahead to the 2027 draft, the Jets currently hold the sixth, ninth and 13th picks, per Tankathon. The first two choices would come from the Dallas Cowboys and Indianapolis Colts via the Quinnen Williams and Sauce Gardner trades, respectively.

 10. The last word: One year ago, Oct. 25, 2025, the Jets lost one of their most beloved players, Nick Mangold, who died at 41 due to complications from kidney disease. He was a fun-loving personality, a blue-collar tough guy and an outstanding player. He made his last Pro Bowl in 2015. No Jets offensive lineman has made it…

title: Inside the silent messages Boye Mafe sends every game day
summary: The Bengals defensive end uses sign language to say "I love you" to his mother, Bola, who died of pancreatic cancer in 2018.
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- Before the chaos of each game unfolds, Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Boye Mafe has a conversation that centers him in a special place.

 He closes his eyes and starts talking to his mother, Bola, who died of pancreatic cancer in 2018. And in those moments, Mafe lays out his vision for what's about to unfold.

 I know you're watching over me. I want to put on a show for you. I love you and this is what I'm going to do for you. 

 Then he'll wrap up the message by using American Sign Language to say "I love you" before he continues the rest of his pregame routine. Mafe does the same after each sack.

 But it's about more than signs. Everything Mafe does is about what he signals. From those messages to Bola, to his pregame outfits, to how he plays, it's all about honoring the systems and structures that built him into one of the NFL's leading pass rushers and a Super Bowl champion.

 

 "I try not to let circumstances dictate who I am," Mafe told ESPN. "At the end of the day, I am who I am and I want to be true to who I am."

 That doesn't come easily. Mafe, the son of proud Nigerians, grapples with a phenomenon that is common among those with generational ties to other places -- the more time passes, the harder it is to stay connected to those roots.

 But all it takes is one glance on game day to see just how strong those ties are.

 How Boye Mafe's mother impacted her community 
 To fully understand why Mafe signs to his late mother requires understanding his upbringing in the western suburbs of Minneapolis.

 Mafe and his siblings often communicate via American Sign Language. Starting with his older sister, Tayo, they all decided to study it in high school as their alternative language. And over the years the practice has stuck, even during games. Once, Tayo recalled signing to Mafe when he suffered an injury at Minnesota. He quickly signaled back that it wasn't anything serious.

 Of all Mafe's six siblings, he is the one who spent the most time in their mother's seamstress shop on 1110 Lowery Avenue in North Minneapolis. There, Bola did more than mend clothes. She served as a cultural hub for many, not just Nigerians or those with Yoruba roots.

 And she invested in the community. She volunteered at a battered women's shelter, made vests for Mafe's entire church choir and often let her customers have some extended credit.

 

 "She had a lot of patience because sometimes people couldn't pay and she was like, 'Oh, pay me later,'" said Angie Onayiga, one of Bola's longtime friends. "She still gave them the clothes, sold things for them."

 When Bola was diagnosed with cancer while Boye was in high school, the bond between mother and son deepened. Boye and his brother Domi did everything they could to make sure Bola was as comfortable as possible as the disease progressed.

 How she fought the disease made a lasting impact on Boye.

 "Not one day I see her cry or one day I see her down sad or [say] woe is me," Boye said. "She always found the light and made joy in any moment she could.

 "I try to bring that into my life."

 And he needed those lessons as he got deeper into his NFL career.

 Why Boye Mafe was a better fit for the Bengals 
 Those who have spent time around Mafe know where his temperament comes from.

 "My mom didn't waste words," Tayo said. "He's like that. He just has this quieter confidence. When he walks in a room, you just know it. And my mom had that."

 But that confidence was tested during the end of his run with the Seattle Seahawks , who selected him in the second round of the 2022 draft out of Minnesota.

 In Seattle, there was a consensus about what Mafe brought to the Seahawks -- a high-motor player, an energetic pass rusher and someone who could develop into a hybrid edge player who could also drop into pass coverage when needed.

 

 In 2023, his second season in the NFL, Mafe started in all 16 of his appearances and totaled a career-high nine sacks. But over the next two seasons, those numbers dwindled, as did the amount of time he spent on the field.

 He recalled a particular three-game stretch during one of those seasons when he was "in the dumps" about not playing well. Then he remembered what he learned from his mom.

 "I had to remind myself I am who I am," Mafe said. "And I thought about how she would do it and what she would do in those situations. And you always got to look at the glass half full.

 "And when I started looking at the glass half full in a lot of situations, it makes getting through tough times happen, and tough times also will pass."

 This offseason, the Bengals had a glaring need at edge rusher. Trey Hendrickson , an All-Pro defensive end who totaled 61 sacks in five seasons with Cincinnati, left in free agency and signed with the Baltimore Ravens . Joseph Ossai landed a big contract with the New York Jets , making pass rush an even bigger need.

 Mafe fit exactly what the Bengals were looking for.

 

 "The talent was always there," said Bengals assistant Sean Desai, who was in Seattle when the Seahawks drafted Mafe. "And it was an opportunity for him, I feel like, to come to a place and get a fresh start in terms of being a full-time player."

 Through five games this season, Mafe is playing a career-high 74% of his team's defensive snaps. He is one of three Bengals players who each have a team-high three sacks and is seventh in the NFL in pass rush win rate, per ESPN Analytics and NFL Next Gen Stats.

 "He seems to me like a guy that's free-spirited, in terms of just enjoying the journey, and he plays with great energy on game day," Bengals defensive coordinator Al Golden said. "He's getting better technically at all the things that we're asking him to do, which is awesome to see. And we just need him to keep growing."

 How Boye Mafe stays true to his family's heritage 

 Every time Mafe takes the field, he carries a piece of his family's culture. His father, Adewale, is in Nigeria and recently celebrated his 70th birthday with a gathering of roughly 500 friends and family, including Boye.

 Mafe sports a decal of the Nigerian flag -- next to a U.S. flag -- on the back of his helmet, honoring a place he knows firsthand.

 Like four of his siblings, Mafe -- who was born in Minnesota -- spent eighth grade at a boarding school in Nigeria, a move that Bola and Adewale Mafe made to immerse their children in their culture and give them a true feel of where they came from.

 His mother shaped how Mafe represented that, too. Growing up, he had several pieces of traditional Nigerian garb made by Bola.

 

 On certain game days this season, Mafe will wear an agbada, the long, flowing robe predominantly worn by Yoruba people. Mafe still has some of the fabrics that were in Bola's shop on Lowery Avenue and will sometimes have his current tailor use them in new designs.

 Instilling that sense of culture has been paramount to their family dynamic, even as the generations grow older.

 "[Their parents have] always been involved in organizations that maintain the culture," said Tayo, who also started a Nigerian organization of her own. "They've always put us around [it] and made sure that we knew their culture.

 "But they're also very open, knowing that we are here in the diaspora and that it's like you are living in two cultures."

 Mafe has remained true to those principles and to the people who raised him. With each sign to his mother during game days and so many other aspects of his life, he is determined to signal to the world why he is who he is.

 "At the end of the day, it's something that's demonstrative and you can see," Mafe said. "It's one thing for me to say and talk to her, but it's another thing for me to show."

title: Fernando Mendoza is embracing being Raiders' latest Hispanic QB
summary: The rookie's next chapter is inspired by the legacies of a Hispanic coach, QB and a Raiders' fan base embracing the culture.
full_text:
IN HIGH SCHOOL in 2021, Fernando Mendoza watched former Texas A&M quarterback Zach Calzada, a Cuban American like himself, and wondered about other Cubans and Hispanic quarterbacks who played at the next level. More importantly, he wanted to know how many of them had success in the NFL, even winning Super Bowls --- a dream of his.

 A Google search opened Mendoza's eyes. He researched Tom Flores and Jim Plunkett, who are considered trailblazers for Latinos in the sport. Flores (Mexican American) was the first Hispanic quarterback in the NFL in 1960 when he debuted for the Oakland Raiders -- who are now based in Las Vegas. Plunkett, also Mexican American, was a college standout at Stanford, winning the Heisman Trophy in 1970 before being drafted by the New England Patriots with the first overall pick in 1971.

 Plunkett is the first Hispanic American player to win the Heisman Trophy and be drafted No. 1.

 

 Flores and Plunkett simultaneously became the first Hispanic coach and first Hispanic quarterback to win a Super Bowl. The duo helped the Raiders defeat the Philadelphia Eagles in Super Bowl XV in 1981 -- the first of two Super Bowls that they won together. Plunkett was named the game's Most Valuable Player.

 "To see that example [and] to know whatever I am doing, it is possible, meant a great deal to me," Mendoza told ESPN.

 As the Raiders' No. 1 pick in April's draft, Mendoza is now doing more than just viewing Flores and Plunkett as inspirational figures. Mendoza is continuing their legacy. Should Mendoza start for the Raiders, he'll join another No. 1 pick in Carolina Panthers QB Bryce Young as the only starting quarterbacks of Hispanic descent in the NFL this season.

 Regardless of whether he wants to be, he is a beacon of hope for the Raiders, with a fairly large Hispanic fan base. Flores and Plunkett symbolize the franchise's glory days, and they believe Mendoza can help bring the team back to relevance. Mendoza understands the role bestowed upon him can be pressure and a privilege. At the same time, it's added motivation for him to have a career that can be an inspiration for others who look like him.

 "It's a great sense of pride knowing that it's been done before and it can be done; winning a championship [while] being Hispanic as the focal point," Mendoza said. "However, it's also a great deal of pressure, and that's something I take upon myself whenever I make decisions."

 
 

 WHEN MENDOZA ARRIVED in Las Vegas after April's 2026 NFL draft , the magnitude of his presence was evident. The Raiders have not been to the postseason since 2021, which was the last year they finished with a winning record. The organization hasn't been to the Super Bowl since 2002 and hasn't hoisted the Vince Lombardi Trophy since Plunkett and Flores led the Raiders to a victory over the Washington Commanders in Super Bowl XVIII in 1984.

 On top of that, Las Vegas has also swung and missed at finding a long-term answer at quarterback in recent years. Even now, with 38-year-old Kirk Cousins leading the offense, he is still a short-term solution. Mendoza, on the other hand, is looked upon as someone who can provide stability for years to come.

 Fernando Paredes, a 45-year-old Mexican and founder/president of Raiders Laguna, a fan club for those living in the Comarca Lagunera region of Mexico, said it's a "dream" for Mendoza to be a part of the organization.

 Paredes became a Raiders fan at age 9. No one in Paredes' family watched football. However, his dad gifted him a Raiders bomber jacket, leading Paredes to watch Raiders games and ultimately fall in love with the organization.

 

 Paredes' excitement for Mendoza stems from Latinos such as Flores and Plunkett leading the team to championships.

 "That is the hope that Raiders Nation has with Fernando Mendoza," Paredes said. "All of Raider Nation in Mexico ... we hope."

 Flores played six seasons (1960-61, 1963-66) with the Raiders. In 84 games (64 starts) with the Raiders, Flores threw for 11,635 yards, 92 touchdowns and 83 interceptions. Flores was hired by late owner Al Davis to be the head coach in 1979, becoming the second Hispanic coach in NFL history. Tom Fears was the first when the New Orleans Saints hired him in 1967.

 Mendoza is the fifth quarterback of Hispanic descent to play for the Raiders, joining Flores, Plunkett, Chon Gallegos (Mexican American) and EJ Manuel (Afro-Latin American). Gallegos was a backup for six games in 1962, while Manuel made one start in two games with the Raiders in 2017.

 "We've accomplished a lot of good things, and I'm looking forward to watching [Mendoza] progress and help the Raiders get back to the Super Bowl," Plunkett, who played eight seasons with the Raiders (1978-86), told ESPN.

 The Raiders are believed to have one of the league's largest Hispanic fan bases, welded in part by Plunkett and Flores. At the same time, the team's previous homes, Los Angeles and Oakland, and even their current one, Las Vegas, have substantial Hispanic populations.

 Hispanics represent 34.7% of Las Vegas' population, according to the latest U.S. Census . They make up 47.2% of the population in Los Angeles and 28.7% in Oakland.

 

 Mexico has one of the Raiders' largest international fan bases. In 2021, the Raiders were awarded marketing rights in Mexico through the league's Global Markets Program . They also have various fan clubs based in Mexico such as Raiders Laguna and Raiders Nation MX, which occasionally host watch parties and events.

 Raiders Spanish play-by-play commentator Harry Ruiz, a Mexican American from Los Angeles, said Mendoza playing quarterback for the Raiders is significant for their Hispanic fans because they have a quarterback who looks like them.

 "When it comes to Latinos, especially in a space like football in the United States, you support each other," continued Ruiz, who is in his seventh year as an announcer for the Silver & Black. "He might not be our [same country of origin], but we embrace him because his family went through the fight that my parents went through -- fighting for the American dream -- and now he's living the dream at the highest level in the NFL as the quarterback."

 Former Carolina Panthers and Washington Commanders coach Ron Rivera, a former NFL linebacker and the third Hispanic coach in league history, expressed a similar sentiment.

 " The Black Hole [a well-known Raiders fan club] is a mixture of all the fan bases that are out there celebrating the Raiders," Rivera said. "To know that Fernando represents one of them is a big deal."

 When former punter Leo Araguz, a Mexican American, was with the Raiders, he remembered the strength of the team's Latin fan base and the love they showed him. The Raiders provided Araguz with his first shot at the NFL after he played college football at Stephen F. Austin State University.

 He had brief stints with the Miami Dolphins and San Diego Chargers, but the Raiders gave Araguz a chance to play when they signed him in 1996. Araguz went on to play four seasons (51 games) with the Raiders and holds the NFL record for most punts in a game (16).

 "Al Davis took a chance on us," Araguz told ESPN. "The Latin community is always going to be cheering for the Raiders because I think it comes from the fact that Al Davis did have that Hispanic connection to his players."

 Davis was a champion of diversity. In 1989, 10 years after Flores became the Raiders' head coach, Davis hired Pro Football Hall of Fame offensive tackle Art Shell to be the NFL's first African American head coach. In 1968, the Raiders drafted Eldridge Dickey with the 25th overall pick, making him the first African American quarterback selected in the first round.

 Araguz said the stars aligned perfectly for the Raiders when they drafted Mendoza. Araguz looks forward to seeing the community standing behind Mendoza and watching kids wear the former Indiana star's jersey to games.

 "We are excited for all of it," Araguz…

title: Patriots must improve turnover differential if they want to win, other notes
summary: It's one of Mike Vrabel's four pillars of the team identity -- and New England is struggling with it after losing to the Bears on Thursday.
full_text:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Quick-hit thoughts and notes around the New England Patriots and NFL:

 1. Turnover differential: The 4-3 Patriots have not won the turnover differential in a game this season and posted a minus-1 in Thursday's competitive 30-24 road loss to the Bears .

 Looking for one thing that needs to change if the team hopes to get where it desires? Start there.

 Mike Vrabel's team, which thrives on a four-part identity  that prioritizes "ball security and ball disruption," is a shocking minus-7 in turnover differential entering next Sunday's road game against the Miami Dolphins . The Patriots' 14 giveaways are the second most in the NFL behind the winless Chargers' 15. And despite having a goal of creating three turnovers per game on defense, New England has totaled just seven overall.

 "We just have to keep working at it. Just within the defense, we have to find a way to manufacture those -- whether it's punching the ball out ..." said veteran safety Kevin Byard , who led the NFL last season with seven interceptions but is still looking for his first in 2026.

 

 Byard pointed to himself first, highlighting a fourth-quarter play Thursday night against quarterback Caleb Williams that could have helped turn around the turnover struggles. The Bears were deep in their own territory on third-and-9 with 4:59 remaining, holding a 27-21 lead, and Byard and fellow defensive backs Marcus Jones and Christian Gonzalez were in zone coverage. Williams delivered a laser to receiver Rome Odunze for 21 yards, just between Byard's outstretched diving reach and narrowly in front of Jones.

 "That play to Rome, the ball went maybe a millimeter above KB's finger. If it was a little lower, KB would have tipped it, and who knows what would have happened?" Gonzalez said.

 It was a big-time throw from Williams, a reminder of his rising stardom, which Byard acknowledged. But it also had potential to be a big-time defensive play.

 "Almost being able to get that window, Caleb made a terrific throw. But the way I see it for me, it's 'go make that play for your team.' It's millimeters, but that's how it is. This is a game of inches, and the story is Caleb made a helluva throw, but if I can get just a little bit closer, it's 'KB helped his team win the ballgame.' So that's the stuff I look at, to make those plays," he said.

 "That's what I was brought here to do, so I'm disappointed on my end from that point. One play doesn't obviously lose a game, but I just want to be able to make that play for my team."

 One of the first things Vrabel said after the game was, "We need to turn the ball over [defensively], and we have to tackle better."

 In games the Patriots have forced at least one turnover, they are 4-1. In games they haven't forced a turnover, they're 0-2 (Seahawks, Bears).

 

 Meanwhile, the one offensive turnover against the Bears -- quarterback Drake Maye 's inaccurate end zone pass in the second quarter to rookie tight end Eli Raridon  -- further highlighted the issue.

 Maye played well other than the miscue, which he called one of the turning points and a reminder of how one mistake can be the difference against a high-caliber opponent. Unlike some of his early-season turnovers, which were more decision-based, the pick was more about execution because the play could have been made -- as evidenced by Maye connecting with Raridon for a touchdown on the same play later in the game.

 "He'll learn from it, like he always does. I'm glad he's ours," Vrabel said.

 Last year, the Patriots finished with a plus-3 turnover differential -- 19 takeaways and 16 giveaways.

 2. Quiet A.J.: Since his return from a high right ankle sprain, receiver A.J. Brown has played 101 of 122 offensive snaps and been targeted 16 times, while totaling just six receptions for 75 yards.

 Not ideal, but he isn't discouraged.

 Brown said offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels attempted to get him involved early in Thursday's game, but a combination of the Bears focusing on taking him away and Maye making the right play by taking what was there led to Brown not registering his first catch until late in the first half.

 "I'm a vet. I understand how the game goes. I know what type of player I am," Brown said. "Every time I line up, I get a lot of attention, so teams try to take me away, and it gives a lot of opportunity for other guys to make plays -- and soften it up for me. And whenever I get my shots, I have to make them, too."

 

 One area Brown didn't address was his blocking, which showed up as a deficiency Thursday -- including on a first-quarter wide receiver screen in which he missed his assignment. It was a reminder that the Patriots could benefit from Brown showing more consistently the relentless mentality that has defined his career.

 3. AVT's contract: One of the unique aspects of the three-year, $42 million contract that guard Alijah Vera-Tucker signed with the Patriots in March is that he receives a record $250,000 for every game he is on the 46-man game-day roster. So with Vera-Tucker landing on injured reserve Thursday, forcing him to miss at least four games, that means he loses out on at least $1 million.

 4. TreVeyon's time:  During the past three weeks, running back TreVeyon Henderson 's usage has declined sharply, part of which can be traced to the ankle injury he sustained against the Raiders on Oct. 11. But after averaging 28 snaps per game in his first three contests of the year, he has averaged just 14.5 over the past two games he has played from start to finish.

 "TreVeyon will help us plenty here down the stretch," Vrabel said when asked about Henderson's limited action.

 Through seven games, Rhamondre Stevenson leads Patriots running backs with 64% of the snaps, followed by Henderson (27%) and Corey Kiner (12%).

 5. 'Close' theme: If there was a theme in the Patriots' locker room after Thursday's loss, it was that Vrabel reminded them about the importance of margin for error against top opponents -- if a play or two goes the other way, the result might be reversed. It was a more positive vibe than one might expect.

 Cornerback Marcus Jones said that Vrabel also told players, "We're close ... to being the team we want to be. Understanding how to respond is very important as well. That's something we've learned we can do."

 

 6. Snapping to it : Four topics with second-year center Jared Wilson , who has played 97% of the offensive plays through seven games:

 
 Moving from left guard to center : "Things have been going great. Of course, you have things here or there you want to clean up -- not perfect, we're all human ... every aspect can always get better, but mainly in the run game, for sure." 
 Why center is his favorite spot:  "Once they moved me over at Georgia, I was like, 'This is where I need to be.' I feel like I can show my athleticism there. I just love the position. It was something Kirby [Smart] thought I'd be really good at, and I trusted him. I just wanted to get on the field. Now I'm here, and love it." 
 How a bond is built with Maye:  "The reps are important. But also sitting down at lunch and talking. There's the [weekly] O-line dinners he pops in to." 
 Favorite parts about New England: "I like Boston. A really clean city." 
 
 7. Van Roten eligible : The Patriots have to be judicious with their decisions of whom to designate to return from injured reserve -- there's a limit of eight overall -- and some of those spots have already been accounted for (e.g. Brown, Marcus Bryant , etc.), while others seem like they will be decisively reserved (e.g. Mack Hollins , Romeo Doubs , etc.).

 A question potentially to be answered this week is whether veteran center/guard Greg Van Roten (hip) will be one of them? He's eligible for the first time and has been around the locker room of late, and the Patriots were so thin on the interior that they elevated Xavier Newman-Johnson  on Thursday from the practice squad as their backup…
